note: Generated by scripts/gen-api-tables.mjs from the declarations and doc comments in src/, for what the pages' PropTables name. A description is the doc comment on the declaration and a default is the component's own initialiser: edit those, then regenerate.

props.name: surface
props.description:
The group's chrome: one bordered shell with dividers, a panel per section, or none.
Resolves through the provider when omitted, so `UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: items
props.description:
Bounded sections, each rendered as the canonical icon/title/badge/description row.
Ignored when `children` are supplied.

props.name: media
props.description:
How leading icons are framed. Only meaningful alongside `items`; the column is dropped
entirely when no item has one. `UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: value
props.description: The controlled value of the item(s) that should be expanded.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The uncontrolled value of the item(s) that should be initially expanded.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Whether multiple items can be open at the same time.

AccordionItemData.description: One section for the bounded `items` API; use the compound parts for richer rows.

members.name: value
members.description: Stable identifier. Used as the item's `value`.

members.name: description
members.description: Supporting line below the title, inside the trigger.

members.name: icon
members.description: Leading media. Framed per the root's `media` prop.

members.name: badge
members.description: Trailing node after the title — usually a `<Badge>`.

ActionButtons.description: The same definitions rendered as visible buttons — a toolbar rather than an overflow.

props.name: actions
props.description:
The same definitions `ActionMenu` takes, side by side rather than collapsed into a menu:
that is the point of the shape. Each entry's `tone` and `buttonStyle` carry through to
its button.

props.name: max
props.description:
How many render as buttons before the rest collapse into an overflow menu built from
the same array. Unset, every definition is a button.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this toolbar's own copy: `strings.overflow` names the overflow menu's trigger.

props.name: renderLink
props.description: Routes `href` actions through the app's router, as `ActionMenu`'s `renderLink` does.

ActionDialog.description:
A dialog with a generated footer: cancel and confirm in a fixed order, an async- and
form-aware confirm, and a tone for the glyph and the confirm colour. Use the base Dialog when
the body owns its actions.

props.name: width
props.description:
Maximum width: one of the kit's steps, or a CSS length. A dialog's max width is a real
per-dialog decision — a confirmation is narrow and a form is wide.

props.name: trigger
props.description:
The element that opens it, which makes the overlay uncontrolled. Supply this OR `open`,
not both.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled: hands the open state to the caller. Supply this OR `trigger`, not both.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Fires after it closes, whatever dismissed it.

props.name: title
props.description: Supply one even with `hideHeader`: it names the dialog for screen readers.

props.name: hideHeader
props.description: Keeps the title and description for assistive technology and hides them.

props.name: closeOnEscape
props.description: Escape dismisses. Off for destructive or in-progress work.

props.name: surfaceStyle
props.description: Inline styles on the surface itself, e.g. CSS variables a theme editor previews.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description:
Runs, then the overlay closes. The second of the three confirm paths: `formId` wins over
it, and it wins over `onAsyncConfirm`.

props.name: onAsyncConfirm
props.description:
Awaited with a spinner; closes on success, stays open on rejection and reports through
`onError`. The last of the three confirm paths, after `formId` and `onConfirm`.

props.name: onError
props.description:
Receives a rejected async confirm, so a consumer can toast or report it. The overlay stays
open.

props.name: closeOnAsyncComplete
props.description: `false` keeps the overlay open after a resolved async confirm — a multi-step flow.

props.name: loading
props.description: Forces the pending presentation, for confirm work owned outside the overlay.

props.name: formId
props.description:
The first of the three confirm paths: the confirm button calls `requestSubmit()` on that
form, so native validation runs and the form's own `onSubmit` owns the outcome. Neither
callback fires.

props.name: footer
props.description: Replaces the generated footer. Every action prop stops applying.

props.name: emphasis
props.description:
Lets `tone` drive the confirm button's colour as well as the header glyph. Without it the
tone is presentational only — a warning-toned dialog whose action is just the action, with
an ordinary primary confirm, is a real combination.

props.name: tone
props.description: The semantic tone of the header glyph and the notice, and with `emphasis` the confirm.

props.name: showIcon
props.description: Draws the tone's glyph beside the title.

props.name: alertMessage
props.description:
A notice between the header and the body — the consequence, before committing — inside the
scroll region: a warning pinned above it would stay while the thing it warns about scrolls
away.

ActionHttpError.description:
The `Error` createHttpActionRunner throws for a failed response, carrying `status`,
`statusText`, `body` and the `Response`, plus the body's own `errors` when it has them. What
`parseErrors` receives for an HTTP failure.

ActionMenu.description:
Overflow commands for a page, a card, a table or a row — one component so grouping,
destructive ordering, checkbox rows and links behave the same everywhere.

props.name: actions
props.description:
Commands to offer; `visible: false` omits one entirely. Destructive entries move last
unless `preserveOrder` is set.

props.name: label
props.description: Trigger text. Omit for an icon-only trigger — `strings.trigger` names it then.

props.name: icon
props.description: Trigger glyph. Defaults to the vertical ellipsis.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this menu's own copy: `trigger` names an icon-only trigger, which without a
visible label has no other name.

props.name: buttonProps
props.description: Props for the default trigger button. Ignored when `renderTrigger` replaces it.

props.name: align
props.description:
How the surface lines up with the trigger along the side it opens on.
`UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: side
props.description: Where the surface opens relative to the trigger.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Class for the menu surface itself: the escape hatch for styling it.

props.name: width
props.description:
Fixed surface width: any CSS length, or `"trigger"` to match the trigger, for a menu that
reads as the field's own list. Left unset the menu sizes to its widest row.

props.name: minWidth
props.description: A floor under the content-sized width.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description:
Ceiling for the content-sized default: a reading measure rather than the viewport, so one
long label doesn't widen every row. Unset, the surface also stops at the space available.

props.name: closeOnSelect
props.description:
Closes the menu when an entry is chosen. Turn it off for a menu of checkbox rows, where
the reader is setting several things at once; an entry's own `closeOnSelect` overrides
it. `UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: labelVisibility
props.description:
Where the trigger's `label` shows. `responsive` hides it below `sm`, leaving the glyph,
for a toolbar that has to survive a phone; `hidden` hides it at every width.
`UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: preserveOrder
props.description: Keeps the declared order instead of moving destructive entries last.

props.name: renderLink
props.description:
Routes `href` actions through the app's router, keeping this framework-agnostic. Return
an element, not a function that spreads props: the menu merges its own props onto the
element, so the row keeps its menu item role.

props.name: renderTrigger
props.description:
Replaces the trigger entirely, for a menu hanging off something that is not a button:
an account block, a sidebar row, a tab. For different words on a plain button, use
`label` and `icon`.

members.name: trigger
members.description: Accessible name for an icon-only trigger, which has no visible text of its own.

members.name: overflow
members.description: Accessible name for the trigger holding the actions that did not fit as buttons.

ActionOverlayOutlet.description:
Renders the active action's modality — alert, dialog, or drawer. Mount one inside the
`ActionProvider`; every surface that runs an action with a `modality` then shares it.

ActionProvider.description: Owns the action registry and the run state. Mount one near the app shell.

ActionScope.description:
Declarative registration, for actions that belong to a subtree rather than a component.
Registers `actions` under `scope` while mounted, and surfaces inside it resolve in that scope.

ActionSheet.description:
ActionDialog's recipe over a sheet, for longer work: a filter rail, an inspector, a long
form. Its own props are the edge's — side, size, length, inset, modality.

props.name: size
props.description: Cross-axis extent: a side panel's width.

props.name: length
props.description: How far it runs along its edge; `inset` sets the gap from the viewport. See base/sheet.

props.name: modality
props.description:
How much of the page it takes hostage. `modal` traps focus, locks scroll and makes the page
inert; `non-modal` sits beside the app (inspectors, filter rails) and leaves the
surrounding page interactive; `trap-focus` is in between. A non-modal panel is not
announced as a dialog, so never use it for a question that must be answered.

not both.

props.description: Controlled: hands the open state to the caller. Supply this OR `trigger`, not both.

members.name: emptyHint
members.description: A second line under the empty title. Empty hides it.

members.name: undated
members.description: The group label for an entry with no timestamp.

members.name: you
members.description: Substituted for the viewer's own name.

members.name: changesTitle
members.description: Captions inside an expanded event.

members.name: moreLabel
members.description: For a count of hidden metadata entries: "+2 more".

members.name: sources
members.description: `source` → label and `event` → label, merged one level deep. An empty string hides the badge.

ActivityAction.description: An activity's action: the kit's `ContextAction`, bound to the activity.

members.name: presentation
members.description: `inline` renders a button under the row; `menu` keeps it in the overflow. `placement` wins when both are set.

members.name: onClick
members.description: Receives the subject the set was resolved against.

members.name: visible
members.description: `false`, or a predicate returning false, omits the action for that subject.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Worked out per subject, so a locked row shows the action greyed rather than missing.

members.name: placement
members.description:
Forces this entry to one side when the set is split between buttons and a menu:
`inline` stays a button whatever `max` is, `menu` always overflows, and `auto` fills
the buttons in order up to `max`.

members.name: type
members.description: `checkbox` renders a toggle driven by `checked` / `onCheckedChange`.

members.name: href
members.description:
Renders the entry as a link. A native `<a href>` by default, which is a full page
navigation — pass `renderLink` to route it through the app's router instead.

members.name: description
members.description: Second line under the label.

members.name: shortcut
members.description: Trailing content — a keyboard shortcut, rendered in the shortcut treatment.

members.name: trailing
members.description: Trailing content beside the shortcut — a badge, a count.

members.name: group
members.description:
Starts a new group, ruling off above this entry. A string also captions it; `true`
rules off without a heading (e.g. to set apart a sign-out or delete).

members.name: buttonStyle
members.description: Treatment when the action renders as a button. `link` is a ghost that underlines.

members.name: closeOnSelect
members.description: Overrides the menu's `closeOnSelect` for this entry.

members.name: render
members.description: Replaces the rendered entry — a framework `<Link>`, for instance.

ActivityActionsMenu.description: A row's overflow menu: its actions, bound to the activity.

members.name: id
members.description: Compared against `currentUserId` to render "You" instead of a name.

members.name: old
members.description: `null` means there was no prior value; `undefined` means it is not reported.

members.name: new
members.description: `null` means the value was cleared.

members.name: description
members.description: Used when neither side is given — "recalculated", "re-indexed".

ActivityChanges.description:
The before-and-after of an edit. Changes render as pairs rather than prose so a long diff
stays scannable.

props.name: bare
props.description: Drops the frame, for use inside a panel that already has one.

ActivityDateLabel.description:
The date heading a group of rows on the rail. An empty label, from an ungrouped feed,
renders nothing.

ActivityEmptyState.description:
The state with no events: the empty feed, with a glyph in the marker column so it reads as
empty rather than broken.

props.name: hint
props.description: A second line, for a feed that can say WHY it is empty.

ActivityExpandToggle.description:
The control that opens a row's detail. A real button rather than a clickable row, so a
keyboard reader can reach it without traversing the entry.

ActivityFeed.description: The timeline of events, grouped by date on one rail.

props.name: activities
props.description:
In display order. Grouped by date as they come, not bucketed — bucketing would silently
reorder a feed sorted by something other than date.

props.name: density
props.description: How much of a row is drawn. `rich` adds metadata, changes, resources, and actions.

props.name: itemSpacing
props.description: The rhythm between rows, independent of how much each row draws.

props.name: defaultExpandedIds
props.description: Uncontrolled: the rows expanded at first.

props.name: expandedIds
props.description: Controlled. Supplying it hands expansion to the caller.

props.name: onExpandedIdsChange
props.description:
Always gets the full id list, controlled or not, because a consumer persisting the set
needs the set.

props.name: currentUserId
props.description:
Turns this person's own name into “You”. Both ids must be defined for the match, or a
feed with no ids anywhere would call every actor “You”.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows initial loading for an empty feed, or an update status above existing rows. Keeps
loaded details and composer drafts mounted.

props.name: error
props.description:
Failure feedback for a load or refresh, with an optional retry action through `onRetry`.
A failed refresh keeps existing history visible; the consumer owns the request and its
loading state.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: The retry action offered with `error`.

props.name: eventConfig
props.description:
Merged over the kit's defaults, so one event can be redefined without restating the rest.
Every `status_changed` in an application should look the same; deciding per call site
guarantees it eventually does not.

props.name: slots
props.description:
`renderRow`, `renderHeadline`, `renderMarker` and `renderDetails` replace a row's parts;
`renderDateLabel`, `empty`, `loading`, `header` and `footer` the feed's own regions.
`renderRow` returning `undefined` hands the row back to the feed — which is how
ActivityLog replaces only its comment rows.

props.name: locale
props.description: Overrides the scope's dates locale, for a feed rendered in another language.

props.name: onResourceClick
props.type: (resource: ActivityResourceRef, config: ActivityResourceConfig | undefined, activity: ActivityItem<TData>) => void

props.name: resources
props.description:
The registry rows look their resources up in, by key. A hundred rows referencing
`order:1234` follow when it is renamed, and none of them stores the name. This is the
registry's seed, re-seeded whenever this reference changes.

props.name: onResourcesChange
props.description: Fires on every mutation, so the registry can be persisted.

members.name: header
members.description: Above the first row — usually a composer.

ActivityHeadline.description:
The sentence, assembled from typed segments rather than interpolated. The fallback is the
point: an event whose actor or subject is missing still reads as a sentence instead of
rendering “undefined updated”.

props.name: currentUserId
props.description: Matched against a segment's `actorId` to render "You".

props.name: onResourceClick
props.type: (resource: ActivityResourceRef, config: ActivityResourceConfig | undefined, activity: ActivityItem<TData>) => void

members.name: event
members.description: The domain event key. Looked up in the event registry for an icon and a tone.

members.name: source
members.description: Which system it came from. Drives the source badge.

members.name: segments
members.description:
The headline as typed parts: actor, field, value, status, resource, text. Preferred over
`headline`: “Maria changed Status from Draft to Published” is a person, a field, and two
values, and a template string cannot express that.

members.name: headline
members.description:
The fallback when there are no segments. The actor's name is split out of it, so a feed
migrated from a system that only stored sentences still gets a clickable actor.

members.name: timestamp
members.description: A pre-formatted time, bypassing the formatters entirely.

ActivityLog.description:
Events and comments on one rail, built on ActivityFeed: a comment is an activity whose row is
a `CommentItem`, so both share markers, date groups and ordering.

props.name: entries
props.description:
A union of comment entries and activity entries, sorted here by `order`. An entry with no
timestamp sorts to the far end rather than shuffling.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows initial loading for an empty log, or an update status above existing entries. Keeps
loaded entries and the composer mounted during a refresh.

props.name: error
props.description:
Fetch failure feedback, independent of comment submission errors, with an optional retry
action through `onRetry`. A failed refresh keeps existing history visible; the consumer
owns the request and its loading state.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: The retry action offered with `error`.

props.name: order
props.description: `desc` puts the newest first, which is what a log usually wants.

props.name: activityStrings
props.description: Separate from the comment copy: the two vocabularies are unrelated.

props.name: renderers
props.description: Keyed by entry kind, replacing the built-in row for that kind.

props.name: composer
props.description:
The comment composer: `enabled`, the `context` it posts against, `onSubmit`, and its
`position`. Omit to render the log read-only. Its `inlineSubmit` defaults to `false` here,
unlike a standalone composer: a log's submit sits above a wall of history, and one hidden
on the toolbar reads as formatting.

props.name: getStatusLabel
props.description: Turns `comment.status` into something a reader recognises.

members.name: context
members.type: { id: string; type: string; moduleKey?: string; }

members.name: inlineSubmit
members.description: Puts the submit on the toolbar instead of a footer row. Defaults to `false`.

ActivityMarker.description:
The dot on the rail. It knows whether it is last, because the connector below it is what
tells a reader the run has ended.

props.name: last
props.description: The rail stops at the last row rather than running into nothing.

ActivityResourceConfig.description: What a resource looks like, held once in the registry and looked up by every row that references it.

members.name: tone
members.description:
The record type's colour, drawn on the chip's glyph only — chip colour is reserved for
state (`badge`). See the vocabulary note in activities.module.css.

members.name: badge
members.description: The record's own state, as toned text inside the chip. Colour here IS the meaning.

members.name: note
members.description: Shown on hover.

ActivityResourceRef.description: A pointer. The registry holds what it points AT.

members.name: key
members.description: Domain-scoped, conventionally `order:1234`.

members.name: label
members.description: Used when the registry has no entry for the key.

ActivityResourceTag.description:
The chip naming what was edited, or whatever else an event acted on. Its label is the
registry entry's (`config`), then `fallbackText`, then the ref's own, then the raw key.

props.name: fallbackText
props.description: Used when the registry has no entry and the ref has no label.

props.name: showDetails
props.description: Compact references inside a headline omit their secondary facts.

ActivityRow.description:
One entry on the rail. Density changes the marker size and the row rhythm together —
changing one without the other is what makes a compact feed look mis-aligned rather than
dense.

props.name: detailLabels
props.type: { changes?: string; metadata?: string; resources?: string; }
props.description: Captions for the expanded detail groups.

props.name: absoluteTime
props.description: Shown on hover of the relative time — the exact moment.

props.name: onResourceClick
props.type: (resource: ActivityResourceRef, config: ActivityResourceConfig | undefined, activity: ActivityItem<TData>) => void

props.name: value
props.description:
The address, as fields — line1, line2, city, region, postalCode, country. Anything
empty simply drops out.

props.name: format
props.description:
`block` is the envelope form: an `<address>` element with a line per row. `inline` is
one line, in a span, for a cell or a summary.

props.name: countryCode
props.description:
An ISO country code deciding the line order (`US`, `GB`, `DE`). Read from
`value.country` when that is a code; never inferred from the reader's locale — the
locale is a language and the address is a place.

props.name: order
props.description: Overrides the ordering outright, for a country the kit does not know.

AddressParts.description:
Postal address ordering. There is no `Intl` for addresses, so this ships three common
orderings keyed by country, a documented default, and an explicit `order` for the rest.

members.name: region
members.description: State, province, county — whatever the country calls the level above a city.

AiAgent.description: The identity strip that says which agent is answering.

props.name: avatar
props.description: Replaces the icon medallion — an image, a gradient mark.

props.name: variant
props.description: `inline` is a single-line chip; `card` is a tile.

AiArtifact.description: The frame around a produced artifact: its title, its actions, and what it holds.

props.name: collapsed
props.description: Header only — the artifact as a chip that opens somewhere else.

AiAttachment.description: One file a turn carried, as a chip or a thumbnail tile, with its upload progress.

props.name: thumbnailUrl
props.description: Renders the chip as a thumbnail tile.

props.name: errored
props.description: Overrides progress.

AiChainOfThought.description: The step timeline of an agent's plan.

props.name: steps
props.description: Order is significant.

members.name: body
members.description: Anything the step produced — a tool call, a code block, sub-steps.

AiChat.description:
The agent header, the transcript, and the composer, wired together. No fetcher, router or
streaming client: messages, input, queue and attachments are props, and submitting is a
callback.

props.name: messages
props.description:
Oldest first. Each carries `parts`, which is where the mix lives — text, reasoning, a chain
of thought, a tool call, code, sources, a task, an artifact, a confirmation, attachments,
or custom.

props.name: inputValue
props.description:
The composer's text. Controlled: the composer holds no draft of its own, so clearing it
after a submit is the consumer's, which is also where the failed-send-restores-the-text
case lives.

props.name: onInputChange
props.description: Receives every edit to `inputValue`.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description:
Fires on Enter or the send button. An attachment on its own is a valid message — “here,
look at this” needs no words.

props.name: onStop
props.description: What the stop control calls while `streaming`.

props.name: streaming
props.description:
Flips submit to stop. Separate from `disabled`, because a streaming chat is still readable
and still cancellable; a disabled one is neither.

props.name: agent
props.description:
Name, icon, subtitle, tone and status for the header strip. `null` hides the strip
entirely.

props.name: slots
props.description:
Seven regions replaced outright — `header`, `intro`, `belowMessages`, `empty`, `queue`,
`suggestions`, `input` — plus `renderMessage` for a turn. This is the seam that keeps a
prop per idea out of the API.

AiChatAgent.description: Who is answering. Drives the header strip.

members.name: avatar
members.description: Replaces the icon medallion — an image, a gradient mark.

members.name: progress
members.description: 0–1, while it is still uploading.

AiChatAttachmentsStrip.description:
The files attached to the turn being written, as one of the strips above the composer's
field; a sent turn's attachments render as one too.

AiChatConversation.description:
The transcript. Exported, like the composer and the empty state, because a consumer building
a different chat layout against the same data should get the parts without taking the shell.

props.name: messages
props.description: Oldest first.

AiChatEmptyState.description:
The state before the first turn. Exported, like the transcript and the composer, because a
consumer building a different chat layout against the same data should get the parts
without taking the shell.

props.name: below
props.description: Under the body — a grid of starter prompts, usually.

members.name: authorName
members.description: Falls back to a role-derived label in the bubble.

members.name: pending
members.description: Renders the shimmer INSTEAD of the parts — the turn before the first token.

members.name: trailing
members.description: Under the bubble: a feedback row, a retry, a footnote.

AiChatPromptInput.description:
The composer. Exported, like the transcript and the empty state, because a consumer building
a different chat layout against the same data should get the parts without taking the shell.

props.name: streaming
props.description: Flips submit to stop.

props.name: showAttach
props.description: Defaults to showing whenever `onAttach` is given.

props.name: leadingActions
props.description: Before the attach button — a model picker, usually.

props.name: trailingActions
props.description: Before submit.

props.name: submitKeyLabel
props.description: What the hint calls the submit key.

members.name: stopAria
members.description: Replaces the submit label while a response is streaming.

members.name: hint
members.description: `{{submitKey}}` and `{{newlineKey}}` are replaced by the real shortcuts.

AiChatQueue.description: The strip above the composer holding the messages waiting to send.

members.name: intro
members.description: Before the transcript — a welcome card, an agent introduction.

members.name: belowMessages
members.description: After the transcript, before the composer.

members.name: renderMessage

Alert.description:
A notice in a tone. Status tones bring their own glyph, so colour is not the only signal.
A destructive alert interrupts the screen reader; every other tone is a polite status.

Structural presentation. `inverse` is a solid slab for a single emphatic notice; the
tone still describes the intent.

Leading glyph. Defaults to the tone's own conventional glyph; pass a node to replace
it, or `false` for an alert that must have none.

AlertDialogCancel.description:
The answer that backs out. Both answers close the dialog; `AlertDialogAction` is the one
that commits. With no dismissal and no corner close, they are the only ways out.

props.description: The element this answer becomes — a form submit, a router link.

AlertDialogContent.description:
A centred surface that demands an answer. It fixes `placement` to centre and announces as
`alertdialog`; both dismissal routes are fixed off and the corner close is off by
default, so the backdrop and Escape never decide for the reader. `modality`, `surface`
and `initialFocusRef` are OverlayContent's props.

props.name: size
length
props.description:
Along-axis extent, for an edge placement. Less than full detaches the panel and centres
it on that axis. It is measured against the space the inset leaves rather than the
viewport: 70% of an inset panel is 70% of what is between the offsets, and the rest is
split between the two ends. Full needs no inset to look right, which is why a
corner-anchored sheet sets only `inset`.

props.name: inset
props.description:
The gap to the viewport edges. `false` is flush — a sheet welded to the side; `true`
uses the kit's gap; any CSS length sets your own. One offset, spent on every side the
panel does not run to, so an inset side panel sits the same distance from the top, the
side and the bottom. Any gap detaches it, rounds all four corners and gives it a full
border.

The search-driven single-select picker, for a screen that already holds its results: the

row replaces results and `onSearch` does not fire; `0` allows browsing before typing.

and each chip's remove control.

props.description:
The server query: fires after `debounceMs` with the trimmed value, only at or above

props.name: debounceMs
props.description: The quiet period before `onSearch` fires, in milliseconds.

props.name: creatable
props.description: Offers an inline create row when nothing matches. Needs `onCreate` to do anything.

AsyncPreviewRoot.description:
The root of the compound over `useAsyncPreview`: it runs the fetch, the cache and the open
state for the parts inside it. Compound rather than one `renderPreview` prop because the four
states want four different shapes, and a single render prop makes the caller branch on all
of them every time.

props.name: onShow
props.description:
The fetcher, run when the preview opens or the trigger prefetches it. Supply this or
`data`, not both.

props.name: type
props.description:
Names the kind of record. Passed back to `onShow`, so one fetcher can serve several types.
Caching requires `cacheKey`.

props.name: context
props.description: Whatever the fetcher needs — usually an id. Handed to `onShow` unchanged.

props.name: cacheKey
props.description:
The record identity and cache key: it enables the cache. Change it when the record
changes; absent, nothing is cached, and each open fetches or consumes its hover prefetch.

props.name: cachePolicy
props.description:
`cache-first` serves a fresh cache entry without a request. `always` refetches on every
open — for a value that changes while the reader is on the page.

props.name: staleTime
props.description:
How long a cache entry counts as fresh, in ms: five minutes. Entries are evicted on read;
nothing wakes up on a timer.
