AuthSplitPanel.description:
Form beside a panel, for a caller composing both halves itself. `AuthShell
variant="split"` is the same arrangement with the shell's own card.

props.name: form
props.description: The sign-in surface. Usually an AuthShell with `variant="bare"`.

props.name: panel
props.description:
Marketing copy, a testimonial, an illustration. Hidden below 56rem of available width
unless `panelMobile` stacks it; omitting it gives the form the full available width.

props.name: panelPosition
props.description:
Which side the panel is drawn on. The form stays first in the DOM either way, so
reading and keyboard order remain form first.

props.name: panelMobile
props.description: What the panel does when this container is narrower than 56rem.

Avatar.description: A person or an entity as a disc: an image, with initials behind it for when there is none.

props.name: size
props.description: Disc size. One of the kit's few size props: an avatar has no content to scale with.

AvatarBadge.description: A small status mark on the disc's corner.

AvatarCell.description:
A name with its avatar, falling back to initials, and an optional subtitle. One of the cells
every admin table has, so a page does not rewrite it per column: a thin arrangement over the
kit's primitives that adds the cell's part — the alignment, the truncation, the empty case.

props.name: imageUrl
props.description: Falls back to initials when absent or broken.

AvatarFallback.description: Shown when there is no image. Initials, not a placeholder glyph.

AvatarGroupCount.description:
The "+3" at the end of an `AvatarGroup`. A count rather than another avatar, so a group of
twelve does not need twelve images to say so.

AvatarImage.description:
The picture. An empty `alt` is correct beside a visible name; the name already announces
the person.

AvatarUpload.description: The round variant, sized for a profile image.

props.name: id
props.description: Applied to the file input itself, so a `FormField` label can address it.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this control's own copy — the empty frame, the overlay, and remove.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen file, controlled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the chosen file, or `undefined` when it is removed.

props.name: onRejectedFiles
props.description:
Receives the refused files. Report them through FormField's `error` prop: the error and
helper text are associated with the native input.

props.name: previewUrl
props.description:
An already-stored image. Uncontrolled, removing it clears its preview; when `value` is
controlled, clear both `value` and `previewUrl` in `onValueChange` to remove it.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The field's label, from `FormField`; the input is named by it and its action ("Logo Upload image").

props.name: accept
props.description:
Native accept filter, e.g. `.pdf,image/*`. Enforced here as well as by the dialog, and
checked before `onValueChange` rather than after, like every constraint.

props.name: minSizeBytes
props.description: Smallest file accepted, in bytes.

props.name: maxSizeBytes
props.description: Largest file accepted, in bytes.

props.name: validateFile
props.description: Runs after the type and size checks.

props.name: tone
props.description: Semantic colour: what the badge means. `variant` decides how much of it is applied.

props.name: variant
props.description: How much of the tone is applied. Structural, not semantic.

props.name: dot
props.description: A leading status dot in the badge's own tone.

props.name: pending
props.description: Draws the dot hollow, for a state that has not happened yet: "queued", not "failed".

props.name: pulse
props.description: Animates the dot, for a state that is actively changing.

props.name: render
props.description:
The element the badge becomes — an anchor or a router link, for a badge that links.
The dot and `children` go inside it.

props.name: selectedCount
props.description: The bar renders nothing at zero, so a caller can mount it unconditionally.

props.name: totalCount
props.description: Optional denominator for the summary. Omit when the total is unknown or unbounded.

props.name: onClear
props.description: Drops the selection. Omit to render no clear control — a selection the user cannot drop needs a reason.

props.name: placement
props.description: `floating` docks to the bottom centre of the viewport; `inline` sits in flow.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this bar's own copy: `summary(selected, total)`, `clear`, and the region's accessible `label`.

props.name: children
props.description: The bulk actions. Buttons, a menu, whatever the surface needs.

props.name: amount
props.description:
How far to escape, on the spacing scale. Match it to the padding being cancelled — a
surface at `--space-md` bleeds `md` — so the two move together under a density change.

props.name: axis
props.description:
Which way to escape; `both` covers every direction. Sideways is the common case: an
image bleeds across and keeps its vertical rhythm.

props.name: status
props.description: A chip, usually — the booking's state.

props.name: details
props.description:
Rendered as a real `<dl>`, so a screen reader pairs each value with its own label. A
`fullWidth` detail spans the row and gets its own ground.

props.name: title
props.description:
The heading. Either it or `description` renders the header; neither, and the block is a
bare surface.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting copy on its own row, so a long one wraps under the whole header.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading glyph on the title line.

props.name: titleSuffix
props.description: Content immediately after the title — a badge, a count.

props.name: headerEnd
props.description: Controls at the end of the title line.

props.name: surface
props.description:
Outer chrome. What separates `bordered` from `card` is the ground: a bordered block is a
ruled region and the page shows through it; a card block lifts off it.

props.name: flush
props.description:
Drops the surface's inset and clips to its radius, for content that runs to the edge
(divided cells, ruled rows); children pay their own inset. Only meaningful on a surface
that has an inset to drop.

members.name: fullWidth
members.description: Spans the row and sits on its own ground — for a note or an address.

BooleanIndicator.description: A yes/no state as a dot and a word. The word is required, since colour alone fails.

props.name: value
props.description: The state, drawn as a dot and a word so it does not rely on colour alone.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides what each state is called: `strings.true` and `strings.false`, the two words.
Yes/No, Enabled/Disabled, Paid/Unpaid — "Active"/"Paused" beats "true"/"false".

members.name: true
members.description:
What each state is called. Yes/No, Enabled/Disabled, Paid/Unpaid — the pair is
domain copy, not a fixed vocabulary.

BreadcrumbProgress.description:
A wizard’s position, as a trail. Not Breadcrumbs: a trail describes where you ARE in a
hierarchy you can climb, and this describes how far along a sequence you have got — the
steps behind you are done, not ancestors.

props.name: currentIndex
props.description: Zero-based.

props.name: onStepClick
props.description:
Makes completed steps and the current one reachable, never later ones. Without it the
steps are plain list items.

members.name: hint
members.description: A second line, shown from lg up where there is room for it.

members.name: step
members.description:
Names each step — "Step 2: Billing", and "Step 1: Account, completed" for one already
walked past. The current step is marked by `aria-current`, so it needs no word here.

members.name: position
members.description: The summary above the trail — "Step 2 of 4".

Breadcrumbs.description:
The trail to the current page, in a `<nav>`. The current page is a span marked
`aria-current="page"`, not a link: a link to the page you are on is a dead control.

props.name: items
props.description: The trail. The last entry renders as the current page.

props.name: separator
props.description:
Replaces the chevron between crumbs. It is decorative either way — the trail's meaning
is in the links.

props.name: label
props.description: Names this one trail. Overrides the strings default.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides the default name for every trail.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the trail.

Button.description:
The kit's action primitive. No `size` prop by design: geometry follows the scale factors,
so a denser region is a scope (styles/FACTORS.md).

props.name: tone
props.description:
Semantic colour intent. Resolves through the provider when omitted, so `UIProvider`
defaults can change it.

props.name: buttonStyle
props.description: Fill treatment, independent of `tone`. `UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description: Square button sized to its height. The label becomes the accessible name.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretches the button to its container's width.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a spinner and blocks interaction. The label keeps its space so the button does
not resize mid-action.

props.name: render
props.description:
The element this button becomes — an anchor, a router link, a label. `children` stay
the content and keep the button's label wrapper, so a link still sizes like a button.
`render` is how every kit component changes its element, the contract Base UI's parts
already take.

  <Button render={<a href="/settings" />}>Settings</Button>

ButtonGroup.description: Adjacent buttons that read as one control: one hairline seam, squared inner corners.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The direction the buttons run in.

ButtonGroupSeparator.description:
The seam between welded buttons, where the collapsed border alone is not enough. A plain
`Separator` here would draw a full-height rule against the group's own border.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The orientation of the group it sits in; the seam runs across it.

ButtonGroupText.description:
A label that sits in the run without becoming pressable — a unit, a prefix, a count. A
span, so it adds no tab stop.

CSPProvider.description:
Passes the request nonce and inline-style policy to every Base UI-backed primitive below
it. Place it once around the React root during SSR; `disableStyleElements` is for
consumers that provide the equivalent positioning CSS themselves.

props.name: nonce
props.description: The nonce value to apply to inline `<style>` and `<script>` tags.

props.name: disableStyleElements
props.description: Whether inline `<style>` elements created by Base UI components should not be rendered. Instead, components must specify the CSS styles via custom class names or other methods.

CURRENCY_SYMBOLS.description:
The code-to-symbol map the currency options are labelled from, exported so a caller can
render the same symbol elsewhere. A starting set: anything not here is passed as a full
option.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this calendar's own copy — the caption controls, which are icon-only and have
no other name. `DatePicker` passes its own strings straight through, so one override
names both.

props.name: mode
props.description: Selection behaviour, as on `DatePicker`: one date, a range, or several dates.

props.name: value
props.description: The selection, in the shape the mode uses.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the new selection, in the shape the mode uses.

props.name: month
props.description:
The month shown, for a calendar whose position is driven from outside. Uncontrolled
unless supplied.

props.name: onMonthChange
props.description: Called with the first day of the month the calendar moves to.

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description:
How many months to show side by side. Two is the usual range picker; each grid keeps its
own caption, so the second month is not anonymous.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description:
Which day begins the week; `0` is Sunday. Falls back to the provider's dates setting
rather than a hard-coded Monday, so `UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: minDate
props.description: Earliest selectable day, inclusive.

props.name: maxDate
props.description: Latest selectable day, inclusive.

props.name: disabledDates
props.description: Refuses individual days — weekends, holidays, days already booked.

CalendarDayData.description: One day, after the events have been placed on it.

members.name: events
members.description: All-day first, then by start time.

members.name: endDate
members.description: Inclusive. An event without one occupies its start day alone.

members.name: category
members.description: A category id. An unknown one falls back to the neutral token.

members.name: metadata
members.description: Free-form payload. The default card reads `customerName`, `guestCount`, `serviceName` and `cellTitle` when present.

members.name: chooseMonth
members.description: Describes what the caption button does (switch to the month grid); the month is its name.

Card.description:
The single surface primitive. Slot props (`title`, `description`, `actions`, `footerText`,
…) cover the common shape; `CardHeader`, `CardContent` and `CardFooter` are exported for
composing.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading glyph on the title line.

props.name: title
props.description: Header copy. The title truncates rather than pushing header controls off the row.

props.name: titleSuffix
props.description: Badges, status, or counts immediately after the title.

props.name: tooltip
description
props.description: Header copy under the title.

props.name: surface
props.description:
Outer chrome. `framed`, the bezel, is the default; `card` is the plain panel. Change it
for a whole product once with `UIProvider` `defaults.card.surface`.

props.name: headerStart
props.description: Full-width row above the title — an eyebrow or breadcrumb. Rare.

props.name: headerEnd
props.description: Metadata or a secondary control before the action and overflow menu.

props.name: headerAction
props.description: A single control at the end of the header. Use `actions` for a list of commands.

props.name: actions
props.description:
Overflow commands, collapsed into one menu trigger and rendered by the shared
`ActionMenu`: a destructive entry moves last and is separated.

props.name: titleLevel
props.description:
Renders the title as a heading of this level, for a card that heads a page or a region.
Unset, the title is a span that heading navigation can't find.

props.name: media
props.description:
A full-bleed strip above the header — a cover image, a map, a brand band — clipped to
the card's top corners.

props.name: alert
props.description: Banner between header and content. A plain string is wrapped in an `Alert`.

props.name: alertTone
props.description: Tone of the alert band.

props.name: contentTop
props.description: Content inside the content inset, above `children`.

props.name: contentBottom
props.description: Content inside the content inset, below `children`.

props.name: footerText
props.description: Muted text in the footer band.

props.name: footerSlot
props.description: Footer band under the content — a single primary action fits well here.

props.name: headerDivider
props.description: A rule between the header and the content. `UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: footerDivider
props.description: A rule between the content and the footer.

props.name: expandable
props.description:
Clips content to a collapsed height with a fade, and adds a toggle. `true` uses
`--card-collapsed-height`; the object form sets the height for this card only.

props.name: expanded
props.description: Whether an expandable card's content is expanded, for controlled expansion.

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.description: Whether an expandable card starts expanded, for uncontrolled expansion.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Called with the new state when the reader expands or collapses the content.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this card's own copy — the info glyph, the overflow trigger, and the
disclosure control's name in each state.

members.name: id
members.description: Stable key. Falls back to a string `label`, then the index.

members.name: label
members.description:
What the entry says. The only part of the row that gives way: a long label truncates
instead of pushing the shortcut or trailing content off.

members.name: type
members.description: `checkbox` renders a toggle driven by `checked` / `onCheckedChange`.

members.name: href
members.description:
Renders the entry as a link. A native `<a href>` by default, which is a full page
navigation — pass `renderLink` to route it through the app's router instead.

members.name: description
members.description: Second line under the label.

members.name: shortcut
members.description: Trailing content — a keyboard shortcut, rendered in the shortcut treatment.

members.name: trailing
members.description: Trailing content beside the shortcut — a badge, a count.

members.name: group
members.description:
Starts a new group, ruling off above this entry. A string also captions it; `true`
rules off without a heading (e.g. to set apart a sign-out or delete).

members.name: tone
members.description: Semantic intent. `destructive` also moves the entry last and separates it.

members.name: buttonStyle
members.description: Treatment when the action renders as a button. `link` is a ghost that underlines.

members.name: visible
members.description: `false` omits the action entirely.

members.name: closeOnSelect
members.description: Overrides the menu's `closeOnSelect` for this entry.

members.name: render
members.description: Replaces the rendered entry — a framework `<Link>`, for instance.

CardActionStrip.description:
A card's commands as buttons. One array decides which action is primary and how the rest
follow, so a page of cards cannot disagree about it.

props.name: actions
props.description:
The commands, as the overflow menu takes them. The first is the primary action; the rest
follow in outline unless an entry sets its own `buttonStyle`.

props.name: separator
props.description: A rule above the strip, ruling it off from content that runs right into it.

props.name: align
props.description: Where the buttons sit along the strip.

props.name: fullWidthPrimary
props.description:
Stretches the first action, for a card whose action is the point, or a narrow card where
two buttons will not fit.

props.name: renderLink
props.description: Routes `href` actions through the app's router.

CardCheckboxGroup.description:
The same cards as `CardRadioGroup` for a multiple choice: takes and returns an array of
values.

props.name: options
props.description: The choices, in the shape `CardRadioGroup` takes.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial values, for uncontrolled selection.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with every chosen value.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column count at full width, as on `CardRadioGroup`.

props.name: name
props.description: Field name, used for the group's native form participation.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every option.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Applies the invalid treatment. Pair it with a message on the FormField.

props.name: aria-label
props.description:
The group's name and description. `FormField` supplies `aria-labelledby` and
`aria-describedby`.

members.name: description
members.description: Supporting sentence. Card and list groups show it; a pill has no room for one.

members.name: icon
members.description: Leading glyph. A Lucide icon, any component taking a className, or a rendered node.

members.name: tooltip
members.description:
Detail that doesn't fit the row, shown in a tooltip from an info glyph beside the label.
The glyph isn't focusable; the text also becomes the option's accessible description.

CardPrimaryAction.description:
Stretches an anchor across the whole card, so the card is one tab stop rather than a grid
of them (wrapping the card would nest its controls inside an anchor). Interactive children
are lifted above it in CSS.

props.name: label
props.description:
The link's accessible name. The visible title is not necessarily the destination, and
many cards share one.

CardRadioGroup.description:
Single-select as a grid of cards: a title, an optional description, an icon and a
tooltip. `CardCheckboxGroup` is its multi-select twin.

props.name: options
props.description:
The choices, in the one shape card, list and pill groups share: value, label,
description, icon, and an optional tooltip.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial value, for uncontrolled selection.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the chosen value.

props.name: columns
props.description:
Column count at full width: the track floor, not a fixed count — the grid still steps
down on its own container's width. Pick it from how much each card has to say.

props.name: name
props.description: Field name, used for the group's native form participation.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every option.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Applies the invalid treatment. Pair it with a message on the FormField.

props.name: aria-label
props.description:
The group's name and description. `FormField` supplies `aria-labelledby` and
`aria-describedby`.

members.name: description
members.description: Supporting sentence. Card and list groups show it; a pill has no room for one.

members.name: icon
members.description: Leading glyph. A Lucide icon, any component taking a className, or a rendered node.

members.name: tooltip
members.description:
Detail that doesn't fit the row, shown in a tooltip from an info glyph beside the label.
The glyph isn't focusable; the text also becomes the option's accessible description.

CardSkeleton.description:
A placeholder that reserves the real card's box, so the page doesn't reflow when content
lands. Matching the surface and the line count is the whole job: a placeholder of the wrong
shape moves the page twice.

props.name: surface
props.description:
Match the real card's surface. Unset, it takes the card's default (the provider's
`defaults.card.surface`, framed out of the box).

props.name: showHeader
props.description: Reserves the header's height.

props.name: lines
props.description: Lines of content to reserve. Match the real card's.

props.name: label
props.description: What the placeholder announces while it waits. Unset, the skeleton's own loading copy.

members.name: tooltip
members.description: Accessible name for the info glyph beside the title.

members.name: actions
members.description: Accessible name for the overflow trigger in the header.

members.name: expand
members.description: The disclosure control's name in each state, when the card is expandable.

Carousel.description:
A native scroll-snap track with controls. Script only reports the current slide and
scrolls to a chosen one.

props.name: children
props.description: The slides, usually `CarouselSlide`s.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Which axis snaps.

props.name: controls
props.description:
Where the previous/next buttons sit: `outside` the track, `overlay` on its edges, or
`none` when you compose your own with `CarouselControl`.

props.name: showDots
props.description: Shows the position indicators, and lets them be clicked.

props.name: dotStyle
props.description: `pill` stretches the active indicator instead of only recolouring it.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this carousel's own copy — the region name, the two icon-only controls, and
each pagination dot. It travels through the context, so a control placed with
`CarouselControl` is named by the same override as one the root rendered.

props.name: label
props.description:
Names the region for assistive technology; unset, `strings.label` does. A carousel with
no name is an unexplained scroll box, and a page with two needs two names.

props.name: viewportClassName
props.description:
Styles the scroll container rather than the outer frame — for a carousel that needs its
own padding inside the clip.

CarouselControl.description:
A single previous/next control placed by the caller rather than by the root, for composing
your own layout with `controls="none"`. Must sit inside a `Carousel`.

props.name: direction
props.description: Which way the control moves the track.

CarouselDots.description:
The position indicators on their own, placed by the caller outside the track. Must sit
inside a `Carousel`.

props.name: dotStyle
props.description: `pill` stretches the active indicator instead of only recolouring it.

CarouselSlide.description: One slide of the track, announced as a slide.

props.name: size
props.description: Track width this slide occupies — "100%", "50%", "18rem".

members.name: label
members.description: Names the region. A page with two carousels needs two names.

members.name: previous
members.description: The controls are icon-only, so these are the only names they have.

members.name: goToSlide
members.description: Accessible name for a pagination dot, by the slide it jumps to.

members.name: roleDescription
members.description: What the region and each slide are (`aria-roledescription`), announced before their name.

CategoryNav.description:
A vertical list of destinations with a count on each. Not SideNav: this is a FILTER rail,
where the rows are categories of one list rather than pages of a product, and the count
is the reason a reader picks one.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the region. A page with two rails needs two names.

members.name: id
members.description: Stable identity. The row reports this, not its index.

members.name: count
members.description: A count of what the row selects. `0` renders — "none" is information.

members.name: hint
members.description: A second line under the label.

CellValue.description:
One column's value, formatted. Beside MetadataValue on purpose: that renders a labelled fact on
a detail panel, this renders a value in a grid, where alignment and truncation are the column's
decisions rather than the value's.

props.name: kind
props.description: Which primitive renders it. Defaults to `value`.

props.name: display
props.description: Pre-rendered content, used verbatim; bypasses `kind` and all formatting.

props.name: href
props.description: Where the value navigates, for `link` and the contact kinds.

props.name: pattern
props.description: date-fns pattern, for the date and time kinds.

props.name: from
props.description: The unit the raw value is already in. `fileSize` only.

props.name: moneyUnit
props.description: Minor or major units. `money` only; see the primitive.

props.name: fallback
props.description: What shows when the value is absent.

props.name: missing
props.description: Forces the missing state regardless of the value.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Lets the cell wrap. Cells are nowrap so columns stay readable.

members.name: version
members.description: Shown in mono beside the title — it is an identifier, not prose.

members.name: timestamp
members.description: Already formatted.

ChangelogStrings.description: Copy owned by the timeline blocks. Labels are copy, separate from the data keys (`added` vs "Added").

members.name: byline
members.description: Precedes the author — "— Alice Mercer".

props.name: entries
props.description:
id, kind, title, and optionally description, version, timestamp, author. `kind` is
added | removed | modified | fixed.

ChartContainer.description:
Recharts on the kit's tokens: Recharts owns geometry, this owns chrome. Each series key
maps to `--color-<key>`, so colours are set once in the config; prefer `var(--chart-1)` …
`var(--chart-5)`, which follow the theme.

props.name: config
props.description:
Maps each data key to a label, a colour, and an icon. Each colour becomes
`--color-{key}` on the container.

props.name: children
props.description:
One Recharts chart. `label` and `description` become its `<title>` and `<desc>` unless
it sets its own.

props.name: label
props.description:
What the chart shows, as a sentence a screen reader can speak ("Monthly revenue against
expenses, January to June"). Without it the focusable plot is announced by its tick text.

props.name: description
props.description: A longer summary of the data or its takeaway, read after the label.

ChartLegendContent.description:
The legend body, passed to `ChartLegend` as its `content`. Names, colours and icons come
from the container's config.

props.name: payload
props.description: Supplied by Recharts.

props.name: hideIcon
props.description: Drops the swatch, for a legend beside a chart whose colours are already named.

props.name: nameKey
props.description: Key in the payload holding each series name, when it is not the data key.

ChartPayloadItem.description: One entry of what is under the cursor. Shaped by Recharts, narrowed here.

ChartTooltipContent.description:
The tooltip body, passed to `ChartTooltip` as its `content`. Names, colours and icons come
from the container's config.

props.name: active
props.description:
Supplied by Recharts. A content component is cloned with it; it never receives it from
you.

props.name: payload
props.description:
The entries under the cursor. Supplied by Recharts, which clones a content component with
them; it never receives them from you.

props.name: label
props.description: The hovered category, supplied by Recharts. `labelKey` and `labelFormatter` change what shows.

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Drops the label row.

props.name: hideIndicator
props.description: Drops the swatches.

props.name: indicator
props.description: Shape of the swatch beside each value.

props.name: nameKey
props.description: Key in the payload holding each series name, when it is not the data key.

props.name: labelKey
props.description: Key in the payload holding the tooltip label, when it is not the data key.

props.name: labelFormatter
props.description: Formats the tooltip's heading — a date key into a readable date.

props.name: formatter
props.type: (value: NonNullable<ChartPayloadItem["value"]>, name: NonNullable<ChartPayloadItem["name"]>, item: ChartPayloadItem, index: number) => React.ReactNode
props.description: Formats each value. Without it, numbers get locale grouping.

Checkbox.description:
A native checkbox under the kit's styling, so form, keyboard and label behaviour are the
platform's. `checked` and `defaultChecked` are its controlled and uncontrolled state, and
`onChange` receives the native change event: read `event.target.checked` for the next
state.

props.name: label
props.description: Rendered beside the box and wired to it, so the text is part of the target.

props.name: indeterminate
props.description:
The dash state, for a parent whose children are partly checked: neither on nor off.
Independent of `checked`, which it outranks visually.

props.name: steps
props.description: id, status, title, and optionally badge, content, disabled.

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.description: Uncontrolled starting state. Defaults to the first unfinished step.

props.name: expanded
props.description:
The open steps, controlled. Uncontrolled, the checklist opens the first unfinished
step.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Reports the open steps when a reader opens or closes one.

props.name: onStepOpen
props.description: Fires on the transition into open — for analytics, not for state.

members.name: badge
members.description: Usually a `<Badge>` — "Required", "Recommended".

members.name: content
members.description: Shown when the step is open. Forms, instructions, an action row.

ChecklistStrings.description: Copy owned by the onboarding blocks. Status labels name the step's glyph for screen readers.

members.name: formatProgress
members.description: "2 of 4 complete".

CodeEntry.description:
A discount code or a gift card. One component for both: a title, a field, a button, and
an applied state. The only real difference is that a gift card holds a BALANCE — money
that may outlast this order — where a discount either applies or does not. That is one
optional prop, not a second component.

props.name: kind
props.description:
Picks the preset: the icon, the default copy, and whether the code is upper-cased on
submit. Gift card codes are printed in capitals and nobody types them that way.

props.name: appliedCode
props.description: The code in force. Present switches the card to its applied state.

props.name: appliedDiscount
props.description: What it took off, already formatted.

props.name: balance
props.description:
What is left on the card, already formatted — money that may outlast this order, and
the one real difference between the two kinds. Gift cards only.

props.name: error
props.description: A rejection message, shown under the field.

props.name: title
props.description:
The heading. Either it or `description` renders the header; neither, and the block is a
bare surface.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting copy on its own row, so a long one wraps under the whole header.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading glyph on the title line.

props.name: titleSuffix
props.description: Content immediately after the title — a badge, a count.

props.name: headerEnd
props.description: Controls at the end of the title line.

props.name: surface
props.description:
Outer chrome. What separates `bordered` from `card` is the ground: a bordered block is a
ruled region and the page shows through it; a card block lifts off it.

props.name: flush
props.description:
Drops the surface's inset and clips to its radius, for content that runs to the edge
(divided cells, ruled rows); children pay their own inset. Only meaningful on a surface
that has an inset to drop.

CodeEntryStrings.description:
Copy for `CodeEntry`, which serves both a discount code and a gift card.

Two presets rather than two components: the wording differs because redeeming a gift
card is a balance lookup before it is an application, but the interaction is identical.

members.name: helperText
members.description: Under the title. Empty for the discount case, which needs no explaining.

members.name: fieldLabel
members.description: The field shows no visible label, so this is its only accessible name.

members.name: balance
members.description: What is left on a gift card. Unused by the discount preset.

Collapsible.description: A disclosure that animates to its content's natural height, in CSS alone.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the content is shown, for controlled state.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the content starts shown, for uncontrolled state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires on every toggle, from the pointer or the keyboard.

CollapsibleContent.description:
The disclosed region. It stays mounted while collapsed, to animate, and is inert then, so
its controls leave the tab order.

CollapsibleTrigger.description: The control. Carries `aria-expanded` and points at the content.

props.name: previewValue
props.description:
What the swatch shows, when it differs from the value — a resolved token, say. Defaults
to the current value.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description:
Called with the colour as a string. Typed text is any CSS colour and is not normalised —
what is typed is what is stored; the picker's value arrives in `format`.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this field's own copy — the swatch's name. The swatch is a control, with the
native picker under it, so it needs one.

props.name: format
props.description:
The notation the picker emits — typed text is never rewritten. The kit's own palette is
OKLCH, which is why that is the default; a consumer whose tokens are hex, rgb or hsl
gets their own notation back. The conversion is culori's. With the deprecated `emitHex`
and no `format`, it is `hex`.

props.name: emitHex
props.description: Makes the picker emit hex. `format` wins where both are given.
props.deprecated: Use `format="hex"`; this spelling stays because it is published API.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Glyph before the value, in its own lane so the text never runs under it.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Glyph after the value, in its own lane so the text never runs under it.

props.name: startAddon
props.description:
Short text attached before the value, outside the text itself — a currency symbol, a
protocol, an at sign.

props.name: endAddon
props.description: Short text attached after the value, outside the text itself — a unit, a domain.

props.name: showCharacterCount
props.description: Shows "12 / 80" in the trailing lane. Requires `maxLength`.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Character cap, and the limit the count counts against. Input past it is refused.

props.name: clearable
props.description:
Shows a clear control once the field has a value. Clearing goes through the native
value setter, so React's value tracker stays in sync.

props.name: onClear
props.description: Called after the clear control empties the field.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Replaces the trailing affordance with a spinner, which outranks every other trailing
affordance.

props.name: invalid
props.description:
Applies the invalid treatment. Pair it with FormField's error for the message, so the
border and the announcement cannot disagree.

props.name: returnValueWithAddons
props.description:
Includes string addons in the value reported by `onChange`. Off, because an addon is
presentation: a caller that stores "$" and the number has to strip it again on the way
out.

members.name: picker
members.description: Names the swatch, which is a control (the native picker sits under it).

members.name: clear
members.description: Accessible name for the inline clear action.

members.name: characterCount
members.description: Accessible description of the character counter, e.g. "12 of 80 characters".

ColumnGroup.description: A band above the header row, spanning several columns.

members.name: columns
members.description: Column ids; must be contiguous.

ColumnVisibilityToggle.description: The columns menu, one of the table's own controls: one checkbox per hideable column.

props.name: buttonProps
props.description: Extends or replaces the trigger's public Button composition.

ComboboxArrow.description: An arrow pointing from the popup to its anchor, part of its placement machinery.

ComboboxBackdrop.description: A layer behind the open popup, part of its placement machinery.

ComboboxChip.description:
One selection inside `ComboboxChips`, with its remove control.

The remove control is named from the chip's text, so pass the label as plain text. For
a chip with richer content, `strings.removeChip` supplies the name instead.

ComboboxChips.description:
The multi-select field: the container is the field, and the input sits among the chips so
typing continues where the last selection ended.

ComboboxChipsInput.description: The query input among the chips, so typing continues where the last selection ended.

ComboboxClear.description: The control that empties the field.

ComboboxCollection.description: The renderer that maps a list to items.

ComboboxDropdown.description:
The popup: status row, results, create row, pager and footer. It renders an empty popup
rather than nothing, because a popup that vanishes mid-type reads as a broken control
rather than an empty result.

props.name: listRef
props.description: The scrollable viewport, watched for pagination.

props.name: anchor
props.description: What the popup positions against. The chips row, for a multi-select.

props.name: applyFooter
props.type: { applyLabel: string; cancelLabel: string; onApply: () => void; onCancel: () => void; }

props.name: errorSlot
props.description: Error content, shown instead of everything else.

ComboboxEmpty.description:
Renders only when a search returns nothing, so "no matches" never flashes before the first
keystroke.

ComboboxInputTrigger.description:
The input with its trailing chevron and optional clear button. Its trailing padding is
computed from the same variables that size the controls, so text never runs under them.

props.name: showClear
props.description: Shows the clear button beside the chevron.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Applies the invalid treatment.

props.name: strings
props.description: Names the two trailing controls: the clear button and the chevron.

ComboboxItem.description:
A result row with a trailing selection check. Children go in the label slot. The same row
the pickers render.

ComboboxItemIndicator.description: The tick on a chosen item, on its own, for a row that lays its parts out differently.

ComboboxPopup.description:
The list's surface, anchored to the field's width — unlike a dropdown menu, a listbox that
does not line up with its field reads as a different control.

ComboboxPopupInput.description:
The search band inside the popup, for a combobox opened from a button (`ComboboxTrigger`)
rather than typed into: focus lands here when the popup opens, typing filters the list,
and the arrow keys and Enter still move through the list below it. Give it an
`aria-label` — its placeholder is not a name.

ComboboxPortal.description:
The popup's portal, which escapes an ancestor that clips or transforms. Routed through the
nearest `UIPortalHost` like every kit popup.

ComboboxPositioner.description: Anchors the popup to the trigger, and flips it when there is no room below.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description:
Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the distance to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

ComboboxRoot.description:
The state: Base UI's combobox root, holding `value` and `onValueChange`, `inputValue` and
`onInputValueChange`, `items` and `multiple`. The parts around it are the Base UI anatomy
with the kit's surface applied — parts, not a recipe; the searchable, single- and
multi-select recipes compose them. Field parts carry `data-field-control` /
`data-field-shell`, matching Input, Textarea and Select.

ComboboxSeparator.description: A rule between groups of results.

ComboboxStatus.description: Async status — "Searching…", "12 of 340". Hidden while empty.

ComboboxTrigger.description:
The whole field as one trigger, for a value that can only come from the list — a
select-like combobox with no free text. Pair it with `ComboboxPopupInput`: Base UI drives
the list's keyboard cursor from an input. For a short list with no search, use `Select`.

ComboboxValue.description: The current selection, shown in a `ComboboxTrigger`.

CommandDialog.description:
The palette as an overlay, opened and closed through `open` and `onOpenChange`. The
caller binds the shortcut that opens it.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. Pair with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: The open state to start with, when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the next open state, whichever control or route changed it.

props.name: title
props.description: Shorthand for `strings.title`: the palette's accessible name.

props.name: description
props.description: Shorthand for `strings.description`.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this palette's own copy. All of it is hidden from view.

props.name: commandProps
props.description:
Configures the cmdk root the dialog owns: custom filtering, looping, labels, and other
command behaviour.

CommandEmpty.description: Shown when nothing matches. Not optional — a silent empty list reads as broken.

props.name: heading
props.description: Optional heading to render for this group.

CommandInput.description: The filter. Owns focus when the palette opens.

CommandItem.description: A row. Its `value` is what the filter matches; its label is what is read.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Event handler for when this item is selected, either via click or keyboard selection.

props.name: value
props.description:
A unique value for this item.
If no value is provided, it will be inferred from `children` or the rendered `textContent`. If your `textContent` changes between renders, you _must_ provide a stable, unique `value`.

CommandSeparator.description:
The rule between groups. Presentational and skipped by the keyboard, so arrowing through
results never lands on it.

CommandShortcut.description: The key hint at the end of a row.

members.name: title
members.description: Names the dialog (visually hidden; the search field is the visible cue).

members.name: description
members.description: Describes it to assistive technology, also hidden.

members.name: url
members.description: Absent while uploading — there is nothing to link to yet.

members.name: progress
members.description: 0–100 while in flight.

members.name: error
members.description: Why the upload failed, as the consumer's message. Kit-side rejections use `CommentAttachmentRejection` codes.

CommentAttachmentChip.description:
One file, in four states: staged, uploading, failed and posted. One row for all four,
because a failed upload that looks different from a staged one is a row the reader has to
learn twice — and finishing an upload never reflows.

props.name: editable
props.description: Reveals the remove control.

CommentContent.description:
A comment's body in whichever format it was stored — plain `text`, sanitised `html`, or a
read-only `rich` block document. Three of them, because a comments table outlives any one
editor and the rows written last year still have to render.

props.name: sanitizer
props.description: Replaces the kit's allow-list. There is no way to skip sanitising.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this component's own copy — the quote attribution.

members.name: status
members.description: A moderation or workflow state, shown beside the timestamp.

members.name: canDelete
members.description: Per-comment permission override. `undefined` defers to the thread's `canModerate`; `false` refuses regardless.

members.name: attachments
members.description: `null` entries survive a sparse array from an API and are skipped.

members.name: references
members.description: The mentions in the body, stored beside it. See features/mentions.

members.name: replyToId
members.description: Threading. The id of the comment this replies to.

CommentItem.description:
One comment and the controls that act on it: the author, time and message in a bubble,
reactions and Reply under it, everything else in the overflow menu beside it. Its replies
hang off a rail from its avatar, so who answered whom is a line to follow rather than an
indent to infer.

props.name: replies
props.description: Replies to this comment, when the thread is nested.

props.name: onAttachmentRemove
props.description: Supplying it reveals the remove control on each attachment.

props.name: getStatusLabel
props.description: Turns `comment.status` into something a reader recognises.

props.name: commentActions
props.description:
Extra entries for each comment's overflow menu — copy a link, report, resolve. Bound to the
comment like a table row's actions: `visible` and `disabled` may be predicates, and
`onClick` receives the comment. They sit after pin and edit, before delete; a
`destructive` entry still sorts last.

props.name: maxVisibleReplies
props.description:
Replies an open thread shows; the earlier ones fold behind "Show N earlier replies". The
LAST ones are kept, so list replies oldest first. `0` shows them all.

props.name: clampLines
props.description: Lines of a long body shown before "See more" (measured, so short bodies get no control). `0` never clamps.

props.name: maxVisibleAttachments
props.description:
Attachments shown before the rest fold behind "Show N more". Folding one file saves
nothing, so the fold starts at two hidden. `0` shows every file.

props.name: reactionChoices
props.description:
The reactions "Add reaction" offers. One reacts at once; more open a picker that marks the
reader's own. Every choice arrives through `onReact`.

props.name: renderAttachment
props.description: Replaces an attachment's chip.

props.name: renderReference
props.description: Overrides the mention registry's own `renderChip`.

members.name: emoji
members.description: An emoji or a short token.

members.name: mine
members.description: Whether the viewer is one of them.

members.name: users
members.description: Names behind the count, for the tooltip.

CommentSubmitHelpers.description: Handed to `onSubmit` so the consumer drives the composer from their own result (a resolved promise may still carry errors).

CommentableContext.description: What the comment is attached to.

members.name: moduleKey
members.description: A discriminator for an app that threads several kinds against one record.

Comments.description:
The composer and the timeline, wired together. A control appears only when its callback is
supplied (`onDelete`, `onUpdate`, …); `canComment`, `canModerate` and `allowReplies` cover
viewer permission and thread shape.

props.name: context
props.description:
What the thread hangs off: an `id` and a `type`, and a `moduleKey` where one record carries
several threads. Passed straight through to `onSubmit`. Changing it clears the draft — a
composer that stays mounted must not carry one record's text to the next.

props.name: comments
props.description:
Flat, in display order. Replies nest by `replyToId`, not by position, so one posted an hour
late still appears under its parent. A reply whose parent is not in the array is promoted
rather than dropped.

props.name: composerPosition
props.description:
Where the composer sits — a real per-thread decision: an activity log reads newest-first
and a discussion reads like a chat, and the same page can want both. Replies and edits open
inside the thread either way.

props.name: bare
props.description: Drops the card chrome, for a thread already inside a panel.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading. `false` hides it outright.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description:
Posts a comment or a reply. `helpers.reset()` is what clears the composer — a resolved
promise is not proof of success, and a server answering validation with a 200 would
otherwise throw away what the writer typed.

props.name: onDelete
props.description: Deletes a comment, after a confirmation unless `confirmDelete` is off.

props.name: confirmDelete
props.description:
Asks before deleting. The confirmation is opt-out because deleting takes the replies with
it; turn it off when the app already asks upstream.

props.name: onUpdate
props.description: Saves an edit. As with `onSubmit`, `helpers.reset()` is what clears the composer.

props.name: resources
props.description:
The mention registry, as `useMentions` takes it. Without it the reference control does not
appear.

props.name: onResourceSearch
props.description:
The fallback search, for a mention kind that registers neither `search` nor
`suggestions`.

props.name: attachments
avatarComponent
props.description: Replaces the generated avatar — for an app whose authors have presence or a badge.

`onClick` receives the comment. They sit after pin and edit, before delete; a
`destructive` entry still sorts last.

props.name: maxVisibleAttachments

Attachments shown before the rest fold behind "Show N more". Folding one file saves
nothing, so the fold starts at two hidden. `0` shows every file.

props.name: reactionChoices

The reactions "Add reaction" offers. One reacts at once; more open a picker that marks the
reader's own. Every choice arrives through `onReact`.

props.name: renderItem

Replaces a comment. It receives `defaultItem`, so a consumer can wrap the kit's comment
rather than rebuild it.

props.name: renderAttachment

props.name: renderReference
props.description: Overrides the mention registry's own `renderChip`.

The uploader; without it the attachment control does not appear. Must resolve to a

members.name: maxSize
members.description: In bytes.

members.name: accept

members.name: composerSave

members.name: formatReplyingEyebrow

members.name: replyPlaceholder

members.name: editPlaceholder

members.name: composerReply
members.description: The submit label under a reply — "Post reply", so it is not a second "Reply" button.

members.name: actionsLabel

members.name: formatShowReplies
members.description: Takes the count, because a plural is a language's business.

members.name: formatShowEarlierReplies

members.name: formatRepliesLabel

members.name: seeMoreLabel

members.name: formatShowMoreAttachments

members.name: formatTooLarge

members.name: reactionPickerLabel
members.description: Names the picker that opens when more than one reaction is offered.

Container.description: The single owner of centred content width and the inline gutter.

props.name: gutter

The heading. Either it or `description` renders the header; neither, and the block is a
bare surface.

props.name: description

props.description: Leading glyph on the title line.

Outer chrome. What separates `bordered` from `card` is the ground: a bordered block is a

ContextAction.description:
An action bound to a subject — a table row, a board card, an activity, a record. An
`ActionDefinition` whose handler and predicates take the subject; table, board and
activity actions extend it, and `resolveContextActions` resolves them.

members.name: onClick

members.description: `false`, or a predicate returning false, omits the action for that subject.

`inline` stays a button whatever `max` is, `menu` always overflows, and `auto` fills
the buttons in order up to `max`.

members.name: id

members.name: label
members.description:
What the entry says. The only part of the row that gives way: a long label truncates
instead of pushing the shortcut or trailing content off.

members.name: type
members.description: `checkbox` renders a toggle driven by `checked` / `onCheckedChange`.

members.name: href

Renders the entry as a link. A native `<a href>` by default, which is a full page
navigation — pass `renderLink` to route it through the app's router instead.

members.name: description

members.name: shortcut

members.name: trailing

rules off without a heading (e.g. to set apart a sign-out or delete).

members.name: render

The dropdown's menu opened by right-click over a region, reusing its rows. The trigger is
not a button — the whole area is the target. Every entry must also be reachable another
way (a toolbar, an `ActionMenu`): right-click is undiscoverable, absent on touch and
awkward from a keyboard.

ContextMenuCheckboxItem.description: A row that toggles rather than closing.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading glyph. Aligns to the first line when a description is present.

props.name: description

The dropdown's row, unchanged: `icon`, `description`, `shortcut`, `trailing` and
`variant="destructive"` all apply.

props.name: inset

props.name: variant

ContextMenuLabel.description:
A group's caption. It must sit inside a group — Base UI throws otherwise — and is not an
item: arrow keys skip it.

ContextMenuPortal.description: The portal, for a caller placing the surface itself. The content portals already.

ContextMenuRadioGroup.description: A set of rows that behaves as one choice.

props.name: value
props.description: The controlled value of the radio item that should be currently selected.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Function called when the selected value changes.

ContextMenuRadioItem.description: One choice inside a `ContextMenuRadioGroup`; it toggles rather than closing.

props.name: inset

ContextMenuShortcut.description:
The key hint on an item's trailing edge. Presentational: the item already carries the
accessible name.

A nested menu, opening sideways. It holds the open state, so trigger and panel cannot

props.name: latitude
props.description:
Signed decimal degrees. Either one missing renders the empty label — half a coordinate
locates nothing.

props.name: longitude
props.description:
Signed decimal degrees. Either one missing renders the empty label — half a coordinate
locates nothing.

props.name: format
props.description:
`decimal` is `48.85837, 2.29448`: what an API round-trips and what a reader pastes into
a map. `dms` is `48°51'30.1"N 2°17'40.1"E`, still what marine, aviation and survey
users read.

props.name: precision
props.description: Decimal places in `decimal` form. Five is about a metre, three about a building.

props.name: showHemisphere
props.description:
Adds hemisphere letters (N/S/E/W) to the decimal form: "48.85837°N, 2.29448°E". Off by
default because a signed pair is the portable form, the one that pastes into a map.
`dms` always shows them — an unsigned DMS value is ambiguous.

props.name: strings
props.description: The four hemisphere letters.

CoordinatesInput.description: A latitude and a longitude as one field, each with its own bounds.

props.name: id
props.description:
Applied to the first numeric input, which a `FormField` label addresses; each input
keeps its own `aria-label` for its part.

props.name: value
props.description:
`{ latitude, longitude }`: two strings, kept apart so a half-typed latitude cannot
corrupt the longitude.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the whole value when either part changes.

props.name: decimalPlaces
props.description: Six places is roughly 0.1 m — past the precision of consumer GPS.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this field's own copy — the two axis names. Like every other piece of copy,
each string can be overridden on its own.

props.name: invalid
props.description: The error surface. The message stays on the `FormField`.

props.name: value
props.description: What lands on the clipboard.

props.name: displayValue
props.description:
Shown instead of the raw value, when it differs from what is copied. A rich node is
rendered as-is.

props.name: mono
props.description:
Monospaced, tabular figures for the display content — for an id, a key or a hash, where
one character matters.

props.name: truncate
props.description: Truncates the display content at the width the caller allots, keeping the button in view.

props.name: compact
props.description:
Sizes the trigger to the text rather than to a control's height. A control's height is
right beside a field and wrong inside a list row where the value is a description under
a title: there the button is twice the height of the line it belongs to, and the row's
rhythm bends around it. Every behaviour is unchanged, and the target keeps its minimum
hit area; what it gives up is the pointer target a standalone control is entitled to.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this control's own copy. The name changes between `copy` and `copied`, because
the confirmation is the name for a screen reader.

props.name: silent
props.description: Suppresses both toasts. The copied state on the control is the confirmation then.

props.name: buttonProps
props.description: Passed to the copy control, for a tone or a treatment that suits the surface.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Called with the value once it is on the clipboard.

props.name: onError
props.description:
Called when the clipboard refuses — an insecure origin, a denied permission. A copy that
fails silently is worse than one that never offered.

members.name: copy
members.description: Accessible name for the control before it has been used.

members.name: copied
members.description: Accessible name while the copied state is showing. The name IS the state here.

members.name: success
members.description: Toast raised on success. The component's `silent` prop suppresses toasts.

members.name: error
members.description: Toast raised when the clipboard write is refused — no permission, no secure context.

members.name: name
members.description: What the key is for — "Production", "CI".

members.name: value
members.description: Written to the clipboard.

members.name: displayValue
members.description: Drawn in the row. Pass a masked form when the secret must not be on screen.

props.name: items
props.description: id, name, value, and `displayValue` for the masked form shown in the row.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Uncontrolled.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled.

props.name: onAdd
props.description: Omit to hide the add action.

props.name: onDelete
props.description: Omit to hide the delete action. The delete confirmation belongs to the caller.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Fires after the value reaches the clipboard — for analytics.

CredentialListStrings.description: Copy owned by the admin blocks. Counts are functions, so a translation controls pluralisation.

members.name: label
members.description: What the crumb reads as.

members.name: href

A router link element, so the library never imports a router. It replaces the plain

CurrencyCell.description:
An amount through Money. One of the cells every admin table has, so a page does not rewrite it
per column: a thin arrangement over the kit's primitives that adds the cell's part — the
alignment, the truncation, the empty case.

CurrencyInput.description:
An amount and its currency in separate channels: "€1,234.50" in one string would need a
locale-dependent parse downstream. The amount is `value`, a string — read
`event.target.value` in `onChange`; the currency code travels through `currency` and
`onCurrencyChange`.

props.name: currency
props.description: Controlled currency code, e.g. "EUR".

props.name: defaultCurrency
props.description: The starting currency code, for an uncontrolled field.

props.name: onCurrencyChange
props.description: Called with the new currency code: a separate channel from the amount.

props.name: currencies
props.description:
Which codes the picker offers. Codes are looked up in `CURRENCY_SYMBOLS`; anything else
takes a full option.

props.name: currencyPosition
props.description: Which side the selector sits on.

props.name: disableCurrencySelector
props.description: Drops the currency selector, for an amount whose currency is decided elsewhere in the form.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this field's own copy. It extends the decimal strings, which extend the input
strings — a currency field is one of each, so it owns the selector's name, the two
steppers, and the clear action alike.

props.name: invalid
props.description: The error surface. The message stays on the `FormField`.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Glyph before the value, in its own lane so the text never runs under it.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Glyph after the value, in its own lane so the text never runs under it.

props.name: startAddon
props.description:
Short text attached before the value, outside the text itself — a currency symbol, a
protocol, an at sign.

props.name: endAddon
props.description: Short text attached after the value, outside the text itself — a unit, a domain.

props.name: showCharacterCount
props.description: Shows "12 / 80" in the trailing lane. Requires `maxLength`.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Character cap, and the limit the count counts against. Input past it is refused.

props.name: clearable
props.description:
Shows a clear control once the field has a value. Clearing goes through the native
value setter, so React's value tracker stays in sync.

props.name: onClear
props.description: Called after the clear control empties the field.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Replaces the trailing affordance with a spinner, which outranks every other trailing
affordance.

props.name: returnValueWithAddons
props.description:
Includes string addons in the value reported by `onChange`. Off, because an addon is
presentation: a caller that stores "$" and the number has to strip it again on the way
out.

props.name: decimalPlaces
props.description: How many digits after the separator are accepted, and used when normalising.

props.name: min
props.description: The lower bound.

props.name: max
props.description: The upper bound.

props.name: allowNegative
props.description: Accepts a minus sign.

props.name: allowEmpty
props.description: Lets the field be left blank: a blank is a valid value.

props.name: step
props.description: The increment: renders − / + buttons that snap the value to multiples of this.

props.name: roundingMode
props.description:
How halves are resolved when stepping or normalising. `half-even` (bankers' rounding)
avoids accumulating bias across many money rows.

props.name: normalizeOnBlur
props.description:
Rounds, pads to the full decimal places and clamps to the range when focus leaves.
Doing it per keystroke would fight the reader mid-number.

props.name: endAdornment
props.description:
A unit rendered after the field, inside the stepper group — wrapping a stepped field in
a second shell would double the border.

CurrencyInputStrings.description: Extends the decimal strings, because a currency field IS one, with a selector added.

members.name: currency
members.description: Names the selector that changes what the number beside it MEANS.

members.name: decrement
members.description: The steppers are icon-only, so these are the only names they have.

members.name: clear
members.description: Accessible name for the inline clear action.

members.name: characterCount
members.description: Accessible description of the character counter, e.g. "12 of 80 characters".

props.name: surface
props.description:
The wrapper's chrome. `card` is the ordinary treatment; `glass` is a hairline outline for a
table inside another card, where two card surfaces are a box in a box; `flat` draws nothing.

props.name: headerTransparent
props.description: Drops the header row's muted fill.

props.name: columns
props.description:
Ordinary TanStack column definitions, or a `[columns, deps]` tuple memoised here, because
an array rebuilt every render resets column state on every keystroke elsewhere on the page.

props.name: data
props.description: The page to render. The table never slices it.

props.name: enableSorting
props.description: Turns on sorting: the header control AND the state behind it.

props.name: enableFiltering
props.description: Turns on the toolbar's filter AND the state behind it. Requires `filterColumn`.

props.description:

cannot exist with selection switched off.

Pins the header row. A pinned pane needs a bounded container to be pinned inside — sticky

props.description:
Pins the first column — and the selection checkbox before it, when there is one — while

selected rows and a `clearSelection`.

props.name: bulkActions
props.description:
The actions inside the default selection bar, or a function of the same context — the
selected rows and a `clearSelection` — that returns them.

props.name: rowActions
props.description:
Each row's actions, or a factory of them. The factory form is what a real table needs:
“Delete” belongs on a cancelled booking and nowhere else. `href` is carried as data — the
table never navigates.

props.name: rowActionsDisplayMode
props.description:
How row actions render: a menu, inline buttons, or `auto`. `auto` measures the TABLE, not
the window: whether three buttons fit is a question about the table, and the same one is
as often in a drawer as at page width.

props.name: pageCount
props.description:

props.name: page
props.description: The current page, from 1.

props.name: onPageChange
props.description: Receives the page the pager moves to.

props.name: totalRowCount
props.description: The result-count line beside the pager.

Persists column visibility to localStorage under `dt.{storageKey}.columns`. An explicit
`defaultColumnVisibility` still wins over the persisted value: a developer who hides a
column in code means it.

Row actions as a menu, as buttons, or whichever fits. `auto` measures the CONTAINER, not the
window: whether three buttons fit in an actions column is a question about that column.

The table's own controls — scroll arrows, the columns menu, full screen — in one bordered group.

The filter bar and the table as one surface: filter state, row filtering, the bar inside the
table's topbar, and pagination, all against one row set.

import whichever reads better at the call site.
