props.description:
A date-fns pattern, when the default is not what this column needs. `DatePrimitive`
falls back to the scope's `dates.format`, `Time` to its `dates.timeFormat`, and
`DateTime` to the two joined.

DateBlock.description:
A date as a calendar leaf, rendered as `<time>` with a machine-readable `dateTime`, so the
stacked fragments stay one parseable value.

props.name: date
props.description:
A Date, an ISO string, or a timestamp. Nothing parseable renders nothing — an empty leaf
would be a claim.

props.name: time
props.description:
An already-formatted time or range — "09:00 – 10:30" — under the weekday in the stacked
layout.

props.name: dateTime
props.description: Overrides the machine-readable value, which is otherwise the date's ISO string.

props.name: layout
props.description: A calendar leaf, or a phrase at the size of the line it sits in.

props.name: boxed
props.description:
The leaf's box and month band: a bounded surface. Defaults on for stacked and off for
inline; turn it off for a surface that already frames the leaf.

props.name: showWeekday
props.description: Shows the weekday.

props.name: showMonth
props.description: Shows the month. Without it there is no band.

props.name: showYear
props.description: Adds the year under the month, for a date outside the current one.

props.name: weekdayFormat
props.description:
date-fns pattern for the weekday. Names come from the `UIProvider`'s date-fns locale, so
these are patterns, not strings: a Greek scope reads "Κυρ" without a strings object.

props.name: dayFormat
props.description: date-fns pattern for the day.

props.name: monthFormat
props.description: date-fns pattern for the month, named in the scope's locale.

props.name: yearFormat
props.description: date-fns pattern for the year.

DateCell.description:
A date, in the scope's pattern unless `pattern` says otherwise. One of the cells every admin
table has, so a page does not rewrite it per column: a thin arrangement over the kit's
primitives that adds the cell's part — the alignment, the truncation, the empty case.

props.name: pattern
props.description: date-fns pattern. Falls back to the scope's own.

DateFilterEditor.description:
The editor for a `date` filter: one date, or a range for `between`. A date commits as it is
picked.

props.name: triggerSource
props.description: Only a toolbar-opened editor has a list to go back to.

DateMetaCell.description:
A date with a second line under it, given or derived from the parsed date. One of the cells
every admin table has, so a page does not rewrite it per column: a thin arrangement over the
kit's primitives that adds the cell's part — the alignment, the truncation, the empty case.

props.name: secondary
props.description: A second line under the date. A function derives it from the parsed date.

props.name: pattern
props.description: date-fns pattern. Falls back to the scope's own.

props.name: ref
props.description: The trigger button — the element a caller would focus or measure.

props.name: id
props.description:
Applied to the trigger, the only labelable element. Its name comes from the chosen date,
so the field's label must reach it.

props.name: mode
props.description: What a click selects: one date, a range, or several dates.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen value. Its shape follows `mode`: a `Date`, a `{ from, to }`, or an array.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the new value, in the shape `mode` gives it.

props.name: displayFormat
props.description: How the chosen value is written in the trigger: a date-fns pattern. The popup is unaffected.

props.name: invalid
props.description: The error surface. The message stays on the `FormField`.

props.name: clearable
props.description:
Adds a clear control to the trigger once something is chosen: a real button beside the
calendar glyph, named through `strings` — not an icon with a click handler.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this picker's own copy — the clear control and the calendar's captions. The
same object reaches the calendar inside the popup, so one override names the month
controls too.

props.name: presets
props.description:
Shortcuts down the side — "Last 30 days", "This month": the rail beside a range
calendar. `createRangePresets({ strings, weekStartsOn })` builds the built-in set in your
language and week.

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description:
How many months are shown side by side: two for a range, one otherwise. The header
becomes a range when more than one.

props.name: closeOnSelect
props.description:
Closes the popup as soon as a complete value is chosen. On by default for a single date
and off for a range, because a range is not chosen until both ends are.

props.name: header
props.description: A band above the calendar — a title, a mode switch. Use `DatePickerHeader`.

props.name: footer
props.description: A band below it — a summary, Clear and Apply. Use `DatePickerFooter`.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Styles the popup surface. `className` stays on the trigger.

props.name: minDate
props.description: Earliest selectable day, inclusive.

props.name: maxDate
props.description: Latest selectable day, inclusive.

props.name: disabledDates
props.description: Refuses individual days — weekends, holidays, days already booked.

DatePickerFooter.description:
The region below the calendar inside the popup, for the picker's `footer` slot: the row
that holds a summary and controls such as Clear and Apply. Exported so a caller can supply
their own without rebuilding the calendar.

props.name: summary
props.description: A summary of what is chosen — "3 – 7 March, 5 days".

props.name: actions
props.description: Controls at the trailing edge.

DatePickerHeader.description:
The region above the calendar inside the popup, for the picker's `header` slot — a title,
a mode switch. Exported so a caller can supply their own without rebuilding the calendar.

props.name: description
props.description: A second line — the range's length, the constraint in force.

props.name: action
props.description: A control at the trailing edge — a mode switch, a clear.

members.name: clear
members.description: Accessible name for the control that empties the field.

members.name: placeholder
members.description: Shown in the trigger while there is no date.

members.name: dateCount
members.description:
The trigger's text once more than two dates are chosen. Optional so older complete
strings objects still type-check.

members.name: chooseMonth
members.description: Describes what the caption button does (switch to the month grid); the month is its name.

members.name: value
members.description: Returns the value the preset selects, in whatever shape the mode uses.

DatePrimitive.description:
A date in the scope's pattern. Also exported as `Date`, its natural name: `DatePrimitive`
exists because `Date` collides with the global in a file that also constructs one, so
import whichever reads better at the call site.

props.name: value
props.description:
The moment to show: whatever the API returned — a Date, an ISO string or an epoch
number. Parsed once, here.

props.name: pattern
props.description:
A date-fns pattern, when the default is not what this column needs. `DatePrimitive`
falls back to the scope's `dates.format`, `Time` to its `dates.timeFormat`, and
`DateTime` to the two joined.

props.name: start
props.description:
Where the range begins. Either end may be absent — an open range is a real state, not
an error.

props.name: end
props.description:
Where the range ends. Either end may be absent — an open range is a real state, not an
error.

props.name: pattern
props.description:
A date-fns pattern for both ends, when the collapsing is not wanted: only the default
drops a repeated month.

props.name: separator
props.description: Between the two ends. An en dash by default.

DateTime.description:
The same value as a date and a time. Three components rather than a granularity prop,
because a column shows one of them and never switches.

props.name: value
props.description:
The moment to show: whatever the API returned — a Date, an ISO string or an epoch
number. Parsed once, here.

props.name: pattern
props.description:
A date-fns pattern, when the default is not what this column needs. `DatePrimitive`
falls back to the scope's `dates.format`, `Time` to its `dates.timeFormat`, and
`DateTime` to the two joined.

DateTimeInput.description:
A date and a time in one field: a date picker and time segments editing one value, stored
as an ISO string.

props.name: id
props.description: Applied to the date trigger, so a `FormField` label can address this pair.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value, as an ISO string.

props.name: minuteStep
props.description: Minutes snap to this in the time segments.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: `FormField` supplies these; the date trigger and each time segment carry them.

DatesConfig.description:
`UIConfig`'s `dates` slice: the week start, the fallback patterns, the date-fns locale and
the relative-time wording.

members.name: weekStartsOn
members.description: First day of the week in calendars and pickers. 0 = Sunday.

members.name: format
members.description: date-fns pattern the date primitives fall back to.

members.name: timeFormat
members.description: date-fns pattern for a time of day. `"p"` uses the locale's own convention.

members.name: locale
members.description:
The date-fns Locale OBJECT — what actually translates month and weekday names, and the
built-in relative-time wording. It cannot be derived from a BCP-47 tag such as
`formatting.locale`: the locales are modules, and importing all of them to look one up
would put every language in every bundle, so the consumer imports the one it needs.

members.name: formatRelativeTime
members.description: Replaces the relative-time wording ("7 days ago", "in 2 hours").

DecimalInput.description:
The numeric field this family builds on: a text input, not `type="number"`, whose spinner
is unstyleable, whose wheel changes values, and whose invalid input reads back as "". The
`value` is always a plain string, never a number: read `event.target.value` in `onChange`.

props.name: decimalPlaces
props.description: How many digits after the separator are accepted, and used when normalising.

props.name: min
props.description: The lower bound.

props.name: max
props.description: The upper bound.

props.name: allowNegative
props.description: Accepts a minus sign.

props.name: allowEmpty
props.description: Lets the field be left blank: a blank is a valid value.

props.name: step
props.description: The increment: renders − / + buttons that snap the value to multiples of this.

props.name: roundingMode
props.description:
How halves are resolved when stepping or normalising. `half-even` (bankers' rounding)
avoids accumulating bias across many money rows.

props.name: normalizeOnBlur
props.description:
Rounds, pads to the full decimal places and clamps to the range when focus leaves.
Doing it per keystroke would fight the reader mid-number.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this field's own copy — the two icon-only steppers, plus everything `Input` contributes.

props.name: endAdornment
props.description:
A unit rendered after the field, inside the stepper group — wrapping a stepped field in
a second shell would double the border.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Glyph before the value, in its own lane so the text never runs under it.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Glyph after the value, in its own lane so the text never runs under it.

props.name: startAddon
props.description:
Short text attached before the value, outside the text itself — a currency symbol, a
protocol, an at sign.

props.name: endAddon
props.description: Short text attached after the value, outside the text itself — a unit, a domain.

props.name: showCharacterCount
props.description: Shows "12 / 80" in the trailing lane. Requires `maxLength`.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Character cap, and the limit the count counts against. Input past it is refused.

props.name: clearable
props.description:
Shows a clear control once the field has a value. Clearing goes through the native
value setter, so React's value tracker stays in sync.

props.name: onClear
props.description: Called after the clear control empties the field.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Replaces the trailing affordance with a spinner, which outranks every other trailing
affordance.

props.name: invalid
props.description:
Applies the invalid treatment. Pair it with FormField's error for the message, so the
border and the announcement cannot disagree.

props.name: returnValueWithAddons
props.description:
Includes string addons in the value reported by `onChange`. Off, because an addon is
presentation: a caller that stores "$" and the number has to strip it again on the way
out.

members.name: decrement
members.description: The steppers are icon-only, so these are the only names they have.

members.name: clear
members.description: Accessible name for the inline clear action.

members.name: characterCount
members.description: Accessible description of the character counter, e.g. "12 of 80 characters".

DefaultDialogContent.description:
The picker the assignment dialog shows when a consumer supplies none — the dialog body when
not replaced. Exported so a custom dialog can keep it and add to it, rather than starting
from nothing.

DefaultDialogSummary.description:
What is about to be committed, restated above the confirm. A picker can scroll, and the
chosen row is often out of sight by the time the reader reaches the button. Falls back to a
`label` field; pass `getSelectionLabel` to be exact.

DialogContent.description:
OverlayContent with `placement` fixed to centre, and that is the whole of the dialog.
`modality`, `surface`, `dismissal`, `initialFocusRef` and `showCloseButton` are
OverlayContent's props, with the same defaults.

The rest of a dialog is Overlay's own parts, imported from `base/overlay` under their own
names. There is no second name for them, so nothing about them can drift.

props.name: size
length
props.description:
Along-axis extent, for an edge placement. Less than full detaches the panel and centres
it on that axis. It is measured against the space the inset leaves rather than the
viewport: 70% of an inset panel is 70% of what is between the offsets, and the rest is
split between the two ends. Full needs no inset to look right, which is why a
corner-anchored sheet sets only `inset`.

props.name: inset
props.description:
The gap to the viewport edges. `false` is flush — a sheet welded to the side; `true`
uses the kit's gap; any CSS length sets your own. One offset, spent on every side the
panel does not run to, so an inset side panel sits the same distance from the top, the
side and the bottom. Any gap detaches it, rounds all four corners and gives it a full
border.

props.name: modality
props.description:
How much of the page the surface takes hostage: scrim, inert background and scroll
lock (`modal`), focus alone (`trap-focus`), or neither (`non-modal`).

props.name: surface
props.description: `bare` drops the region dividers, for content that draws its own chrome.

props.name: dismissal
props.description:
Each route out, separately. Off for a decision that must be answered, or for work in
progress. AlertDialogContent fixes both off.

props.name: initialFocusRef
props.description: Element to focus on open, instead of the first tabbable node.

props.name: showCloseButton
props.description: Renders the corner dismiss control. AlertDialogContent turns it off.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this surface's own copy — the corner dismiss control's name.

props.name: width
props.description: The first part. The parts stay separate numbers until the render joins them.

props.name: height
props.description: The second part.

props.name: depth
props.description: The third part, optional — two values render as a plane.

props.name: unit
props.description: Appended once, not per part.

props.name: separator
props.description: Between the parts. A multiplication sign, not the letter x.

DimensionsInput.description: Length, width and height as one field, with one unit for all three.

props.name: id
props.description:
Applied to the first numeric input, which a `FormField` label addresses; each input
keeps its own `aria-label` for its part.

props.name: value
props.description:
`{ length, width, height }`: three strings, one field. Each part is independently
editable.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the whole value when any part changes.

props.name: unit
props.description: Controlled unit. Switching unit does not convert — it relabels.

props.name: defaultUnit
props.description: The unit the field starts in.

props.name: onUnitChange
props.description: Called with the new unit. Switching relabels rather than converting — the number is the caller's.

props.name: units
props.description: Which units the selector offers.

props.name: decimalPlaces
props.description: Digits after the separator, applied to every part of the field.

props.name: showHeight
props.description:
Shows the third dimension box. Turn it off for a value that is a plane rather than a
solid: a two-dimensional measurement.

props.name: showUnitSelector
props.description: Shows the unit selector. Turn it off for a field with one fixed unit.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this field's own copy — the three axis names and the unit selector. Like every
other piece of copy, each string can be overridden on its own.

props.name: invalid
props.description: The error surface. The message stays on the `FormField`.

members.name: unit
members.description: Names the unit selector, which has no visible label of its own.

DirectionProvider.description:
Tells script-positioned UI — menus, popovers — the writing direction of a subtree. Set
`dir` on `<html>` or the region as well, so the browser handles selection, caret and
scroll, and the kit's logical CSS mirrors.

props.name: direction
props.description:
The reading direction for a subtree, as the menus, popovers and other script-positioned
parts inside it read it. The kit's CSS is logical and follows the `dir` attribute, so
set `dir` on the region as well for its layout to mirror.

DirtyStateBanner.description: Tells the reader there are unsaved changes, with the actions that resolve them.

props.name: actions
props.description: Save and discard, usually.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Deliberately narrower than `AlertTone`: unsaved work is neither an error nor a
success.

members.name: display
members.description:
Where the filter lives in the bar. `always` keeps a pill on screen with no value, for the
one or two filters a screen is really about. `collapsed` hides it behind the add button
until it has one. `hidden` still applies but never draws — which is how a screen scopes a
list to the current account.

members.name: priority
members.description:
Sort order in the bar: lower first. Ties keep the authored order, so pills do not
reshuffle as values come and go.

DocumentStackIllustration.description:
Two staggered documents — for invoices, reports, files. Drawn from the theme's own tokens
rather than shipped as an image, so an empty state cannot be the one thing on the page
that ignores a rebrand — and it costs no request.

DropdownMenu.description: A menu that opens from a trigger. It holds the open state the parts share.

DropdownMenuCheckboxItem.description: A row that toggles rather than closing.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading glyph. Aligns to the first line when a description is present.

props.name: description
props.description: Second line under the label. Wraps rather than truncating on one line.

props.name: inset
props.description: Indents a row with no icon, so its label lines up with rows that have one.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether the checkbox item is currently ticked.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Event handler called when the checkbox item is ticked or unticked.

DropdownMenuContent.description:
The menu's surface. It sizes to its widest row by default, capped at a reading measure;
`width`, `minWidth` and `maxWidth` change that.

props.name: width
props.description:
Fixed surface width: any CSS length, or `"trigger"` to match the trigger (Select-like).
Unset, the menu sizes to its widest row, capped by `maxWidth`.

props.name: minWidth
props.description: Floor for the content-sized default.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description:
Ceiling for the content-sized default: a reading measure, so one long label doesn't
widen every row. Unset, the surface also stops at the space available.

props.name: container
props.description:
Where the popup renders. Defaults to the nearest `UIPortalHost`, else the primitive's
own target.

props.name: align
props.description: How to align the popup relative to the specified side.

props.name: side
props.description:
Which side of the anchor element to align the popup against.
May automatically change to avoid collisions.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description:
Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the distance to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

props.name: alignOffset
props.description:
Additional offset along the alignment axis in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the offset to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

DropdownMenuItem.description:
A menu row. Its icon, description, shortcut and trailing content are props rather than
children, so every row lays out the same and only the label gives way.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading glyph. Aligns to the first line when a description is present.

props.name: description
props.description: Second line under the label. Wraps rather than truncating on one line.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: Trailing content — a keyboard shortcut, a badge, a count.

props.name: trailing
props.description: Trailing content beside the shortcut, for anything that is not a shortcut.

props.name: inset
props.description: Indents a row with no icon, so its label lines up with rows that have one.

props.name: variant
props.description: `destructive` marks a row that deletes or discards.

DropdownMenuLabel.description:
A group caption. It must sit inside a `DropdownMenuGroup` — it throws otherwise. The label
is not an item: it is not focusable and arrow keys skip it, which is why a styled item
would be wrong here.

DropdownMenuLinkItem.description:
An item that navigates. A real anchor, so middle-click and copy-link work and a screen
reader announces a link rather than a button.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading glyph. Aligns to the first line when a description is present.

props.name: description
props.description: Second line under the label. Wraps rather than truncating on one line.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: Trailing content — a keyboard shortcut, a badge, a count.

props.name: trailing
props.description: Trailing content beside the shortcut, for anything that is not a shortcut.

props.name: inset
props.description: Indents a row with no icon, so its label lines up with rows that have one.

props.name: variant
props.description: `destructive` marks a row that deletes or discards.

DropdownMenuPortal.description:
Escapes the menu from an ancestor that clips or transforms — a card with overflow hidden,
a scrolling pane. `DropdownMenuContent` portals already; this is for a caller placing the
surface itself.

DropdownMenuRadioGroup.description: One choice from the menu: a set of `DropdownMenuRadioItem`s.

props.name: value
props.description: The controlled value of the radio item that should be currently selected.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Function called when the selected value changes.

DropdownMenuRadioItem.description: A single-choice item inside a `DropdownMenuRadioGroup`, carrying its own indicator.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading glyph. Aligns to the first line when a description is present.

props.name: description
props.description: Second line under the label. Wraps rather than truncating on one line.

props.name: inset
props.description: Indents a row with no icon, so its label lines up with rows that have one.

DropdownMenuSeparator.description: The rule between runs of items.

DropdownMenuShortcut.description:
The key hint on the trailing edge of an item. Presentational: it announces nothing,
because the shortcut is already on the item that owns it.

DropdownMenuSub.description:
A nested menu: `DropdownMenuSubTrigger`, then `DropdownMenuSubContent`. It holds the open
state both belong to.

DropdownMenuSubContent.description: The panel a nested menu opens. It belongs to a `DropdownMenuSub`, which holds the open state.

props.name: width
props.description:
Fixed surface width: any CSS length, or `"trigger"` to match the trigger (Select-like).
Unset, the menu sizes to its widest row, capped by `maxWidth`.

props.name: minWidth
props.description: Floor for the content-sized default.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description:
Ceiling for the content-sized default: a reading measure, so one long label doesn't
widen every row. Unset, the surface also stops at the space available.

props.name: container
props.description:
Where the popup renders. Defaults to the nearest `UIPortalHost`, else the primitive's
own target.

props.name: align
props.description: How to align the popup relative to the specified side.

props.name: side
props.description:
Which side of the anchor element to align the popup against.
May automatically change to avoid collisions.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description:
Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the distance to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

props.name: alignOffset
props.description:
Additional offset along the alignment axis in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the offset to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

DropdownMenuSubTrigger.description: The row that opens a nested menu. It belongs to a `DropdownMenuSub`, which holds the open state.

DropdownMenuTrigger.description: The control the menu hangs off.

props.name: render
props.description:
Allows you to replace the component's HTML element
with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

Dropzone.description:
The drop target on its own, for a surface that wants the drag behaviour without
FileUpload's list and validation around it. It reports dropped or picked files and owns
no state; the box is a `<label>` for a real file input, so it is keyboard-reachable and
submits in a plain form.

props.name: onDrop
props.description: Called with what was dropped or picked. Nothing is validated first.

props.name: accept
props.description: MIME types or extensions, as the native input takes them.

props.name: compact
props.description: A shorter box, for a zone beside other fields rather than filling a panel.

props.name: icon
props.description: Replaces the cloud glyph.

props.name: inputProps
props.description: Native attributes for the input itself — `name`, `form`, `required`.

props.name: label
props.description: Replaces the prompt — "Attach your receipts". Shorthand for `strings.instruction`.

props.name: hint
props.description: Replaces the second line — the accepted types, the size cap — with any node.

props.name: footer
props.description: Controls rendered below the label, not inside it, where clicks would open the file dialog.

members.name: instruction
members.description: The prompt, singular and plural (two keys, since plurals vary by language).

members.name: dragOver
members.description: Replaces the prompt while something is over the box.

members.name: helper
members.description: A second line under the prompt — the accepted types, the size cap.

props.name: value
props.description: The length. Seconds unless `from` says otherwise.

props.name: from
props.description: The unit the incoming value is in.

props.name: maxParts
props.description:
How many units to show before truncating. "2 hours 14 minutes 3 seconds" is rarely
useful — the reader wants the magnitude, and the tail is noise.

props.name: unitDisplay
props.description: How each unit is written.

props.name: text
props.description: The document as plain text.

props.name: value
props.description: The address. Becomes both the text and the `mailto:` href.

props.name: display
props.description:
Shown instead of the address — a person's name, for instance. The href is still the
address.

props.name: subject
props.description: Prefills the message's subject. Encoded into the `mailto:`, not concatenated into it.

props.name: body
props.description: Prefills the message's body. Encoded into the `mailto:`, not concatenated into it.

Empty.description:
What a surface shows when it has nothing to show, with an `action` slot for the next step.
`mediaVariant` dresses the media, and `padding` sizes it from a panel cell to a whole page.

props.name: media
props.description: Icon or illustration: the visual.

props.name: mediaVariant
props.description:
The media's chrome. `none` renders the media raw; `icon` and `icon-soft` set a glyph in
a tile; `illustration` centres it with room below.

props.name: renderMedia
props.description: Media as a function of the variant, for a visual that changes with its chrome.

props.name: title
props.description:
Names the absence: "No invoices yet", not "Nothing here". Falls back to `strings.title`,
so a bare `<Empty />` still renders during scaffolding.

props.name: description
props.description:
Why it is empty, or what will fill it. `false` hides it, for a title that already tells
the whole story.

props.name: action
props.description:
Buttons or links offering the next step. An empty state that only explains is a dead
end.

props.name: footer
props.description: Quiet copy under the action — a hint, a learn-more, a shortcut.

props.name: padding
props.description:
Breathing room, on both axes: `sm` for panels and cells, `lg` for a whole page. The
inline padding is what keeps copy off a dashed edge.

props.name: border
props.description:
The dashed outline. Off by default; use it when the empty state stands in for a card's
body and the edge says "something goes here".

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this state's own copy: `title`, `description`, and `ariaLabel`. The region
announces through `role="status"`, so a list that empties out while the reader is on the
page says so.

members.name: title
members.description: Fallback headline for a bare `<Empty />`; screens should pass their own ("No invoices yet").

members.name: ariaLabel
members.description: The region's accessible name; `Empty` is a `role="status"`, so a list emptying out is announced.

EmptyValue.description: The absent state on its own, for a slot that has nothing to show.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: Rendered when the value is absent.

props.name: truncate
props.description: Ellipsises the value at one line. Every flex box in the chain needs `min-width: 0` — see `Text`.

ErrorState.description: A whole region that has failed, announced at once.

props.name: onRetry
props.description:
Renders the retry control when set. With neither this nor `action`, the state reports
the failure without offering a dead button.

props.name: action
props.description: Replaces the retry control entirely.

ErrorSummary.description:
Collects what failed into one place at the top of a form. The count is in the heading
because it tells the reader how much there is to fix.

props.name: title
props.description: Replaces the heading, which otherwise counts the list.

props.name: description
props.description: Copy under the heading.

props.name: errors
props.description: The problems, one per item. An item may link to its field.

props.name: action
props.description: A control beside the summary — "Review the first problem".

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Moves focus to the summary when it has problems, and again whenever the count changes — what a failed submit wants. Items may be links to their fields (`Email is not valid.`).

EventCalendar.description:
A month grid, a week strip, or an agenda over one list of events. Views change only the day
range and layout; placing events onto days is shared.

props.name: events
props.description:
The calendar does no fetching of its own. An event with an `endDate` appears on every day
it spans, not only its first.

props.name: categories
props.description: The categories events name. Each owns its colour, so colour is defined once.

props.name: viewMode
props.description:
Controlled. The switcher works either way. Week steps by weeks; month and agenda step by
months.

props.name: defaultViewMode
props.description: Uncontrolled: the view to start in.

props.name: date
props.description: Where the calendar is looking. Controlled, like the view.

props.name: defaultDate
props.description: Uncontrolled: where the calendar starts looking.

props.name: onEventClick
props.description: A chip press calls this and stops there.

props.name: onDayClick
props.description: A press anywhere else in a day's cell calls this, with the day and everything on it.

props.name: maxEventsPerDay
props.description:
Chips drawn per day before the rest collapse into an overflow line. The overflow dots are
the categories of the HIDDEN events, not the first three in the list.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description:
0 is Sunday. Falls back to the provider's dates config, then Monday — the same source the
kit's own pickers read.

props.name: enableCategoryFilter
props.description: Makes the legend chips toggle their category.

props.name: visibleCategories
props.description:
Ids currently shown. An EMPTY list means all are shown — a filter nobody has touched hides
nothing.

props.name: actions
props.description: Rendered in the header, before the today and navigation controls.

props.name: minDate
props.description: Navigation stops here, and days beyond it are drawn but not clickable.

props.name: maxDate
props.description: Navigation stops here, and days beyond it are drawn but not clickable.

props.name: disabledDates
props.description:
Days drawn but not clickable. A `DateRule` takes dates, a predicate, or both, combined
with OR.

props.name: filterEvent
props.description:
Hides events at render time without touching `events`. Counts and the overflow line
follow it, so what is drawn and what is counted agree.

props.name: renderEvent
props.description: Replaces how an event draws: its chip in a day cell, its card in the agenda.

props.name: renderDayCell
props.description: Replaces a day's cell. It receives `defaultRender`, so decorating is as easy as replacing.

EventCalendarDayCell.description:
One day in the grid. Deliberately not a button: a cell holds events that are themselves
pressable, and nesting controls makes both unreachable by keyboard. The day number is the
keyboard affordance; the cell's click only widens the pointer target.

props.name: onEventClick
props.description: Fires instead of `onClick` when the press was on an event chip.

EventCalendarEventBadge.description:
One event as a chip in a day cell: a category dot, the title and the start time. At the
narrowest widths only the dot remains.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this chip's own copy — its accessible name.

EventCalendarEventCard.description:
One event in full, for an agenda row or a popover. The card reads its metadata by name —
`customerName`, `guestCount`, `serviceName` — so a consumer's own fields appear without a
mapping step.

members.name: eventAt
members.description: Names one event chip from its title and start time; one function so word order is translatable.

EventCalendarHeader.description:
The period and the controls that move it. The month jump is icon-only because the label
beside it already names the month — spelling it on the button too is the same word twice.

props.name: displayLabel
props.description: The formatted period — "March 2026", or a week's span.

EventCalendarLegend.description:
The category key, and the filter when one is wired. The WHOLE chip toggles rather than a
checkbox beside a swatch — the swatch is the target a reader aims at anyway.

props.name: visibleCategories
props.description: Empty means all are shown.

members.name: jumpToMonth
members.description: Names the month/year jump control, which draws no label of its own.

members.name: filterCategories
members.description: Names the legend when it filters, so a screen reader knows the chips do something.

members.name: moreEvents
members.description: The overflow line under a day's chips.

members.name: viewMode
members.type: { label: string; month: string; week: string; agenda: string; }

members.name: label
members.description: The accessible name of the view switcher itself, not of the current view.

members.name: weekdaysShort
members.type: [string, string, string, string, string, string, string]
members.description: Sunday first. The calendar rotates them to match `weekStartsOn`.

FieldBinding.description:
What a bound field hands to a control: what `useFormFieldBinding` returns, spreadable onto
the control.

members.name: invalid
members.description: Present so a control can render its invalid state without a separate lookup.

FieldGroup.description:
Several fields sharing one label and one supporting line — a date range, a name split in
two. A real `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`, so the legend is announced when focus enters the
group.

props.name: legend
props.description: The group's one label, announced when focus enters the group.

props.name: description
props.description: The group's one supporting line.

FieldShell.description:
The field surface on its own, for composing a control the kit does not ship. The shell
wears the surface and the control inside gives up its own, so an icon or a trailing
action reads as part of one field rather than a box inside a box.

props.name: start
props.description: Rendered before the control — an icon, a prefix, a currency symbol.

props.name: end
props.description: Rendered after the control — a unit, a clear button, a reveal toggle.

props.name: children
props.description: A direct control, or an explicit adapter for a wrapped/custom control.

FieldState.description:
One field's state, as an adapter reports it. Everything past `value` and `setValue` is
optional.

members.name: accept
members.description:
Native accept filter, e.g. `.pdf,image/*`. Enforced here as well as by the dialog, and
checked before `onValueChange` rather than after, like every constraint.

members.name: minSizeBytes
members.description: Smallest file accepted, in bytes.

members.name: maxSizeBytes
members.description: Largest file accepted, in bytes.

members.name: validateFile
members.description: Runs after the type and size checks.

FilePickerInput.description:
A file field shaped like an Input, showing the chosen file's name, for a form row. The
file input covers the whole control, so any part of it opens the dialog, and the `accept`
wiring and the re-validation come with it. `FileUpload` is the drop-zone alternative.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled.

props.name: constraints
props.description: Type and size limits. Re-checked here, not left to the file dialog.

FileRejection.description: One refused file: a code and numbers, which `FileUploadStrings` turns into a sentence.

FileRejectionDetails.description: The numbers behind a rejection, for the component to write copy from.

members.name: limitBytes
members.description: The bound that was exceeded, in bytes.

members.name: maxFiles
members.description: The file cap, for `too-many`.

members.name: customMessage
members.description: Only ever what a `FileValidator` returned. Nothing here is written by the kit.

props.name: value
props.description: The size. Bytes unless `from` says otherwise.

props.name: from
props.description:
The unit `value` is given in. Converted with the same base, so `from="megabytes"` means
2^20 under `binary` and 10^6 under `decimal`.

props.name: base
props.description:
Which base and which labels. `binary` divides by 1024 and labels it MB — the pairing
Windows and most file managers show, chosen so a size agrees with the machine it
describes rather than with SI. `decimal` is SI-correct and what Apple platforms and
storage vendors use. `iec` is strictly correct. The default does not move, so nothing
already shipped changes.

props.name: align
props.description:
For a size given a box of its own. A COLUMN of sizes is aligned by the column —
`<TableCell align="end">` — because the primitive is a span, and blockifying it to
align would break the text runs it also sits in.

members.name: from
members.description: The unit the incoming value is already in.

members.name: base
members.description: Which base and labels to use (see the note above). Default `binary`.

props.name: id
props.description: Applied to the file input itself, so a `FormField` label can address it.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen files, controlled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the next selection, after validation.

props.name: onRejectedFiles
props.description:
Receives the files that failed validation, each with a reason code. Rejected files never
reach `onValueChange`.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Accepts more than one file.

props.name: maxFiles
props.description: Cap on the selection. Defaults to 1 for single, unlimited for multiple.

props.name: selectionMode
props.description:
Whether a second drop adds to the set or replaces it. Defaults to `append` with
`multiple`, else `replace`.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Applies the invalid treatment to the zone. The message stays with FormField.

props.name: compact
props.description:
A single row rather than a panel, for a zone that sits inside a form rather than owning
a page.

props.name: label
props.description: Shorthand for `strings.instruction`.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this control's own copy, the rejection sentences included.

props.name: hint
props.description: The line under the zone: the constraint text a reader needs before they choose.

props.name: showList
props.description:
Shows the chosen files under the zone. Turn it off only when something else on the page
shows them — a caller rendering its own list.

props.name: showRejections
props.description:
Shows the refused files under the zone, each with its reason. Turn it off only when
something else on the page shows them.

props.name: progress
props.description: Per-file transfer progress, 0–100, keyed by file name.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: `FormField`'s wiring, applied to the input.

props.name: accept
props.description:
Native accept filter, e.g. `.pdf,image/*`. Enforced here as well as by the dialog, and
checked before `onValueChange` rather than after, like every constraint.

props.name: minSizeBytes
props.description: Smallest file accepted, in bytes.

props.name: maxSizeBytes
props.description: Largest file accepted, in bytes.

props.name: validateFile
props.description: Runs after the type and size checks.

members.name: instruction
members.description: The drop target's prompt, singular and plural (two keys, since plurals vary by language).

members.name: dragOver
members.description: Replaces the prompt while a file is over the zone. Falls back to Dropzone's own.

members.name: uploading
members.description: Announced while a transfer is in flight, named after the file.

members.name: remove
members.description: Names each row's remove control, after the file it removes.

members.name: rejection
members.description: One refused file as a sentence, from the whole rejection (file, code, bound).

members.name: constraintHint
members.description:
The hint built from the constraints when no `hint` is given ("image/* · up to 5 MB");
empty for none. Optional so older complete strings objects still type-check.

members.name: getOptions
members.description: Cached options for a `(filter, query)` key, or `undefined` when there are none.

members.name: setOptions
members.type: (key: string, options: FilterOption[], staleTime: number) => void
members.description: Remember a query's options and schedule their expiry `staleTime` ms from now.

members.name: deleteOptions
members.description: Forget one query's options — what `refetch` does before asking again.

members.name: getLabel
members.description: The option behind a value a pill is displaying, if this cache ever saw it.

members.name: rememberLabels
members.description: Remember the labels in a result set. Returns whether any were new, so callers can skip re-rendering pills.

members.name: clear
members.description: Drop everything and cancel every pending expiry.

members.name: pluralLabel
members.description: Used in "3 statuses selected". Falls back to `label`.

members.name: delay
members.description: Debounce for a `search` filter, in ms.

members.name: validation
members.description:
`min` / `max` / `pattern` / `required`, plus a `custom` returning true or a message.
`zodValidator` and `predicateValidator` bridge the two shapes you probably already have.

members.name: closeOnSelect
members.description: Closes the editor as soon as one option is picked. Single-select only.

members.name: asyncConfig
members.description:
Options for an `async_select`: one channel owning search, caching, abort, and preload —
rather than a `loading` prop and an `options` prop the consumer keeps in step by hand.

members.name: display
members.description: date-fns pattern for the pill.

members.name: param
members.description: date-fns pattern for the stored value — what the server sees.

members.name: format
members.description: Replaces the default rendering of the value in the pill.

FilterDependency.description: This filter only applies once another one has a value.

FilterEditor.description:
Dispatches on the filter's type to one of the five typed editors — SelectFilterEditor,
DateFilterEditor, RangeFilterEditor, TagsFilterEditor and AsyncFilterEditor — behind one
popover: the one place that knows which editor a type gets. Most editors STAGE their value
and commit it on Apply — a multi-select that committed on each tick would be one request per
tick; a date commits as it is picked.

props.name: triggerSource
props.description: Only a toolbar-opened editor has a list to go back to.

FilterErrorBoundary.description:
Keeps one broken filter from taking the page with it. A filter's editor is the most
consumer-owned surface in the feature — custom renders, fetched options, consumer value
shapes — so it is the one most likely to throw.

props.name: filterKey
props.description: Which filter this content edits. Names the filter in the message.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Replaces the default message entirely.

FilterLayout.description:
The default bar: saved tabs, search boxes, active pills, always-shown pills, the add button,
then Clear. For a custom bar, place the exported parts using `useFilterGroups()`.

props.name: dynamicFilterOptions
props.description: Options loaded by the parent, keyed by filter. Overrides `filter.options`.

props.name: loadingFilters
props.description: Per-filter pending state — a chip stands in while its options load.

props.name: mobilePresentation
props.description:
`sheet` uses an inset filter sheet and a saved-view select below 768px; search stays
inline. In the sheet an editor's Apply commits values, Back discards unapplied edits, and
Done closes it; `mobileFilters`, `filterSummary` and `done` in `strings` localize it. Opt
into `inline` controls for a custom mobile layout.

FilterOperator.description:
The comparisons, named rather than a bare union so a consumer writes `FilterOperator.IN` not
`"in"`, and exported as values so a filter definition can switch on them exhaustively.
FilterOperator.type: { readonly EQUALS: "equals"; readonly CONTAINS: "contains"; readonly IN: "in"; readonly NOT_IN: "not_in"; readonly NOT: "not"; readonly BEFORE: "before"; readonly AFTER: "after"; readonly BETWEEN: "between"; readonly GT: "gt"; readonly LT: "lt"; readonly GTE: "gte"; readonly LTE: "lte"; readonly HAS: "has"; readonly HAS_ANY: "has_any"; readonly HAS_ALL: "has_all"; }

FilterOperatorSelect.description:
The comparison segment of a pill. It renders as plain text when there is only one operator,
because a menu offering a single choice is a control that cannot be used and still costs a
chevron and a tab stop.

FilterOperatorStrings.description: Filter copy. Interpolated strings are functions, not templates, so translations can reorder parts.

FilterPill.description:
One applied filter, as three segments in a group rather than one button. “Status · is ·
Confirmed ✕” is three separate decisions with three separate targets, and a single button
makes two of them unreachable.

props.name: active
props.description: Whether the filter currently applies. Drives the clear segment.

FilterProvider.description:
The state every part of a filter bar reads: the filters on offer, the applied ones, and the
async option cache.

props.name: filters
props.description:
Every filter the surface offers. A filter's `type` decides its editor and which
comparisons it offers.

props.name: activeFilters
props.description: The applied filters. Controlled: the provider never writes to its own state.

props.name: onFilterChange
props.description: Receives every change to `activeFilters`, which the provider never makes itself.

props.name: navigating
props.description:
A change is in flight. Controls are disabled, open editors close, and an updating status
appears while the current results remain visible — the bar dims rather than pretending it
has applied.

props.name: onError
props.description: Receives fetch, validation, apply, and render failures.

props.name: cache
props.description:
The async option and label cache. Defaults to one per mounted provider; pass a
`createFilterCache()` instance to keep results and pill labels across navigation.

members.name: preserveUnrelated
members.description: Keeps query keys this does not own.

members.name: resetPageKeys
members.description: Dropped whenever the filters change — page 4 of the old result set is meaningless.

members.name: mobileFilters
members.description: Mobile filter sheet copy. Optional for existing complete translations.

members.name: edit
members.description: Names the pill's value segment, which opens the editor.

members.name: nothingSelected
members.description: The pill's value segment before anything has been picked.

members.name: error
members.type: { title: string; describe: (filterKey?: string) => string; retry: string; }

members.name: validation
members.type: { required: string; minValue: (min: number) => string; maxValue: (max: number) => string; invalidFormat: string; }

FilterTab.description: A saved set of filters, offered as a tab above the bar.

FilterTabs.description:
Saved filter sets as tabs, or as a compact select via `display`. Both compare values and
operators exactly, preserve range endpoint order, and replace previous narrowing. `label`
names the control; `strings.customView` describes a changed selection.

props.name: tabs
props.description:
Saved sets. A tab is active only when every preset is applied AND nothing else is — so it
stops looking selected the moment the reader narrows further.

props.name: display
props.description: Compact saved-view control using the same presets and matching as the tab row.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for either presentation.

FilterType.description:
The filter types, exported as values rather than a type alone so a consumer can build a
filter definition without spelling the strings and can switch on them exhaustively.
FilterType.type: { readonly SELECT: "select"; readonly MULTI_SELECT: "multi_select"; readonly ASYNC_SELECT: "async_select"; readonly SEARCH: "search"; readonly RANGE: "range"; readonly DATE: "date"; readonly TAGS: "tags"; }

FilterValueDisplay.description:
The value segment of a pill: up to two overlapped icons, then a count, before the label.
Icons come before words — a reader scanning five pills recognises the status colours before
reading any label.

FiltersButton.description:
The add-filter button and its two-step popup: the filters not yet applied, then that
filter's editor with a way back. Two steps rather than nested submenus, which cannot be
operated by touch and close under a date picker.

props.name: availableFilters
props.description: Filters with no value yet.

props.name: labelVisibility
props.description: Icon-only is the compact toolbar default; visible suits a standalone call to action.

FormActionsBar.description: A form's actions in one row, with room for status before them.

props.name: children
props.description: The actions. `trailing` wins when both are given.

props.name: leading
props.description: Status or context before the actions — "Last saved 2 minutes ago".

props.name: trailing
props.description: The actions, in place of `children`. It wins when both are given.

props.name: sticky
props.description:
Pins the bar to the foot of its nearest scrolling ancestor, for a form longer than the
viewport.

FormControl.description:
The adapter contract: the one-method interface a form library satisfies to work with the
kit's fields. `useField` is a hook, called once per bound field during render, so an RHF
adapter can delegate to `useController`.

props.name: children
props.description:
A direct control, or an explicit adapter for a wrapped/custom control. Use the function
form when a consumer wrapper hides the actual control, and spread the supplied id and
aria props onto it.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Label beside the control instead of above it — for settings rows.

props.name: htmlFor
props.description:
The id the caption addresses, or `false` when there is no single labelable element.
A string associates the label with a control that already has an id, instead of the
generated one, or one that can't take it. `false` is for a cluster
(repeater, checkbox group, segments): the field becomes a named `group` instead. Opt-in,
because a group sharing its control's name makes `getByLabelText` ambiguous.

props.name: label
props.description:
Caption above the control, wired to it by a generated id unless the control has one of
its own, or `htmlFor` names one.

props.name: required
props.description:
Marks the label and the control: the indicator beside the label, and `aria-required`
on the control.

props.name: hint
props.description: Lowest priority: shown only when neither `error` nor `helperText` is set.

props.name: helperText
props.description: Middle priority: replaces `hint`, and is itself replaced by `error`.

props.name: error
props.description:
Highest priority of the three supporting lines. Announced politely and switches the
control to its invalid state.

FormSection.description: A titled group of fields, on a card's surface.

props.name: title
props.description: The header line.

props.name: description
props.description: The copy under the title.

props.name: actions
props.description: Controls on the title's own line.

props.name: footer
props.description: A footer below the fields.

props.name: surface
props.description:
Outer chrome. Use `flat` when the section already sits inside a card, which is most of
them.

members.name: countryCode
members.description:
An ISO country code deciding the line order, matched case-insensitively. Falls back
to `DEFAULT_ADDRESS_ORDER`; the reader's locale is never used to guess it.

members.name: order
members.description: Overrides the ordering outright.

members.name: separator
members.description: Joins fields on a line that does not specify its own.

members.name: locale
members.description:
The locale a two-letter `country` is named in ("GB" becomes "United Kingdom") via
`Intl.DisplayNames`; English when omitted. A longer `country` is printed as given.

members.name: locale
members.description: date-fns locale object. The React component reads it from the scope for you.

FormattingConfig.description: The locale shared by every formatter. Money and dates have their own slices.

members.name: locale
members.description: BCP-47 tag used by every Intl formatter in the kit.

members.name: preventIPhoneZoom
members.description: Opt in to a 16px minimum for native text fields on detected iPhones only.

props.name: location
props.description: Where it ships from.

props.name: notice
props.description: A standing fact about the group — "Shipping not required".

props.name: noticeIcon
props.description:
The glyph beside the notice. A component rather than a node, so the group sizes it:
one passed as a child arrives at lucide's own 24px default — three lines tall against
the text it annotates.

props.name: items
props.description: The rows, as data.

props.name: children
props.description:
Replaces `items` wholesale, for a caller who needs control of a row — the same seam
Accordion offers.

props.name: actions
props.description:
The first renders as a button; the rest collapse into an overflow menu. One array, so
the menu cannot duplicate the button.

members.name: formatHeading
members.description: Names the group by state and size — "Unfulfilled (3)".

members.name: formatUnitPrice
members.description: Reads the price column aloud — "€50.00 each, 1 of them".

FullscreenToggle.description:
The full-screen toggle, one of the table's own controls, on its own for a consumer building
their own toolbar.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides the default names for every toggle.

props.name: render
props.description: Replaces the underlying Button while retaining the toggle's behavior and content.

GlobalSearch.description:
The command palette's panel. It does not search: `query` is controlled and `results` are
given; debounce, endpoint and ranking belong to the app. It owns the regions, grouping, and
an arrow-key highlight.

props.name: results
props.description:
One shape for every kind, with optional parts: avatar OR thumbnail, a badge, meta, tags, a
timestamp, a trailing figure. A union per kind would be honest about the data and useless
for a list that renders them all the same way.

props.name: query
props.description: Controlled, always. The palette never searches; it renders what it is given.

props.name: onQueryChange
props.description: Receives every edit to `query`.

props.name: onResultSelect
props.description: Fires on click and on Enter, with the whole result including its free-form `data`.

props.name: onClose
props.description:
Fires on Escape. The dialog presentation wires this to closing itself; a panel embedded in
a page usually wants it too.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Swaps the input's clear control for a spinner and shows the loading region. Hidden results
cannot be selected while the loading region is visible.

props.name: idleSections
props.description:
Recent queries and curated suggestions. The palette has no memory of its own — whose
recents these are is a question only the app can answer.

props.name: groupLabels
props.description:
Names a group in the tab strip and above its results. Without it the raw key shows, which
is a useful default only while you are wiring it up.

props.name: slots
props.description:
`input`, `tabs`, `idle`, `empty`, `loading`, `footer`, and `renderResult` — every region,
replaceable one at a time.

props.name: tabs
props.description:
Replaces the auto-generated "All + one per group" strip, for a fixed set of tabs that
should not appear and disappear with the results.

GlobalSearchDialog.description:
The palette presentation over ActionDialog: focus trap, portal, scroll lock, and a dialog
role — none of which a hand-rolled fixed backdrop has.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires on Escape, on a backdrop click, and after a result is chosen.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Merged onto the dialog surface that positions the palette.

props.name: results
props.description:
One shape for every kind, with optional parts: avatar OR thumbnail, a badge, meta, tags, a
timestamp, a trailing figure. A union per kind would be honest about the data and useless
for a list that renders them all the same way.

props.name: query
props.description: Controlled, always. The palette never searches; it renders what it is given.

props.name: onQueryChange
props.description: Receives every edit to `query`.

props.name: onResultSelect
props.description: Fires on click and on Enter, with the whole result including its free-form `data`.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Swaps the input's clear control for a spinner and shows the loading region. Hidden results
cannot be selected while the loading region is visible.

props.name: idleSections
props.description:
Recent queries and curated suggestions. The palette has no memory of its own — whose
recents these are is a question only the app can answer.

props.name: groupLabels
props.description:
Names a group in the tab strip and above its results. Without it the raw key shows, which
is a useful default only while you are wiring it up.

props.name: slots
props.description:
`input`, `tabs`, `idle`, `empty`, `loading`, `footer`, and `renderResult` — every region,
replaceable one at a time.

props.name: tabs
props.description:
Replaces the auto-generated "All + one per group" strip, for a fixed set of tabs that
should not appear and disappear with the results.

GlobalSearchEmptyState.description: What the palette shows after a search that found nothing.

props.name: hint
props.description: One line of guidance toward a next move.

GlobalSearchFooter.description:
The keyboard-hint strip under the list. It is the only place a reader is told which three
keys the palette answers to.

props.name: escKey
props.description: The Escape key's cap. Its two neighbours are glyphs; this one is a word.

props.name: trailing
props.description: Right-aligned content, e.g. the result count.

GlobalSearchIdleSection.description: A static section shown while the query is too short to search on.

members.name: items
members.type: Array<{ id: string; label: ReactNode; icon?: ReactNode; onSelect?: () => void; }>

GlobalSearchIdleState.description:
What the palette shows before there is anything to search: recent queries and curated
suggestions, both supplied by the consumer — the palette does not remember anything itself.

props.name: fallbackIcons
props.description: Heading glyphs for sections without one: the first gets `recent`, the rest `suggestions`.

GlobalSearchInput.description:
The search row. Thin on purpose — base Input already owns the leading icon, the clear and the
sizing, so this only wires the palette's key handling to it.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the clear control.

GlobalSearchMeta.description: One inline fact on the secondary line.

members.name: mono

members.name: title

members.name: group

The bucket this lands in. Tabs and group headings are both generated from the groups that
actually returned something, unless `tabs` says otherwise.

members.name: data

One rich result — its media, title, context and trailing figure. Exported so a consumer
rendering their own groups keeps the row's highlight and keyboard behaviour.

members.name: idle

members.name: escKey

GlobalSearchTabs.description:
The group filter strip, built on OverflowTabBar rather than Tabs: these narrow one list
rather than switching between panels, and the distinction decides what the arrow keys do.

props.name: counts
props.description: One per tab value. A group with no results still shows its zero.

props.name: showBreadcrumbs

Prepended to the trail, for a root that is not part of the route. `null` omits it
deliberately.

HeaderBreadcrumbs.description:
The sidebar trigger, a rule, and the trail. The three travel together because their
arrangement is the part that goes wrong — a trail without the rule reads as the first
crumb, and a trigger placed after it reads as part of the path. The trigger stays fixed
while the trail truncates.

props.name: showSidebarTrigger
props.description: Renders the sidebar collapse control before the trail.

props.name: triggerSlot
props.description: Replaces that control — for a shell whose navigation opens some other way.

props.name: renderLink
props.description: Renders links through the application's router; without it, plain anchors.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the trail's navigation landmark; override it when a page carries two headers.

HeaderGlobalSearchTrigger.description:
The same trigger — a button shaped like a field, for a palette where the typing happens —
reporting into a controlled `open`. A separate component so a trigger never half-owns the
palette's state.

props.name: shortcutModifier

Which modifier the hint names. Detected from the platform on the client when omitted
(the server renders the non-Mac hint).

props.name: enableShortcut
props.description: Binds ⌘/Ctrl+K. Off for a page that already uses it.

props.name: shortcutSlot
props.description: Replaces the hint — for a product whose palette opens on something else.

members.name: time

members.name: href
members.description: Makes the row a link. Without it the row is a button.

props.name: notifications

props.name: unreadCount

Shown on the trigger. Separate from the unread entries in `notifications`, which are
only the most recent page.

props.name: renderNotification
props.description: Replaces the row entirely, for a product whose notices are not title-and-body.

props.name: renderLink

members.name: trigger

members.name: heading

members.name: unread
members.description: Announced count on the trigger, so the badge is not read as a bare number.

members.name: unreadItem
members.description: Announced on an unread row, whose tint and dot are visual only.

HeaderSearch.description:
The trigger for a command palette, not a search field. It LOOKS like an input and IS a
button, which is the honest shape: typing happens in the palette, so a real field here
would take a keystroke and then throw it away.

props.name: shortcutModifier

Which modifier the hint names. Detected from the platform on the client when omitted
(the server renders the non-Mac hint).

props.name: enableShortcut
props.description: Binds ⌘/Ctrl+K. Off for a page that already uses it.

props.name: shortcutSlot
props.description: Replaces the hint — for a product whose palette opens on something else.

members.name: placeholder

members.name: shortcutMac

HeaderSlots.description: The regions `Header` arranges, passed as its `slots`.

members.name: brand
