members.name: breadcrumbs
members.description: Replaces the built-in breadcrumbs entirely.

members.name: center
members.description: Shrinks before the right cluster — put a search field here.

members.name: right
members.description: Fixed-size controls: notifications, account, theme. Never shrinks.

HeaderToolButton.description:
An icon control in the right cluster — one shape for all of them, because a row where the
theme toggle is 32px and the help button is 36px reads as a mistake before anyone can
name it.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name. Icon-only controls have no other.

props.name: active
props.description: Marks it engaged — reported as `aria-pressed`, not just coloured.

props.name: badge
props.description: A count on the glyph. A number, a dot, anything short.

HeaderToolPopover.description:
The same control with a surface hanging off it, in the same one shape as every icon
control in the right cluster.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name. Icon-only controls have no other.

props.name: active
props.description: Marks it engaged — reported as `aria-pressed`, not just coloured.

props.name: badge
props.description: A count on the glyph. A number, a dot, anything short.

HeaderUserMenu.description:
The account control. The three callbacks build a command menu; supplying none and
passing `customContent` instead gives a panel, which is the escape hatch for an account
area that is not a list of verbs.

members.name: avatar
members.description: Image URL. Without one the shell derives initials from the name.

members.name: role
members.description: A job title or a role name, shown where there is room for a third line.

props.name: showIdentity
props.description: Shows the name and email beside the avatar. Off leaves an avatar-only trigger.

props.name: customContent
props.description:
Replaces the menu body wholesale, for content that is not a list of commands (a
workspace switcher, a theme row). Otherwise the three callbacks build the menu.

props.name: renderTrigger
props.description: Replaces the trigger, keeping the menu.

members.name: trigger
members.description: Names the trigger when the caller hides the name — an avatar alone has none.

HighlightedText.description:
The matched span inside a result label. Exported so a custom row keeps the highlight
rather than rendering a plain string beside ones that have it.

HoverCardContent.description: What the card shows: the preview itself, placed against its trigger.

props.name: container
props.description:
Where the popup renders. Defaults to the nearest `UIPortalHost`, else the primitive's
own target.

props.name: align
props.description: How the card lines up along the side it opens on: `start`, `center` or `end`.

props.name: side
props.description:
Where the card opens relative to its trigger: `top`, `right`, `bottom` or `left`, or
the logical `inline-start` or `inline-end`.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description: The gap between the trigger and the card, in pixels.

HoverCardTrigger.description:
What opens the card. Hover and focus both open it, because a card reachable only by
pointer is unreachable to a keyboard.

The delays live here, on the trigger. `closeDelay` is the load-bearing one: it keeps the
card open while the pointer crosses the gap to it, and without it the card closes as the
pointer leaves the trigger.

props.name: delay
props.description: How long to wait before the preview card opens. Specified in milliseconds.

props.name: closeDelay
props.description: How long to wait before closing the preview card. Specified in milliseconds.

IconBadge.description:
A glyph in a tinted medallion. Its size comes from `--icon-badge-size`, so a caller
needing a smaller mark re-points the token instead of redrawing the badge.

props.name: icon
props.description:
A component or a rendered node. A component is called with `aria-hidden`, because the
badge is a mark beside a name that already says it.

props.name: tone
props.description: Sets the fill and the glyph together, so the two cannot come from different tones.

props.name: shape
props.description: A rounded square, or a circle.

props.name: solid
props.description: Fills with the tone and inverts the glyph — for the one badge that must stand out.

props.name: bordered
props.description: A hairline outline, for a badge on a surface it would otherwise blend into.

ImageUpload.description:
A single image, where the picker is the preview in the shape it will have in the
product — a cover, a banner. Add an image, replace it, or remove it.

props.name: id
props.description: Applied to the file input itself, so a `FormField` label can address it.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this control's own copy — the empty frame, the overlay, and remove.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen file, controlled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the chosen file, or `undefined` when it is removed.

props.name: onRejectedFiles
props.description:
Receives the refused files. Report them through FormField's `error` prop: the error and
helper text are associated with the native input.

props.name: previewUrl
props.description:
An already-stored image. Uncontrolled, removing it clears its preview; when `value` is
controlled, clear both `value` and `previewUrl` in `onValueChange` to remove it.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The field's label, from `FormField`; the input is named by it and its action ("Logo Upload image").

props.name: accept
props.description:
Native accept filter, e.g. `.pdf,image/*`. Enforced here as well as by the dialog, and
checked before `onValueChange` rather than after, like every constraint.

props.name: minSizeBytes
props.description: Smallest file accepted, in bytes.

props.name: maxSizeBytes
props.description: Largest file accepted, in bytes.

props.name: validateFile
props.description: Runs after the type and size checks.

InboxCleanIllustration.description:
An open tray under a check — for "all caught up", not for "nothing exists". Drawn from the
theme's own tokens rather than shipped as an image, so it follows a rebrand and costs no
request.

props.name: value
props.description: Person, organisation, or resource name to derive initials from.

props.name: strategy
props.description: First + last word by default; `first-words` keeps the leading N words instead.

props.name: maxCharacters
props.description: How many characters are kept.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Returned when no usable letter or number exists.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: Rendered when the value is absent.

props.name: truncate
props.description: Ellipsises the value at one line. Every flex box in the chain needs `min-width: 0` — see `Text`.

members.name: strategy
members.description: First + last word by default; use first-words to preserve the first N words.

members.name: maxCharacters
members.description: Maximum visible characters. Defaults to 2.

members.name: locale
members.description: Optional BCP-47 locale used for locale-sensitive uppercasing.

members.name: fallback
members.description: Returned when no usable letter or number exists. Defaults to an empty string.

props.name: items
props.description:
Strings, not nodes: `Intl.ListFormat` formats text, and falling back to a hand join for
nodes would quietly lose the locale rules. A row of badges is a `Stack` with a gap.

props.name: join
props.description:
`and` is "A, B and C"; `or` is "A, B or C"; `none` is "A, B, C", for lists that are
not prose, where a trailing "and" reads as a claim the data is not making. Not called
`type`: every other primitive spends that word on the text tone.

props.name: joinStyle
props.description:
`long` is "and", `short` is "&" where the locale has one, `narrow` drops it. Not called
`style`, which is the DOM attribute and would have shadowed it.

props.name: max
props.description:
Shows at most this many, then a count of the rest inside the list, so the
conjunction still lands correctly: "Alice, Bob and 3 more".

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides the list's own copy: `more(count)`, which names the truncated remainder.

members.name: more
members.description: Names the items not shown when `max` truncates. Receives the count.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the fact. Rendered as a `DisplayLabel`, which has one style everywhere.

props.name: value
props.description:
The fact itself. Absent renders the empty marker rather than collapsing the row to its
label — a dash says the fact was looked for.

props.name: layout
props.description: How the free space between label and value is spent — the only thing the three change.

props.name: mono
props.description:
Tabular figures, for an amount or a counter — what makes a column of these compare down
the page instead of jittering with each digit's width.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Glyph before the value, in its own lane so the text never runs under it.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Glyph after the value, in its own lane so the text never runs under it.

props.name: startAddon
props.description:
Short text attached before the value, outside the text itself — a currency symbol, a
protocol, an at sign.

props.name: endAddon
props.description: Short text attached after the value, outside the text itself — a unit, a domain.

props.name: showCharacterCount
props.description: Shows "12 / 80" in the trailing lane. Requires `maxLength`.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Character cap, and the limit the count counts against. Input past it is refused.

props.name: clearable
props.description:
Shows a clear control once the field has a value. Clearing goes through the native
value setter, so React's value tracker stays in sync.

props.name: onClear
props.description: Called after the clear control empties the field.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Replaces the trailing affordance with a spinner, which outranks every other trailing
affordance.

props.name: invalid
props.description:
Applies the invalid treatment. Pair it with FormField's error for the message, so the
border and the announcement cannot disagree.

props.name: returnValueWithAddons
props.description:
Includes string addons in the value reported by `onChange`. Off, because an addon is
presentation: a caller that stores "$" and the number has to strip it again on the way
out.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this field's own copy — the clear label, the character-count format.

InputGroup.description:
The shell, with `role="group"`. It owns the border and the focus ring for whatever is
inside, so the control strips its own.

InputGroupAddon.description:
Something attached to the field — a unit, a prefix, a submit. Clicking it focuses the
control, as a label does, unless the click lands on a button.

props.name: align
props.description:
Where the addon attaches. The inline edges sit on the control's line; the block edges
take a row of their own, for a toolbar above a textarea or a hint below one.

InputGroupButton.description: A quiet Button sized to sit inside the field rather than beside it.

props.name: size
props.description:
The sizes that fit inside a field: two text sizes and their icon-only twins. A
full-height Button would set the field's height rather than fit in it, which is why
this is the one place the kit keeps a size prop on a control.

props.name: type
props.description: The native button type: `button` unless set, so pressing it never submits the form around the field.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Semantic colour intent. Resolves through the provider when omitted, so `UIProvider`
defaults can change it.

props.name: buttonStyle
props.description: Fill treatment, independent of `tone`. `UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description: Square button sized to its height. The label becomes the accessible name.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretches the button to its container's width.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a spinner and blocks interaction. The label keeps its space so the button does
not resize mid-action.

props.name: render
props.description:
The element this button becomes — an anchor, a router link, a label. `children` stay
the content and keep the button's label wrapper, so a link still sizes like a button.
`render` is how every kit component changes its element, the contract Base UI's parts
already take.

  <Button render={<a href="/settings" />}>Settings</Button>

InputGroupInput.description:
The kit's Input with its chrome removed, because the group is drawing it. Every other
prop passes through.

InputGroupText.description:
Secondary text at the group's own size — a unit, a domain suffix, a counter. It inherits
the size, so it cannot drift from the input beside it.

InputGroupTextarea.description:
The kit's Textarea with its chrome removed, because the group is drawing it. Every other
prop passes through.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides the character-count and clear copy.

props.name: maxLength

props.name: showCharacterCount

props.name: loading
props.description: Replaces the trailing affordance with a loading indicator.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Applies the invalid styling, the same as Input. Validation copy stays with FormField.

props.name: rows
props.description:
Visible lines. Without `minRows` it is the floor the field grows from; `maxRows` sets
where it stops growing and scrolls.

props.description:
Height at which the field stops growing and starts scrolling. Without a ceiling a long
note pushes the submit button off the screen.

props.name: variant
props.description: The chosen option, when the product has any.

props.name: stock
props.description: Units on hand. Zero reads as out, which is checked before low.

props.name: reorderLevel
props.description: At or below this, the level reads as low rather than healthy.

props.name: maxStock
props.description: The gauge's upper bound.

props.name: lastRestocked
props.description: Already formatted.

props.name: title

The heading. Either it or `description` renders the header; neither, and the block is a
bare surface.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting copy on its own row, so a long one wraps under the whole header.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading glyph on the title line.

props.name: titleSuffix
props.description: Content immediately after the title — a badge, a count.

props.name: headerEnd
props.description: Controls at the end of the title line.

Outer chrome. What separates `bordered` from `card` is the ground: a bordered block is a
ruled region and the page shows through it; a card block lifts off it.

Drops the surface's inset and clips to its radius, for content that runs to the edge
(divided cells, ruled rows); children pay their own inset. Only meaningful on a surface
that has an inset to drop.

props.name: value
props.description:
The record: sku, barcode, trackQuantity, available, committed, incoming,
lowStockThreshold, inventoryPolicy, binLocation, requiresShipping, weight,
countryOfOrigin, hsCode, tags.

props.description:
Reports the field, its new value, and what it replaced — an undo stack that has to
remember that itself is one that gets it wrong once. Omit for a read-only record.

props.name: sections
props.description:
Narrows what is drawn, so one surface serves a simple product, a variant and a location
record without forking. Every section by default.

The heading. Either it or `description` renders the header; neither, and the block is a
bare surface.

props.description: Leading glyph on the title line.

Outer chrome. What separates `bordered` from `card` is the ground: a bordered block is a

members.description: Off means the other quantity fields have no meaning and are not drawn.

members.name: formatLevel
members.description: Names the gauge, which otherwise states the level by width alone.

members.name: unitPrice
members.description: A number, not a string — the table totals these.

props.name: currency
props.description: ISO 4217. Handed to the Money primitive, which knows each currency's exponent.

props.name: taxRate
props.description: A ratio — `0.2` is 20%. Omit to show no tax row.

Item.description:
A row — a list row, a menu row, a table row. No size prop: row height follows
`--density-scale`, so use a denser scope for a denser list.

props.name: surface
props.description: The row's chrome. Never `default`: the vocabulary is fixed.

props.name: render
props.description:
Allows you to replace the component's HTML element
with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

ItemActions.description: Trailing controls. Kept out of the content flow, so a long title cannot displace them.

ItemContent.description:
The title and description. Takes the remaining width and truncates rather than pushing
the actions off the row.

ItemFooter.description:
A full-width row below the row's own content, for an item that carries a footnote
without it competing with the title line.

ItemGroup.description: Stacks rows and owns the dividers, so a row never draws its own.

props.name: ruled
props.description:
Draws hairlines between rows instead of gaps, and neutral rows drop their inline
padding and go flush. For a run of rows inside one card, where a rem of air between
each reads as unrelated blocks. Bordered and muted rows keep their inset, because they
do draw a surface.

ItemHeader.description:
A full-width row above the row's own content, for an item that carries an eyebrow
without it competing with the title line.

ItemMedia.description: The leading slot: a glyph, an avatar or a thumbnail, aligned to the first line.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Sizes the leading slot. `icon` fits a glyph; `image` gets the larger box an avatar or
thumbnail needs; `plain` leaves the slot to its content.

ItemSeparator.description:
A rule between items, for a group that wants one only in places. `ItemGroup ruled` is the
answer when every row needs one.

props.name: variant
props.description:
How the rule is drawn. Structural, not semantic — a dashed rule is the same divider,
drawn as provisional.

props.name: thickness
props.description:
The rule's thickness: a CSS length, or a number in pixels. Overrides
`--separator-thickness` for this rule, e.g. a seam between panels.

props.name: label
props.description:
Text set into a gap in the rule — "OR", "More options". Horizontal only. It drops the
separator role, because the rule is then decoration around real text.

props.name: aria-hidden
props.description: Indicates whether the element is exposed to an accessibility API.

Kanban.description:
A drag-and-drop board. It never persists: `onValueChange` is the truth, and `onItemMove` the
seam for saving it.

props.name: value
props.description:
The board, as `Record<columnId, T[]>`: a plain object because that is what a board is,
and it serialises without a thought. Column titles and limits are the consumer's — only
the ORDER lives here.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the whole next board after every move.

props.name: getItemValue
props.description: A stable id per item. Everything else is keyed off this.

props.name: onItemMove
props.description:
Fires after a move lands, with both ends of it — from column and index, to column and
index. The seam for persistence or analytics. Idempotent: a move that changes nothing
fires nothing.

props.name: itemActions
props.description:
Each card's actions, or a function of the card. The factory form is what a real board
needs: “Reopen” belongs on a card in Done and nowhere else, and a fixed list would render
it everywhere and disable it.

props.name: onItemClick
props.description:
Fires on a card click that was not the handle or the menu — both mark themselves, so a
click on an icon inside either is caught too.

KanbanColumnContent.description:
A column's droppable region, for a board that wants its own column chrome but the same drag
behaviour.

members.name: activeId
members.description: The id being dragged, or `null`.

members.name: findItem
members.type: (id: string) => { columnId: string; index: number; item: T; } | undefined

KanbanItem.description:
One draggable card, for a board that wants its own column chrome but the same drag
behaviour.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Stops this card being dragged, e.g. while it is mid-mutation.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Overrides the board's `onItemClick` for this card.

KanbanItemActions.description: The card's verbs: its `itemActions`, in a menu.

KanbanItemContextValue.description:
What one card publishes to its parts. `registerHandle`: a mounted handle registers
itself, and the card then attaches drag listeners to the handle instead of its surface.

members.name: item
members.description: `null` when the id resolves to nothing, e.g. a card removed mid-drag.

KanbanItemHandle.description:
The grip. Optional: present, it becomes the only grip; absent, the whole card is. A handle
rather than a draggable card body, because a card carrying a menu and a link has no way to
tell a drag from a press otherwise — and text inside the card stays selectable.

KanbanOverlay.description:
What follows the pointer during a drag — rendered outside the column so it is not clipped by
the scroll container it started in.

props.name: render
props.type: (context: { item: T | null; columnId: string | null; }) => ReactNode
props.description:
Replaces the default outline with the consumer's own card. The default is a placeholder
rather than a copy of the card, because the card's markup lives at the call site.

members.name: formatDragStart
members.description: The drag announcements, as functions so languages can inflect or reorder the sentence.

Kbd.description:
One key, or one chord pressed together written as a single string — "⌘K", not three caps,
because nested `Kbd`s are announced element by element. A native `<kbd>`: every native
attribute passes through.

KbdGroup.description:
Several `Kbd` in a row, for a sequence pressed one after another — "G then I". The caps sit
further apart than the characters inside one, and that gap is what tells a reader the keys
are pressed in turn rather than together.

KeyValueEditor.description:
Key/value pairs rather than an object, so a half-typed or blank key keeps its row and its
value. Convert to an object on submit.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this editor's own copy — the two placeholders, add, and remove.

props.name: sortable
props.description: Adds the drag handle and arrow-key reordering.

props.name: flagDuplicateKeys
props.description:
Flags a key that is already used elsewhere in the list. A blank key is not a
duplicate — it is an unfinished row.

members.name: keyLabel
members.description: Names each field by its row (the placeholder is identical on every row).

members.name: add
members.description: The control that appends a row.

members.name: moved
members.description:
Announced after a keyboard move. Optional so older complete strings objects still
type-check.

members.name: remove
members.description: Names each row's remove control, by its row.

members.name: reorder
members.description: Names the drag handle, including how to move it by keyboard.

members.name: emptyState
members.description:
Shown when the list is empty; the `emptyState` prop replaces it. Optional so older
complete strings objects still type-check.

Label.description:
A form label: a real `<label>`, so clicking it focuses the control it names. Takes
everything a native label takes.

props.name: htmlFor
props.description:
The control's id. Without it the label is decoration: clicking it does nothing and
nothing is announced.

LanguageSwitcher.description:
The locale control. Each option is named in its own language and carries `lang`, so a
screen reader pronounces it correctly.

props.name: locales
props.description: The languages offered, each named in its own language.

props.name: value
props.description: The current locale's `value`.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called with the chosen locale's `value`.

props.name: variant
props.description:
`pills` for two or three languages, where every option is worth showing; `menu` once
there are more, where a row of pills becomes a second navigation.

props.name: label
props.description: Names this one switcher. Overrides the strings default.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides the default name for every switcher.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the control.

Link.description:
The plain anchor the three contact primitives are built on: the kit's `TextLink`, or the
empty mark when there is nothing to link.

ListRadioGroup.description:
Single-select as a divided vertical list, for options with a descriptive second line —
plan tiers, roles. The same component as `CardRadioGroup`, laid out another way.

props.name: options
props.description:
The choices, in the one shape card, list and pill groups share: value, label,
description, icon, and an optional tooltip.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial value, for uncontrolled selection.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the chosen value.

props.name: name
props.description: Field name, used for the group's native form participation.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every option.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Applies the invalid treatment. Pair it with a message on the FormField.

props.name: aria-label
props.description:
The group's name and description. `FormField` supplies `aria-labelledby` and
`aria-describedby`.

members.name: description
members.description: Supporting sentence. Card and list groups show it; a pill has no room for one.

members.name: icon
members.description: Leading glyph. A Lucide icon, any component taking a className, or a rendered node.

members.name: tooltip
members.description:
Detail that doesn't fit the row, shown in a tooltip from an info glyph beside the label.
The glyph isn't focusable; the text also becomes the option's accessible description.

LoaderButton.description:
A `Button` that can run its handler and hold the pending state itself. It also announces
the wait, which `Button`'s own `loading` prop does not.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Semantic colour intent. Resolves through the provider when omitted, so `UIProvider`
defaults can change it.

props.name: buttonStyle
props.description: Fill treatment, independent of `tone`. `UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description: Square button sized to its height. The label becomes the accessible name.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretches the button to its container's width.

props.name: render
props.description:
The element this button becomes — an anchor, a router link, a label. `children` stay
the content and keep the button's label wrapper, so a link still sizes like a button.
`render` is how every kit component changes its element, the contract Base UI's parts
already take.

  <Button render={<a href="/settings" />}>Settings</Button>

props.name: loading
props.description:
Controlled pending state. Omit it and the button holds the state itself, from the
promise `onClick` returns.

props.name: handlesLoading
props.description:
Accepted so call sites that pass it keep compiling; inert. Choosing `LoaderButton` is
already that decision. Swallowed rather than spread, so it never reaches the DOM.

props.name: onClick
props.description: May return a promise; the button then stays pending until it settles.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides the button's own copy: what it announces while it works.

LoadingState.description:
A whole region that is working. A region, not an overlay — it occupies what the content
will occupy. Distinct from `Empty` and `ErrorState`: the three are different answers and
must look different.

props.name: label
props.description: Copy for the wait, replacing the default.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides the default copy.

members.name: value
members.description: BCP 47 tag — "en", "nl", "pt-BR".

members.name: label
members.description: The language's name IN that language — "Nederlands", not "Dutch".

LocalizedObjectField.description:
Several fields per locale — a title and a body, say — behind one switcher, with the
active locale switchable in place. A translation UI built out of plain repeaters loses
which language a row belongs to the moment rows reorder.

props.name: fields
props.description: The fields inside each locale.

members.name: name
members.description: Key in each locale's object.

LocalizedStringField.description:
One value per locale behind a single field with a locale switcher, so a translated field
costs one row instead of one row per language. The active locale is view state, not part
of the value.

props.name: locales
props.description: Which locales the switcher offers, in order. The first is the default.

props.name: multiline
props.description: A textarea per locale rather than an input.

props.name: requiredLocales
props.description: Marks locales that must be filled, so the switcher can flag what is missing.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The field's name; `FormField` supplies the `aria-*` wiring below.

LocalizedStringRepeater.description:
An ordered list of localized strings, each row a `LocalizedStringField`: one value per
language, with the active locale switchable in place. A translation UI built out of plain
repeaters loses which language a row belongs to the moment rows reorder.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this list's own copy — the add control and each row's remove.

props.name: sortable
props.description: Adds the drag handle and arrow-key reordering.

members.name: label
members.description: What earned or spent the points.

members.name: date
members.description: Already formatted.

members.name: points
members.description: The magnitude. The sign is drawn from `earned`, not parsed out of this.

props.name: balance
props.description: A number gets locale grouping; a string is taken as already formatted.

props.name: tier
props.description:
The tier's name. There is no default: it is a caller's word, and an English literal
here is one no strings override could reach.

props.name: tierTone
props.description: The tier badge's tone.

props.name: title
props.description:
The heading. Either it or `description` renders the header; neither, and the block is a
bare surface.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting copy on its own row, so a long one wraps under the whole header.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading glyph on the title line.

props.name: titleSuffix
props.description: Content immediately after the title — a badge, a count.

props.name: headerEnd
props.description: Controls at the end of the title line.

props.name: surface
props.description:
Outer chrome. What separates `bordered` from `card` is the ground: a bordered block is a
ruled region and the page shows through it; a card block lifts off it.

props.name: flush
props.description:
Drops the surface's inset and clips to its radius, for content that runs to the edge
(divided cells, ruled rows); children pay their own inset. Only meaningful on a surface
that has an inset to drop.

members.name: activityLabel
members.description: Over the movement list — without it the rows hang under a balance they only relate to.

Map.description:
A Leaflet map in the kit's vocabulary. Everything else from react-leaflet's MapContainer
passes through, except `zoomControl` — MapZoomControl replaces it.

props.name: center
props.description: Where the map opens, with `zoom`.

props.name: height
props.description:
Minimum height: `sm`, `md` and `lg` are 16, 24 and 36rem, or any CSS length. A MINIMUM, not
a fixed height — the map still grows to fill a flex parent that gives it room, which is what
a map docked beside a list needs.

props.name: surface
props.description:
`framed` draws the border and radius the tiles need against a page of the same colour.
`flush` removes both, for a map that IS the panel rather than one sitting inside it — a
sheet's body, a full-bleed hero.

MapCircle.description:
A circle sized in metres, so it grows as the map zooms in — MapCircleMarker is sized in
pixels, and the difference matters the moment someone zooms. Like every shape primitive it
takes the kit's tokens for stroke and fill, so a drawn area matches the surface it sits on.

MapCircleMarker.description:
A circle sized in pixels, so it keeps its size at every zoom — MapCircle is sized in metres.
Like every shape primitive it takes the kit's tokens for stroke and fill, so a drawn area
matches the surface it sits on.

MapControlContainer.description:
The frame every control sits in. Beyond placement it suppresses Leaflet's handlers, so
a click on a button does not pan the map and a scroll over a menu does not zoom it.

props.name: position
props.description: The corner it anchors to.

MapDrawCircle.description:
The drawing button for a circle. Each shape's button takes Leaflet's own draw options for that
shape, so nothing is re-declared here.

props.name: shapeOptions
props.description: The options used when drawing the circle on the map.

props.name: showRadius
props.description: Whether to show the radius in the tooltip

MapDrawControl.description:
The drawing toolbar. It composes the tool buttons, so a caller who wants only two of them
mounts those two instead of configuring the toolbar out.

props.name: onLayersChange
props.description:
Fires on create, edit, and delete, with the FeatureGroup — call `toGeoJSON()` on it to
persist.

MapDrawDelete.description: Deletes shapes from the drawing's feature group.

MapDrawEdit.description: Edits the shapes in the drawing's feature group.

props.name: selectedPathOptions
props.description:
The path options for how the layers will look while in edit mode.
If this is set to null the editable path options will not be set.

MapDrawMarker.description:
The drawing button for a marker. Each shape's button takes Leaflet's own draw options for that
shape, so nothing is re-declared here.

MapDrawPolygon.description:
The drawing button for a polygon. Each shape's button takes Leaflet's own draw options for that
shape, so nothing is re-declared here.

props.name: drawError
props.description: Configuration options for the error that displays if an intersection is detected.

props.name: shapeOptions
props.description: The options used when drawing the polyline/polygon on the map.

MapDrawPolyline.description:
The drawing button for a line. Each shape's button takes Leaflet's own draw options for that
shape, so nothing is re-declared here.

props.name: drawError
props.description: Configuration options for the error that displays if an intersection is detected.

props.name: shapeOptions
props.description: The options used when drawing the polyline/polygon on the map.

props.name: showLength
props.description: Whether to display distance in the tooltip

MapDrawRectangle.description:
The drawing button for a rectangle. Each shape's button takes Leaflet's own draw options for that
shape, so nothing is re-declared here.

props.name: shapeOptions
props.description: The options used when drawing the rectangle on the map.

props.name: showArea
props.description:
Show the area of the drawn rectangle in m², ha or km².
The area is only approximate and become less accurate the larger the rectangle is.

MapDrawUndo.description:
Undo for the current edit or delete: it steps back what that mode has staged, rather than the
whole session. Outside one there is nothing to undo — leaflet-draw has already committed it.

MapFeatureGroup.description:
A toggleable group of overlays that also answers as one shape for events and bounds, which is
what the drawing tools edit against.

props.name: name
props.description: Names the group in the layers control, and registers it with the enclosing MapLayers.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the group's checkbox in the layers control.

MapFullscreenControl.description: Toggles the map in and out of full screen.

MapLayerGroup.description: A toggleable group of overlays, registered with the enclosing MapLayers by `name`.

props.name: name
props.description: Names the group in the layers control, and registers it with the enclosing MapLayers.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the group's checkbox in the layers control.

MapLayers.description:
Holds the registry every named layer reports into. Tile layers become a radio group and
layer groups a checkbox list in MapLayersControl — no array to keep in step with the
children.

props.name: defaultTileLayer
props.description:
Names a MapTileLayer. Naming nothing REPORTS through `onError` and shows the first
registered layer, rather than throwing — a typo should not take down the page.

props.name: defaultLayerGroups
props.description: The layer groups switched on at first, by name.

props.name: onError
props.description:
Hears about a `defaultTileLayer` or `defaultLayerGroups` naming nothing — a typo that would
otherwise show an empty map and no reason for it.

MapLayersControl.description:
The layer picker. It throws when mounted outside MapLayers rather than rendering an empty
menu, because a control with nothing to control is a wiring mistake, not a state.

props.name: tileLayersLabel
props.description: Heads the tile layers' radio group.

props.name: layerGroupsLabel
props.description: Heads the layer groups' checkboxes.

props.name: position
props.description: The corner it anchors to.

MapLocateControl.description:
Find-me. It draws a pulse at the fix rather than only recentring, because a map that jumps
with no mark leaves the reader hunting for what moved. `watch` follows the device; the watch
is stopped on unmount, since one left running keeps the radio awake.

props.name: icon
props.description:
Rendered to a string and handed to Leaflet as a div icon. The accessible name is written
onto the element after Leaflet builds it, because Leaflet builds it outside React.

MapMarkerClusterGroup.description:
Collapses markers into counted clusters as the map zooms out. Above a few hundred pins the map
stops being readable and starts being a texture.

props.name: icon
props.description: Receives how many markers the cluster holds.

props.name: polygonOptions
props.description: polygonOptions

props.name: spiderLegPolylineOptions
props.description: spiderLegPolylineOptions

MapPolygon.description:
A polygon, taking the kit's tokens for stroke and fill so a drawn area matches the surface it
sits on.

MapPolyline.description: A line, taking the kit's tokens for stroke so it matches the surface it sits on.

MapPopup.description:
Attached to a marker or a shape, a popup is clicked open and stays. A popup is where an
action belongs; a tooltip cannot hold one.

MapRectangle.description:
A rectangle, taking the kit's tokens for stroke and fill so a drawn area matches the surface
it sits on.

MapSearchControl.description: Place search over the map: a PlaceAutocomplete in one of the control corners.

props.name: searchUrl
props.description: Replaces the public, rate-limited Photon endpoint; anything answering Photon's GeoJSON works.

props.name: onResultsChange
props.description: Every result, whenever they change, e.g. for a map that pins them all.

props.name: bbox
props.description: [minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat]; results are restricted to it.

props.name: lat
props.description: Biases results toward a point rather than restricting them.

props.name: zoom
props.description: How local the bias is.

props.name: locationBiasScale
props.description: How strong it is.

members.name: defaultTileLayer
members.description: Names the tile layer that supplies no name of its own.

members.name: editInstructions
members.description: Leaflet-draw's own on-map tooltip while editing.

MapTileLayer.description:
A base map. Give it a `name` and it registers itself with the enclosing MapLayers, which is
how the layers control knows what to offer without being told twice. Without a `url` it draws
OpenStreetMap's own tiles — the only basemap that renders with no key.

props.name: name
props.description:
Names the layer in the layer control, and registers it with the enclosing MapLayers under
that name.

props.name: darkUrl
props.description:
Swapped in when the dark theme is active. The default tiles are inverted in dark mode,
since there is no key-less dark basemap; passing `darkUrl` removes the filter.

MapTooltip.description:
Attached to a marker or a shape, a tooltip comes and goes with the pointer, so it cannot hold
an action; that is what a popup is for. It takes a `side` and an offset, and Leaflet's own tip
is removed, because a single built-in tip cannot sit on a side this component chose.

props.name: side
props.description: The side of its anchor it sits on.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description: Distance from the anchor, in pixels.

props.name: value
props.description: The amount.

props.name: unit
props.description:
A CSS-style unit identifier — `kilogram`, `meter`, `liter`, `celsius`, `byte`.

Passed to `Intl.NumberFormat`, which owns both the abbreviation and where it goes:
English writes "2.5 kg" and French writes "2,5 kg", and neither is a string this
component should be assembling.

props.name: unitDisplay
props.description: `short` is "2.5 kg", `narrow` is "2.5kg", `long` is "2.5 kilograms".

props.name: maximumFractionDigits
props.description: Caps the decimals. The value is not rounded before formatting.

MediaGallery.description:
Chosen images as reorderable tiles, for a gallery rather than a queue. The order is part of
the value: the first tile is the cover.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled. The order is part of the value: the first entry is the cover.

props.name: showCover
props.description: Badges the first tile as the cover. Defaults to true; turn off when order carries no meaning.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this gallery's own copy.

props.name: accept
props.description:
Native accept filter, e.g. `.pdf,image/*`. Enforced here as well as by the dialog, and
checked before `onValueChange` rather than after, like every constraint.

props.name: minSizeBytes
props.description: Smallest file accepted, in bytes.

props.name: maxSizeBytes
props.description: Largest file accepted, in bytes.

props.name: validateFile
props.description: Runs after the type and size checks.

members.name: cover
members.description: Badge on the first tile (hidden with `showCover={false}`).

members.name: add
members.description: The tile that opens the file picker.

members.name: position
members.type: (name: string, index: number, total: number) => string
members.description: Names a tile, with its position and how to move it.

members.name: remove
members.description: Names the control that removes one tile, after its file.

MediaLibrary.description:
The asset browser, as a panel. The detail panel is a column beside the grid, not an overlay,
so several assets can be edited in a row.

props.name: showMeta
props.description: Shows each asset's size and dimensions under its name.

props.name: typeFilters
props.description: The type filters the toolbar offers. A single type filter draws no control.

props.name: confirmOnSelect
props.description:
Picking is confirming: fires `onConfirm` immediately and removes the footer. The shape a
single-select picker wants.

props.name: bulkActions
props.description:
Bulk actions for a selection, rendered in the shared BatchActionBar. Browsing only:
a picker's footer already reports the selection, so the bar is suppressed there.

props.name: slots
props.description:
`headerStart`/`headerEnd`, `toolbarEnd`, `empty`, `loading`, `error`, `footer`,
`uploadEmpty`, plus `renderItem` and `renderDetail`.

props.name: items
props.description:
The assets, when the library searches, filters and sorts them itself. Supply this or
`fetcher`, not both: it is ignored entirely when `fetcher` is set.

props.name: fetcher
props.description:
Supplying it hands searching, filtering, and sorting to the server: the fetcher owns all
three, and `items` is ignored.

props.name: accessors
props.description:
Reads id, name, src, type, size, and the rest off your own shape. Supply only the ones that
differ from MediaLibraryItem's names.

props.name: collections
props.description: The collections the toolbar offers.

props.name: selectionMode
props.description:
`single` replaces the selection rather than toggling off, so a picker never ends up empty
by accident.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled: the selected ids.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Uncontrolled: the ids selected at first.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description:
Receives the selected ids, controlled or not, and the resolved assets too, so a consumer
never has to look them up again.

props.name: onItemUpdate
props.description:
Awaited. A rejection rolls the local overlay back and reaches `onError`; the panel stays
open so the reader can see what failed.

props.name: applyItemPatch
props.description:
Maps a standard metadata patch onto a consumer-owned record shape, without mutating the
original. Defaults to merging fields onto MediaLibraryItem.

props.name: onItemDelete
props.description:
Awaited. A rejection keeps the asset and reaches `onError`; the panel stays open so the
reader can see what failed.

props.name: onUpload
props.description:
Receives the files, the upload options, and helpers carrying stable staged files and IDs,
an AbortSignal, `setProgress`, and `setFileStatus`. Failed files stay queued for retry.
Returning the created items adds AND selects them — the reader uploaded them in order to
use them.

props.name: onError
props.description: Receives failures from the fetcher, uploads, updates, and deletes.

MediaLibraryCard.description: One asset in the grid, with its preview, name and selection control.

MediaLibraryDetailPanel.description:
The panel for the selected asset. The detail is a COLUMN rather than an overlay: an overlay
would cover the grid the reader is comparing against.

MediaLibraryEmptyState.description: The state with no assets: bordered and inset, since it stands in for a grid.

MediaLibraryFooter.description:
The selection bar: what is chosen, and what can be done with it — the summary and the actions
together.

props.name: chrome
props.description: `section` draws the rule and the inset; `bare` leaves both to a surrounding shell.

props.name: visibleCount
props.description: With nothing selected and a filter on, the count replaces the hint.

MediaLibraryFooterActions.description:
The footer's verbs: what can be done with the selection, or with the staged files. Split from
the summary, so a consumer can keep the count and supply their own verbs.

MediaLibraryFooterSummary.description:
The footer line: what is chosen — a selection count while browsing, a staged-file tally while
uploading. A live region, so keyboard picks inside the grid are announced. Split from the
actions, so a consumer can keep the count and supply their own verbs.

props.name: visibleCount
props.description: With nothing selected and a filter on, the count replaces the hint.

MediaLibraryGrid.description:
The composable visual grid. Like the list and the table, it uses the same accessors and
selection callbacks.

MediaLibraryList.description:
The composable compact rows. Like the grid and the table, it uses the same accessors and
selection callbacks.

MediaLibrarySelectionBar.description:
Result counts, pending announcements, and selection of the visible results. Selections the
current filters hide are preserved.

MediaLibraryTable.description:
The composable metadata table for inspecting assets; selection and details remain separate
controls. Like the grid and the list, it uses the same accessors and selection callbacks.

MediaLibraryToolbar.description: Search, filter and view controls. A single type filter draws no control.

MediaLibraryUploadPanel.description:
The drop target and queue inside the library, so uploading happens where the assets are
rather than behind a second dialog.

props.name: showActions
props.description: Hide when a composed picker footer owns upload actions.

MediaPreview.description:
The thumbnail that handles an image, a video, a PDF and a file with no preview at all — the
last being the case a gallery usually forgets. It shows the asset's picture, or a stand-in: a
broken `src` falls back to the type glyph, and `tint` gives an asset without a preview a
recognisable colour.

MediaResourceGallery.description:
The assets attached to a record, in order — with reorder, cover, and detach. Not a browser:
`onAdd` usually opens the library dialog. Reordering uses move buttons rather than drag, so it
works with keyboard, screen reader and touch.

props.name: primaryId
props.description: The cover.

props.name: onAdd
props.description: Usually opens the library dialog.

props.name: maxItems
props.description: The add control hides once reached.

members.name: empty
members.description: Shown in the empty frame, and again over a filled one.

members.name: remove
members.description: Names the control that discards the current file.

members.name: id
members.description: Stable identity, conventionally `"<kind>:<recordId>"`.

members.name: kind
members.description: Must match a key in the resource registry.

members.name: label
members.description: What the chip reads.

members.name: href
members.description: A permalink. With one the chip becomes a link.

members.name: data
members.description: Whatever the consumer wants to carry: the record itself, analytics.

props.name: mentions
props.description: The mentions the record carries, resolved against the body by `data-ref-id`.

props.name: renderMention
props.description:
Takes over every chip. More specific than `resources.<kind>.renderChip`, which is more
specific than `resources.<kind>.tone`.

props.name: sanitizer
props.description:
Replaces the kit's allow-list. There is no way to turn sanitising off — the escape hatch is
a different sanitiser, not the absence of one.

props.name: lineHeight
props.description: Defaults to `relaxed`, the editor's prose leading, so a body does not reflow once posted.

MentionInlineSuggestions.description:
The panel for the inline-trigger flow. Not a popover: the editor keeps focus and the caret.
The consumer wraps the editor in a relatively positioned element; this pins itself below it.

props.name: suggestionsByKind
props.description: Every kind's rows, for the tab counts.

props.name: suggestions
props.description: The active kind's rows.

props.name: query
props.description: Echoed in the header; the consumer owns the input.

props.name: onManualKindChange
props.description: Fires when the writer picks a tab, so the hook can stop auto-switching.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description:
Closes the completion session on Escape or editor blur. Wire to `setPickerOpen(false)`.
Unchanged caret callbacks do not reopen a dismissed query.

members.name: empty
members.description: Shown when the query matched nothing in any kind.

members.name: listLabel
members.description: The list's accessible name.

members.name: formatQuery
members.description: Wraps the search term in the panel header; quotation marks are locale-specific („…“, « … »).

MentionKindTabs.description:
The kind tabs, one of the parts both mention surfaces are built from, so the inline panel and
the popover cannot drift into showing the same data two ways.

props.name: suggestionsByKind
props.description: Row counts per kind, so a tab can say how many matches are behind it.

props.name: focusable
props.description: Inline completion keeps all keyboard focus in the editor.

MentionPicker.description:
The popover for the button flow — the same tabs and rows as the inline panel, plus a search
field of its own, because a reader who pressed a button has typed nothing to search with. The
consumer supplies the Popover and its trigger.

MentionPickerStrings.description: The picker's strings: the inline panel's plus its own search field.

members.name: empty
members.description: Shown when the query matched nothing in any kind.

members.name: listLabel
members.description: The list's accessible name.

members.name: formatQuery
members.description: Wraps the search term in the panel header; quotation marks are locale-specific („…“, « … »).

MentionResource.description: One resource kind the picker offers.

members.name: label

members.name: trigger

The character that opens the picker inline. Optional — a kind with no trigger is still
reachable from the picker button, which is right for one that is browsed rather than typed.

members.name: suggestions

members.name: renderChip

MentionRows.description:
The suggestion rows, one of the parts both mention surfaces are built from, so the inline
panel and the popover cannot drift into showing the same data two ways.

props.name: command
props.description: Use registered Command items inside an existing Command/CommandList.

props.name: id
props.description: Connects an inline editor to its active suggestion.

MentionSuggestion.description: One row in the picker, returned by a kind's `search`.

members.name: description
members.description: Supporting copy under the label, e.g. to tell two people of one name apart.

members.name: kind
members.description: Set by the search, not by the caller: which kind this row came from.

Menubar.description:
The bar. Its menus are `DropdownMenu` roots, each holding a `MenubarTrigger` and a
`DropdownMenuContent` with every row the dropdown menu offers.

The menu itself is the dropdown menu module's, not a copy under a second name — so
groups, labels, checkbox and radio items, submenus and the portal are the dropdown
menu's parts too, and a reader who has learned one has learned the other.

MenubarTrigger.description:
One menu's word in the bar, placed inside a `DropdownMenu` beside its
`DropdownMenuContent`. Once a menu is open, moving along the bar opens the next without
a second click — which is what makes a menubar a menubar rather than a row of dropdowns.

MetadataList.description:
Label/value facts about one thing, in three layouts over the same data. Returns `null`
when the list is empty, so a caller can render it unconditionally.

props.name: items
props.description:
The facts: a label and a value each, and optionally a description, a tooltip, an icon,
an empty label and a renderer.

props.name: layout
props.description:
How the facts are laid out: `grid` (label above value, in columns, for detail panels),
`rows` (a ruled list, for labels of varied length), or `inline` ("Created 4 Jan · By
Alice · v3.2"), whose items take no description. One component, because the three carry
the same data — a screen that switches between them changes a prop, not its items.

props.name: columns
props.description:
How many columns the grid uses — a ceiling for the grid layout. A plain number picks a
responsive recipe; an object sets the breakpoints itself.

props.name: density
props.description:
`compact` tightens the rhythm — the gaps and the row inset — for a dense panel. The value
keeps its size.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description:
Shown for a fact whose value is absent. A dash says "we looked"; an omitted row does
not.

props.name: title
props.description: A label above the facts.

props.name: titleSeparator
props.description: Draws a rule between the title and the first fact.

props.name: separator
props.description: Between a label and its value, inline. Defaults to a colon.

props.name: itemSeparator
props.description:
Between facts: `true` for a rule in the rows layout, or a character for the inline
one.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this list's own copy — the info triggers' names.

MetadataListItem.description: One fact: a label and a value, and optionally a description, a tooltip and an icon.

members.name: id
members.description: Stable identity. Without one the label and index stand in.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the fact.

members.name: value
members.description: A node, or a descriptor that names the fact's kind.

members.name: description
members.description: Supporting copy under the value.

members.name: tooltip
members.description:
Shown from an info trigger beside the label — for a fact that needs explaining. The
trigger is named after the label through `strings.formatInfoLabel` ("Amount info"), a
function rather than a suffix because word order differs by language.

members.name: icon
members.description: A glyph before the label.

members.name: emptyLabel
members.description: Shown when this fact's value is absent, in place of the list's `emptyLabel`.

members.name: render
members.description: Takes over the value entirely, for one fact that none of the kinds cover.

members.name: formatInfoLabel
members.description: The info trigger's accessible name, built from the label — a function because word order varies by language.

members.name: infoFallback
members.description: Used when the field's label is a node rather than a string.

props.name: data
props.description:
The figure and what surrounds it: id, label, value, and optionally valueType, currency,
change, sparkline, icon, subtitle, footer, trend. One shape for every metric surface.

props.name: variant
props.description: Structural only — every variant reads the same data.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Tints the `bordered` and `colored` variants. The kit's vocabulary, so never `danger` or
`default`.

props.name: showSparkline
props.description: Draws the sparkline. Off drops a part the surrounding surface already states.

props.name: showChange
props.description: Draws the change chip. Off drops a part the surrounding surface already states.

props.name: showIcon
props.description: Draws the icon. Off drops a part the surrounding surface already states.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Renders the variant's skeleton, which reserves the resolved tile's height so a grid does
not jump when data lands.

props.name: error
props.description: Renders the error state in place of the figure.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this block's own copy.

props.name: progress
props.description: `colored` only — 0–100, driving the segmented bar.

MetricChange.description: The movement against the comparison period.

MetricData.description:
One figure, for every metric surface: formatted once, and moved between surfaces by
changing the component alone.

members.name: id
members.description: Stable identity, for list keys.

members.name: value
members.description: `null` renders the empty marker rather than collapsing the tile.

members.name: valueType
members.description:
How `formatMetricValue` renders the figure. Currency shows the code rather than the
symbol, because an admin screen routinely shows several at once and "$" does not say
which dollar.

members.name: currency
members.description: ISO 4217, for `valueType: "currency"`.

members.name: sparkline
members.description: Points for the tile's sparkline, in chronological order.

members.name: tooltip
members.description: Behind an info affordance on the label line.

members.name: trend
members.description:
Overrides the trend the direction would imply. Set it for any metric where down is
the good direction.

MetricDataPoint.description: A named point on a time series.

MetricGradient.description:
The one metric on a page allowed to shout. Its ramps come from the categorical chart
palette, never the state tokens — a hero reports no success and no warning, and painting it
`--success` would repaint it whenever a consumer retunes the colour that means things went
right.

props.name: value
props.description: Already formatted — a hero figure is usually shaped by the page, not by a type hint.

props.name: variant
props.description: Forwarded to every cell.

props.name: columns
props.description: `auto` picks the break points from the cell count.

MetricMicroGrid.description:
Six dense cells, each pairing a figure with a different sketch — deliberately not six
sparklines, because when every cell draws the same shape a reader scanning the block has
nothing to tell them apart by except the label. One accent across the whole block: the
SHAPE is the differentiator, and a hue per cell adds a second, weaker one.

MetricSkeleton.description:
The placeholder a Metric shows while its figure is in flight, per variant — a single
generic block would be the wrong height for five of the seven, and the reflow that causes
is the thing a skeleton exists to avoid.

MetricTrendChip.description:
The delta beside a figure. Direction and tone are separate props on purpose: the direction
in `change` is a fact about the number, `trend` is a judgement about it, and for churn,
refunds or latency the two disagree. A chip that could only derive its colour from the
arrow would paint a rising error rate green.

props.name: trend
props.description: Overrides the tone the direction would imply.

members.name: value
members.description: Already formatted — this block draws the shape, it does not format figures.

members.name: chart
members.description: Pins the mark. Otherwise it follows the cell's position.

members.name: dueDate
members.description: Already formatted.

members.name: progress
members.description: 0–100. Drawn only while the milestone is in flight.

members.name: dueOn
members.description: Precedes the due date.

members.name: progressLabel
members.description: Names the progress bar for a screen reader.

props.name: milestones
props.description:
`status` is completed | inProgress | upcoming | blocked. `progress` is drawn only while
the milestone is in flight.

props.name: locale
props.description: Overrides the scope's locale for this value.

props.name: secondary
props.description:
A converted value shown beside the primary one. Passing it is the request for the pair:
the scope's policy can narrow that (`displayMode="primary-only"`) but never widen it,
and never invents a value.

props.name: displayMode
props.description: Whether the pair shows. `dynamic` shows it only when the two codes actually differ.

props.name: layout
props.description: Beside, or under. Falls back to the scope's `money.layout`.

props.name: secondaryEmphasis
props.description: How loud the second value is against the first.

props.name: separator
props.description:
Between the two, inline. A middle dot; pass an arrow for a conversion. It is
`aria-hidden`: read aloud, the mark between two amounts is punctuation for the eye.

props.name: amount
props.description:
The amount, in a channel separate from its currency. A number or a decimal string: a
single dot is decimal, and a grouped US or EU string is parsed by POSITION — whichever
of , or . appears last is the decimal point — so a value that came back through a
European locale does not parse a thousand times too large.

props.name: currency
props.description: The amount's ISO currency code, kept apart from the amount all the way to the render.

props.name: unit
props.description: The unit the amount ARRIVES in. Use `minor` for APIs that store integer minor units.

props.name: minorUnitScale
props.description: Minor units per major unit, for a currency whose exponent is not two.

props.name: formatMode
props.description:
How this amount is written. Falls back to the scope's `money.formatMode`, so
`UIProvider` defaults can change it.

MoneyConfig.description:
`UIConfig`'s `money` slice: the store's currency policy, decided once, so a call site
passes an amount and a conversion, never a policy.

members.name: defaultCurrency
members.description: Used when a `<Money>` is given no currency.

members.name: displayCurrency
members.description: A converted currency shown beside the primary one.

members.name: dualPricingEnabled
members.description: The master switch. Off, a `secondary` passed at a call site still renders.

members.name: displayMode
members.description:
Whether a second currency shows. `dynamic` shows it only when the two codes differ;
`dual` would print a price twice when they match.

members.name: layout
members.description: Where the second value sits: beside the first, or under it.

members.name: formatMode
members.description:
How an amount is written. `with-symbol` is Intl's own placement, which varies by locale
and currency.

MoneyInput.description:
The same field as `CurrencyInput`, taking a single `{ amount, currency }` object, for a form
that stores it that way: it cannot submit one without the other. The amount stays a
string — floats lose cents, and parsing is the caller's decision.

props.name: defaultCurrency
props.description: The starting currency code, for an uncontrolled field.

props.name: currencies
props.description:
Which codes the picker offers. Codes are looked up in `CURRENCY_SYMBOLS`; anything else
takes a full option.

props.name: currencyPosition
props.description: Which side the selector sits on.

props.name: disableCurrencySelector
props.description: Drops the currency selector, for an amount whose currency is decided elsewhere in the form.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this field's own copy. It extends the decimal strings, which extend the input
strings — a currency field is one of each, so it owns the selector's name, the two
steppers, and the clear action alike.

props.name: invalid
props.description: The error surface. The message stays on the `FormField`.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Glyph before the value, in its own lane so the text never runs under it.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Glyph after the value, in its own lane so the text never runs under it.

props.name: startAddon
props.description:
Short text attached before the value, outside the text itself — a currency symbol, a
protocol, an at sign.

props.name: endAddon
props.description: Short text attached after the value, outside the text itself — a unit, a domain.

props.name: showCharacterCount
props.description: Shows "12 / 80" in the trailing lane. Requires `maxLength`.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Character cap, and the limit the count counts against. Input past it is refused.

props.name: clearable
props.description:
Shows a clear control once the field has a value. Clearing goes through the native
value setter, so React's value tracker stays in sync.

props.name: onClear
props.description: Called after the clear control empties the field.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Replaces the trailing affordance with a spinner, which outranks every other trailing
affordance.

props.name: returnValueWithAddons
props.description:
Includes string addons in the value reported by `onChange`. Off, because an addon is
presentation: a caller that stores "$" and the number has to strip it again on the way
out.

props.name: decimalPlaces
props.description: How many digits after the separator are accepted, and used when normalising.

props.name: min
props.description: The lower bound.

props.name: max
props.description: The upper bound.

props.name: allowNegative
props.description: Accepts a minus sign.

props.name: allowEmpty
props.description: Lets the field be left blank: a blank is a valid value.

props.name: step
props.description: The increment: renders − / + buttons that snap the value to multiples of this.

props.name: roundingMode
props.description:
How halves are resolved when stepping or normalising. `half-even` (bankers' rounding)
avoids accumulating bias across many money rows.

props.name: normalizeOnBlur
props.description:
Rounds, pads to the full decimal places and clamps to the range when focus leaves.
Doing it per keystroke would fight the reader mid-number.

props.name: endAdornment
props.description:
A unit rendered after the field, inside the stepper group — wrapping a stepped field in
a second shell would double the border.

MonoValue.description:
Tabular figures and a mono face, for identifiers, hashes and SKUs — codes compared by eye,
down a column.

props.name: children
props.description: The value. `null`, `undefined` or an empty string renders the empty mark.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: Rendered when the value is absent.

props.name: truncate
props.description: Ellipsises the value at one line. Every flex box in the chain needs `min-width: 0` — see `Text`.

MonthYearPicker.description:
Month and year without a day grid, for a period rather than a date — a billing month, a
report window, an expiry. A day grid would imply a precision the value lacks.

props.name: disabledMonths
props.description: Refuses individual months — a period already closed, say.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this picker's own copy — the two year controls.

members.name: month
members.description: 0-indexed, as `Date` months are — so it can be handed straight to `setMonth`.

members.name: durations
members.description: Duration overrides, keyed without the `--duration-` prefix.

members.name: reduced
members.description: `true` forces motion off; unset respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

MultipleDatePicker.description: `DatePicker` with `mode="multiple"` fixed, so the value is always an array of dates.

props.name: id
props.description:
Applied to the trigger, the only labelable element. Its name comes from the chosen date,
so the field's label must reach it.

props.name: displayFormat
props.description: How the chosen value is written in the trigger: a date-fns pattern. The popup is unaffected.

props.name: invalid
props.description: The error surface. The message stays on the `FormField`.

props.name: clearable
props.description:
Adds a clear control to the trigger once something is chosen: a real button beside the
calendar glyph, named through `strings` — not an icon with a click handler.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this picker's own copy — the clear control and the calendar's captions. The
same object reaches the calendar inside the popup, so one override names the month
controls too.

props.name: presets
props.description:
Shortcuts down the side — "Last 30 days", "This month": the rail beside a range
calendar. `createRangePresets({ strings, weekStartsOn })` builds the built-in set in your
language and week.

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description:
How many months are shown side by side: two for a range, one otherwise. The header
becomes a range when more than one.

props.name: closeOnSelect
props.description:
Closes the popup as soon as a complete value is chosen. On by default for a single date
and off for a range, because a range is not chosen until both ends are.

props.name: header
props.description: A band above the calendar — a title, a mode switch. Use `DatePickerHeader`.

props.name: footer
props.description: A band below it — a summary, Clear and Apply. Use `DatePickerFooter`.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Styles the popup surface. `className` stays on the trigger.

props.name: minDate
props.description: Earliest selectable day, inclusive.

props.name: maxDate
props.description: Latest selectable day, inclusive.

props.name: disabledDates
props.description: Refuses individual days — weekends, holidays, days already booked.

MutedValue.description:
The same value two steps quieter, for incidental copy — present, but not something the
reader is meant to act on.

props.name: children
props.description: The value. `null`, `undefined` or an empty string renders the empty mark.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: Rendered when the value is absent.

props.name: truncate
props.description: Ellipsises the value at one line. Every flex box in the chain needs `min-width: 0` — see `Text`.

props.name: value
props.description: The whole name, however it was stored.

props.name: force
props.description:
Title-cases a name that already looks INTENTIONALLY cased. A name arriving all-shouting
or all-lowercase is re-cased without it — those two carry no intent to preserve. Off by
default, because a name is the one field where the stored casing is usually deliberate:
`force` is what overrides that judgement. Hyphens and apostrophes each take a capital
(jean-luc → Jean-Luc, o'brien → O'Brien); an intercap does not, so mcdonald becomes
Mcdonald — Mc, Mac and van der have no rule that is right for every name carrying them.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: Rendered when the value is absent.

props.name: truncate
props.description: Ellipsises the value at one line. Every flex box in the chain needs `min-width: 0` — see `Text`.

members.name: force
members.description: Title-case even when the value already looks intentionally cased.

NativeSelect.description:
The platform `<select>` on the same field surface as `Select`, for a short list, the native
picker on mobile, or a form that must post without JavaScript.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown as a disabled first option when the value is empty.

NavigationMenu.description:
Site navigation with rich panels, in a real `<nav>`. Not Menubar: a menubar commands the
current view, a navigation menu goes somewhere, and the difference decides whether the
items are buttons or links.

The bar, and the one panel every entry shares: each `NavigationMenuContent` is drawn into
its viewport, so moving between entries resizes one panel.

props.name: side
props.description:
Where the bar's one panel opens relative to the open entry. Set on the bar, because
every entry shares the panel: moving between entries resizes it rather than swapping it.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description: The gap between the open entry and the panel, in pixels.

props.name: align
props.description:
How the panel lines up with the open entry. At `start` it lines up with the entry's
start, so a panel under the first entry never hangs past the bar's own edge.

props.name: container
props.description: Where the panel renders. Defaults to the nearest `UIPortalHost`, else the primitive's own.

NavigationMenuContent.description:
One entry's panel content, drawn into the bar's shared panel while its entry is open.
Placement belongs to the panel, so it is set on `NavigationMenu`, not here.

NavigationMenuIndicator.description:
The caret inside a trigger. It tells an entry that opens a panel from a link that goes
somewhere, and turns over while its panel is open. Renders a chevron; children replace it.

NavigationMenuItem.description: One entry: a trigger with its panel content, or a link that goes straight somewhere.

NavigationMenuLink.description:
A destination inside a panel, or an entry of its own. A real anchor, so middle-click and
copy-link work and a screen reader announces a link.

NavigationMenuTrigger.description: The word that opens an entry's panel.

members.name: badge
members.description: Trailing content — a count, a dot.

NavigationTabs.description:
Tabs that navigate, so they render anchors in a `<nav>`, and the active one follows from
the current path. `Tabs` and `TabPanel` are for panels in one page; this is for routes,
and mixing the two is how a browser back button stops working.

props.name: items
props.description: The routes: each a `label` and an `href`, with an optional `icon`, `badge` or `disabled`.

props.name: currentPath
props.description: The current route. The active tab follows from this.

props.name: renderLink
props.description: Routes entries through the app's router. Without it they are plain anchors.

props.name: variant
props.description: `pill` draws the current route as a filled chip, as `TabList variant="pill"` does.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this row's own copy — the region name.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the navigation region. A page with two tab rows needs two names.

props.name: value
props.description: The number, drawn with locale grouping and tabular figures.

props.name: locale
props.description: Overrides the scope's locale for this value.

members.name: name
members.description: Key within each row object.

members.name: type
members.description: `textarea` for prose; `number` narrows the keyboard on a phone.

members.name: hint
members.description: A line under the field.

members.name: span
members.description: Fraction of the row this field takes, 1–12. Defaults to an even share.

ObjectRepeater.description:
A repeating row of several fields, described once as data rather than assembled per row
— contacts, line items, addresses. It reads and writes the array it is given and imports

OtpInput.description:
A one-time code, one box per character, on Base UI's OTPField, so paste and SMS autofill
fill every box.

(or a surrounding `FormField`) replaces it.

Tabs as data, in a row that scrolls rather than wrapping: wrapping onto a second line
changes the page's height as the reader switches. Renders through `Tabs`, or through
`NavigationTabs` — a `<nav>` of links — when every item has an `href`.

`disabled`. A tab with an `href` is a link; without one it is a button.

selects.

in a mixed set it stays tabs and the caller routes in `onValueChange`.

members.name: badge
