The region between the fixed header and footer, and the one that scrolls, so a long
surface never scrolls its own title or its buttons away.

OverlayClose.description:
Closes the overlay. Renders a bare button by default; `render` hands the behaviour to your
own control instead, so the close is a kit Button rather than something this module
styles.

props.name: render
props.description: The element this close control becomes — a kit Button, say; `children` stays its content.

members.name: backdropBlur
members.description:
Blur behind a modal's scrim, in px (a number) or any CSS length. Off by default: a
backdrop filter repaints everything behind the surface each frame.

members.name: darkMenus
members.description:
Dropdown and context menus render in the dark scheme whatever the page is. Default
`true`; `false` lets them follow the scheme they are portalled into, like other popups.
A config value, not a CSS switch: Firefox lacks CSS `if()`.

OverlayContent.description:
The surface, on a native `<dialog>`. `placement`, `modality` and `dismissal` make it a
dialog, a sheet or a drawer — there is no second component for the edge case. Popups
opened inside it render inside it, above it and reachable by keyboard.

props.name: placement
props.description:
Where the surface sits. Centre reads as a dialog, an edge as a sheet. DialogContent and
AlertDialogContent fix it to centre; SheetContent exposes it as `side`.

props.name: size
length
props.description:
Along-axis extent, for an edge placement. Less than full detaches the panel and centres
it on that axis. It is measured against the space the inset leaves rather than the
viewport: 70% of an inset panel is 70% of what is between the offsets, and the rest is
split between the two ends. Full needs no inset to look right, which is why a
corner-anchored sheet sets only `inset`.

props.name: inset
props.description:
The gap to the viewport edges. `false` is flush — a sheet welded to the side; `true`
uses the kit's gap; any CSS length sets your own. One offset, spent on every side the
panel does not run to, so an inset side panel sits the same distance from the top, the
side and the bottom. Any gap detaches it, rounds all four corners and gives it a full
border.

props.name: modality
props.description:
How much of the page the surface takes hostage: scrim, inert background and scroll
lock (`modal`), focus alone (`trap-focus`), or neither (`non-modal`).

props.name: surface
props.description: `bare` drops the region dividers, for content that draws its own chrome.

props.name: dismissal
props.description:
Each route out, separately. Off for a decision that must be answered, or for work in
progress. AlertDialogContent fixes both off.

props.name: initialFocusRef
props.description: Element to focus on open, instead of the first tabbable node.

props.name: showCloseButton
props.description: Renders the corner dismiss control. AlertDialogContent turns it off.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this surface's own copy — the corner dismiss control's name.

surface without one has none. Wraps bare strings the way OverlayTitle does.

OverlayDismissArea.description:
Wraps children so any button inside dismisses the overlay — for a footer whose every
control should close. Wrapping each button individually is where the wiring gets
forgotten. When only some actions should close, keep `<OverlayClose render={<Button />} />`
per action.

OverlayDismissal.description: The two routes out of an overlay, each switchable on its own.

members.name: backdrop

members.name: escape
members.description: Escape dismisses. Off for destructive or in-progress work.

control. It holds its edge while the body scrolls, so a long surface never scrolls its own

PillRadioGroup.description:
A compact single-select of connected pills, for two to four short options — a timeframe,
a view mode. A hidden input submits the value.

props.name: options
props.description:
The choices, in the one shape card, list and pill groups share. A pill shows no
description — it has no room for one.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value. `null` is the cleared state.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the chosen value, or `null` when the selection is cleared.

props.name: allowClear
props.description:
Lets the active pill be clicked again to clear the selection, for a filter whose empty
state is "all".

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretches the pills to fill the container, for a segmented control that owns its row.

props.name: name
props.description: Field name, used for the group's native form participation.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every option.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Applies the invalid treatment. Pair it with a message on the FormField.

props.name: aria-label
props.description:
The group's name and description. `FormField` supplies `aria-labelledby` and
`aria-describedby`.

members.name: description
members.description: Supporting sentence. Card and list groups show it; a pill has no room for one.

members.name: icon
members.description: Leading glyph. A Lucide icon, any component taking a className, or a rendered node.

members.name: tooltip
members.description:
Detail that doesn't fit the row, shown in a tooltip from an info glyph beside the label.
The glyph isn't focusable; the text also becomes the option's accessible description.

PlaceAutocomplete.description:
A text field that turns typing into places. It defaults to the free, key-less, rate-limited
Photon geocoder; set `searchUrl` for production.

props.name: searchUrl
props.description: Replaces the public, rate-limited Photon endpoint; anything answering Photon's GeoJSON works.

props.name: onResultsChange
props.description: Every result, whenever they change, e.g. for a map that pins them all.

props.name: bbox
props.description: [minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat]; results are restricted to it.

props.name: lat
props.description: Biases results toward a point rather than restricting them.

props.name: zoom
props.description: How local the bias is.

props.name: locationBiasScale
props.description: How strong it is.

members.name: loading
members.description: Announced while a lookup is in flight.

members.name: unknownPlace
members.description: For a result the geocoder returned with no name and no street.

PlaceholderPattern.description:
Diagonal hatching for a region with nothing in it yet — a chart with no data, a slot
awaiting an upload. It reads as deliberately empty; a blank box reads as broken. Not a
Skeleton, which says "loading".

Popover.description:
The root: holds the open state its trigger and panel share. `onOpenChange` receives Base
UI's `eventDetails`, which says what an outside interaction does: `eventDetails.reason` is
`"outside-press"`, and `eventDetails.cancel()` keeps the panel open through a click that
belongs to it.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Event handler called when the popover is opened or closed.

PopoverAnchor.description:
What the panel points at, when that is not what opens it: a panel opened by a toolbar
button but anchored to the selection it acts on, or opened by a row's menu and anchored
to the row.

props.name: render
props.description: The element this anchor becomes, in place of a `span`; `children` stays the content.

PopoverContent.description:
The panel. It sits against its anchor at `side` and `align`, and flips when the chosen
side has no room; `sideOffset` and `alignOffset` are the gap to the anchor along each
axis. `initialFocus` and `finalFocus`, from Base UI's popup, decide where focus lands on
open and returns on close; `false` leaves it where it is.

props.name: disablePortal
props.description:
Keeps the panel in place in the DOM. Portalling is the default because an ancestor
that clips or transforms would otherwise cut the panel off.

props.name: inset
props.description:
The panel's own inset. `flush` drops it for content that draws its own edges — a
calendar, a list that runs to the border.

props.name: width
props.description:
Surface width: a CSS length, `"trigger"` to match the control it opened from — what a
select-like panel wants — or `"auto"` to size to the content, capped by the space
actually available. Defaults to a fixed reading width. Same vocabulary as
DropdownMenuContent.

props.name: minWidth
props.description: Floor for the width.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Ceiling for `width="auto"`. Defaults to the space actually available.

props.name: container
props.description: Where the popup renders. Defaults to the nearest `UIPortalHost`, else the primitive's own.

props.name: initialFocus
props.type: boolean | React.RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((openType: InteractionType) => void | boolean | HTMLElement | null)
props.description:
Determines the element to focus when the popover is opened.
By default, focus moves to the first tabbable element inside the popup, except when the popover
is opened by touch — then the popup itself is focused to avoid opening the virtual keyboard.

props.name: finalFocus
props.type: boolean | React.RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType: InteractionType) => void | boolean | HTMLElement | null)
props.description: Determines the element to focus when the popover is closed.

props.name: side
props.description:
Which side of the anchor element to align the popup against.
May automatically change to avoid collisions.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description:
Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the distance to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

props.name: align
props.description: How to align the popup relative to the specified side.

props.name: alignOffset
props.description:
Additional offset along the alignment axis in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the offset to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

PopoverDescription.description: Supporting text, wired to the panel's accessible description.

PopoverFooter.description: The band at the bottom of the panel, for its actions.

PopoverHeader.description: The band at the top of the panel, for its title and description.

PopoverMenu.description:
A "trigger → optional header → search → list" picker: filter facets, operator selects,
assignee menus. For other shapes compose `Popover` and `Command`; inside a surface
something else owns, render `PopoverMenuPanel`.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The clickable the popover anchors to.

props.name: items
props.description:
The choices. Each carries a `value`, a `label`, and optional media — an `icon`, a
`description`.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Receives the chosen item. The menu does not own a persistent selection.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled openness, for a menu opened from somewhere other than its trigger.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the next open state. Pair with `open`.

props.name: search
props.description: Shows the search field above the list.

props.name: searchValue
props.description:
Controlled search value. Supplying `onSearchChange` also hands filtering to the
caller: the local matcher turns off. `strings.searchPlaceholder` is the field's
placeholder.

props.name: onSearchChange
props.description:
Called with the search text. Supplying it hands filtering to the caller — the local
matcher steps aside rather than filtering an already filtered list.

props.name: minSearchLength
props.description:
Characters the search needs before rows show, measured on the trimmed text, controlled
or not. An empty field still shows `items`; from one character up to the minimum,
`strings.formatTypeToSearch(minimum)` shows instead.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Puts a strip in place of the list while results are in flight — an async picker with no
state reads as an empty one.

props.name: error
props.description:
The items could not be loaded: `true` shows `strings.error`, any other node is the
message. Replaces the rows and the empty state, and gives way to `loading`.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Wiring this puts a retry control, labelled by `strings.retry`, under the error.

props.name: header
props.description: Band above the search field, running edge to edge.

props.name: footer
props.description: Band below the list, running edge to edge — confirm and clear buttons.

props.name: closeOnSelect
props.description:
Closes the popover after a row is chosen and returns focus to the trigger. True unless
a `footer` is present: a footer holds confirm and clear actions, which is the
multi-pick shape.

props.name: empty
props.description:
Shown when nothing matches, as a rendered node; for plain copy, use `strings.empty`.
Required in spirit: a filter that matches nothing has to say so.

props.name: loadingSlot
props.description: Replaces the default spinner strip.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this menu's own copy — the filter placeholder, the loading, empty and error rows.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Replaces a row, for an option carrying an avatar or a colour.

props.name: align
props.description: How the surface lines up with the trigger.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description: Gap between the trigger and the surface, in pixels.

props.name: label
props.description:
Names the list, and the search field when there is one. Most needed with
`search={false}`, where the list itself is what focus lands on.

props.name: className
props.description: Class for the popover surface.

members.name: searchValue

members.name: data
members.description: Arbitrary payload handed back to `onSelect`.

PopoverMenuPanel.description:
The body of a `PopoverMenu` (header, search, rows, footer) without the popover, for a
surface something else owns: one step of a two-step popup, a sheet on a phone. The panel
owns no selection and closes nothing — the surface hosting it decides both.

One state shows at a time, in this order of precedence: a query shorter than
`minSearchLength`, then `loading`, then `error`, then the rows. Enter, the arrows, Home
and End pressed in a band or on the retry control stay there instead of reaching the
list.

props.name: items
props.description:
The choices. Each carries a `value`, a `label`, and optional media — an `icon`, a
`description`.

props.name: onSelect

props.name: search
props.description:
Shows the search field above the list. Without it the list is the tab stop — a listbox
pointing at the highlighted row — so the arrows and Enter work in a host whose own
initial focus lands on the first tabbable element.

caller: the local matcher turns off.

matcher steps aside rather than filtering an already filtered list.

state reads as an empty one.

Required in spirit: a filter that matches nothing has to say so.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides the panel's own copy — the filter placeholder, the loading, empty and error rows.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Replaces a row, for an option carrying an avatar or a colour.

props.name: label
props.description:
Names the list, and the search field when there is one. Most needed with
`search={false}`, where the list itself is what focus lands on. The filter editors

props.name: ref
props.description:
The list element. Without a search field it is the tab stop, and what a host's

props.name: className

PopoverMenuStrings.description:
The copy of a `PopoverMenu` or `PopoverMenuPanel`. `error`, `retry` and
`formatTypeToSearch` are optional in the type, so a translation written before them still
compiles; the defaults fill them.

members.name: loading
members.description: Announced while the items are being fetched.

members.name: searchPlaceholder
members.description: Placeholder in the filter field.

members.name: empty
members.description: Shown when the filter matches nothing.

members.name: error
members.description: Shown in place of the rows when `error` is `true`.

members.name: retry
members.description: Labels the retry control under the error, when `onRetry` is wired.

PopoverTitle.description:
The panel's heading, wired to its accessible name. Without a title and description the
panel announces as an unnamed group.

PopoverTrigger.description:
What opens the panel. It is separate from `PopoverAnchor`, so a toolbar button can open a
panel anchored to the thing it acts on.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description:
Whether the element the trigger renders is a real `<button>`. Inferred from `render`
when omitted: an element with an `href` is not, so a link keeps its semantics.

PreviewImage.description:
A thumbnail for a file that has not been uploaded yet, or any image, that falls back to a
glyph rather than the browser's broken-image mark when it fails to load.

props.name: alt
props.description: Empty by default: a thumbnail beside its own filename is decorative.

PreviewTriggerCell.description:
The trigger, shaped for a table cell. It is a button only when there is something to open;
otherwise the same text renders inert.

props.name: value
props.description: The cell's own text.

props.name: secondary
props.description: Second line, quieter.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: Shown when `value` is absent — the em dash, unless a column wants its own word.

props.name: hasPreview
props.description:
Whether this row has a preview at all. Off renders an inert span with the same text and
rhythm, and no caret, pointer or popup ARIA.

props.name: disabledReason
props.description: Why it is unavailable. Shown as a tooltip on the inert cell.

props.name: asName
props.description: Runs the value through `Name` to normalise casing.

ProductContractOverview.description: The contract a product sells under: its metrics, its terms, and its rules.

props.name: terms
props.description:
The contract's facts. They go through MetadataList, so an email or an SKU is rendered by
the kind that knows how; this module does not restate it.

props.name: metricColumns
props.description: How wide the metric row is allowed to get. Drop it for a card in a rail.

ProductDetailsCard.description:
The facts that identify a product. With ProductPoliciesCard, one of the two remaining cards
a product page is assembled from: each a ContentBlock with a list inside and the same four
verbs on every row.

props.name: description
props.description:
`false` suppresses the default description rather than rendering it empty — which is the
difference between a card with no subtitle and a card with a blank line where one was.

ProductEmptyState.description:
What a product card shows with nothing in it, sized to the card rather than to the page — a
full-page empty state inside a half-width card reads as a broken layout.

ProductOperationRow.description:
An operation's row, with a value in the trailing lane. Three cards, one row shape: the rows
differ only in what sits in the trailing lane — a badge, a number, a value — so there is one
row component and three wrappers rather than four near-identical ones.

ProductOptionActionMenu.description:
The per-option overflow menu, exported for screens that lay out options themselves and
want the same verbs and labels as the summary card. Built from one array, so the overflow
cannot offer what the button already does.

members.name: usedForVariants
members.description: Whether this option takes part in generating variants.

ProductOptionsMatrix.description:
The option groups a product's variants are generated from: one card with ruled rows, because
the options are one ordered list. The whole row is the edit target, and the editor replaces
it in place.

props.name: confirmDelete
props.description:
Asks before removing an option. Removing an option removes every variant generated from it
— which is not visible from the option's own row. Off when the app already confirms, so
nobody is asked twice.

props.name: onValueLabelChange
props.type: (option: ProductOptionGroup, value: ProductOptionValue, label: string) => void

props.name: onSaveEditingOption
props.description:
The staged name and values, committed together. Cancel discards them; the draft is
re-seeded from the option each time editing opens, so a cancelled edit cannot leak into the
next one.

props.name: onReorderOptions
props.description: Enables the grip. Without it the list keeps its order and shows no handle.

ProductPoliciesCard.description:
What the customer agrees to. With ProductDetailsCard, one of the two remaining cards a
product page is assembled from: each a ContentBlock with a list inside and the same four
verbs on every row.

members.name: emphasis
members.description:
Rules the line off and weights it: the line the rest add up to. Not a tint — a filled band
on the last line makes a total look like an alert, which is the one thing a total is not.

ProductReadinessCard.description:
What a product still needs before it is ready: a score and the checks behind it. One of the
cards a product page is assembled from, each a ContentBlock holding a list with the same row
verbs.

props.name: score
props.description:
0–100, clamped — a percentage bar cannot show 140, and a NaN would render as an empty
track.

props.name: renderItem
props.description:
Replaces a whole row. The rows are one component with three wrappers, so a consumer
replacing one is replacing the same shape everywhere it appears.

ProductReadinessCardStrings.description: Products copy: one strings object per surface, since the cards are used independently.

members.name: tone
members.description:
The row's state colour: `neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive` or
`info`. No `secondary`: it means “not this one”, which is not a state a product can be in.
An item that is `completed` with no tone derives success, so ticking a box does not also
mean remembering the colour.

ProductReadinessRow.description:
A readiness check's row, with a badge in the trailing lane. Three cards, one row shape: the
rows differ only in what sits in the trailing lane — a badge, a number, a value — so there is
one row component and three wrappers rather than four near-identical ones.

ProductRowActions.description:
A row's verbs, built from one array so the overflow cannot offer what the button already
does. Three menus rather than one — this, ProductVariantActionMenu and
ProductOptionActionMenu — because a variant, an option and a row answer to different sets.

ProductStructureMetricRow.description:
A structure metric's row, with the number in the trailing lane. Three cards, one row shape: the
rows differ only in what sits in the trailing lane — a badge, a number, a value — so there is one
row component and three wrappers rather than four near-identical ones.

ProductSummaryRow.description:
An option's or a policy's row, on the same row shape as the readiness, structure and
operations rows, which differ only in what sits in the trailing lane.

ProductSurface.description:
How ProductOptionsMatrix and ProductVariantsBulkTable draw their frame: `card` frames the
surface; `embedded` renders it bare inside one that already exists.

ProductThumbnail.description:
A variant's picture, or a dashed slot where one would go (a grey square reads as a
failed image). Only a button with `onSelect`; otherwise the slot is inert and muted. One of
the pieces every product surface shares.

props.name: media
props.description: Replaces the image entirely: a video still, a swatch, a monogram.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the slot when it is pressable.

ProductToneDot.description:
A row's state as a dot. One of the pieces every product surface shares: tone is a data
attribute rather than six class names, so a row's state is one string in the DOM and the CSS
reads it once.

ProductVariantActionMenu.description:
A variant's verbs, built from one array so the overflow cannot offer what the button already
does. A separate menu from an option's or a row's, because each answers to a different set.

members.name: columns
members.type: { variant: string; sku: string; price: string; inventory: string; channels: string; status: string; updated: string; actions: string; }

members.name: actions
members.description: Names the trailing menu column for screen readers; it shows no caption.

ProductVariantCell.description:
A label/value pair that survives losing its table: the label is screen-reader-only while a
column heading names the value, and becomes visible below the md breakpoint, where the table
collapses and the headings are gone. One of the pieces every product surface shares.

ProductVariantDetails.description:
One variant, read-only: what it is, what it costs, and which options it stands for. `variant`
is optional because the panel is also what a page shows before one is chosen. Facts derive
from the variant's own fields; `metadata` replaces them.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Optional. Absent renders the empty state — this panel is usually bound to a selection, and
“nothing chosen yet” is a thing to say, not a reason to unmount.

props.name: metadata
props.description: Replaces the derived facts. The default is built from the variant's own fields.

members.name: metadata
members.type: { price: string; inventory: string; sku: string; channels: string; updated: string; }

ProductVariantEditor.description:
The variant form. Values stay strings — the consumer parses on submit — so "24.00" is never
rewritten under the cursor.

props.name: optionFields
props.description:
A select when the field carries choices, a text input when it does not — an app with a
free-text status should not have to invent a list to use this.

props.name: onError
props.description: Receives a rejected submit. Persistence and the message stay with the consumer.

props.name: submitting
props.description:
Shows the pending state and blocks a repeat submit. OR-ed with an internal flag: a
consumer holding the request already knows it is in flight; one that just handed over an
async `onSubmit` does not, and a form that stays live during a save takes the same submit
twice.

members.name: fields
members.type: { name: string; description: string; sku: string; price: string; inventory: string; status: string; channels: string; }

members.name: placeholders
members.type: { name: string; description: string; sku: string; price: string; inventory: string; status: string; channels: string; }

ProductVariantEditorValues.description: Every field is a string: this is a form, and a form's value is what was typed.

members.name: options
members.description: Keyed by option group id.

members.name: value
members.description: Overrides the value held under this field's id.

members.name: choices
members.description: With choices it is a select; without, a text field.

members.name: optionValues
members.description: Rendered value per option group id, shown in the combination column.

members.name: optionValueIds
members.description: The chosen value's id per option group, for grouping rows by an option.

members.name: image
members.description: The variant's picture. Absent draws the empty slot.

members.name: media
members.description: Replaces the image entirely: a swatch, a video still, a monogram.

members.name: image
members.description: The variant's picture. Absent draws the empty slot.

members.name: media
members.description: Replaces the image entirely: a swatch, a video still, a monogram.

ProductVariantsManager.description:
The options and the variants they generate, in one card: the variant grid is a
consequence of the options above it. The grouping control sits between the two halves
because it is a question about the options that changes the grid.

props.name: groupByOptionId
props.description:
Controlled grouping: groups rows under that option's values, in the order the option
declares them — not alphabetically, and not by whichever variant was created first. `null`
leaves the list flat. Uncontrolled, the manager's own Select drives it.

props.name: showGroupBy
props.description: Hides the grouping control, for a surface that drives it from elsewhere.

props.name: optionsStrings
props.description:
The option matrix's own copy. The two children keep their own copy objects: one merged bag
would collide on title, description and the create labels, which both of them have.

props.name: variantsStrings
props.description:
The variant table's own copy, kept apart from `optionsStrings` because both children have a
title, a description and create labels.

props.name: confirmDelete
props.description:
Asks before removing an option. Removing an option removes every variant generated from it
— which is not visible from the option's own row. Off when the app already confirms, so
nobody is asked twice.

props.name: onValueLabelChange
props.type: (option: ProductOptionGroup, value: ProductOptionValue, label: string) => void

props.name: onSaveEditingOption
props.description:
The staged name and values, committed together. Cancel discards them; the draft is
re-seeded from the option each time editing opens, so a cancelled edit cannot leak into the
next one.

props.name: onReorderOptions
props.description: Enables the grip. Without it the list keeps its order and shows no handle.

props.name: cellDisplay
props.description:
`text` or `field`, for every editable field or per field, so a table can make price
editable and leave stock read-only — which is what a price update run actually needs.

props.name: onVariantFieldChange
props.type: (variant: ProductVariantRow, field: ProductVariantEditableField, value: string, context: ProductVariantFieldChangeContext) => void
props.description:
Fires on every edit of an in-place field. Both this and `onVariantFieldBlur` exist, and the
consumer picks: change alone makes every keystroke a state update; blur alone loses the
value if the row is removed mid-edit.

props.name: onVariantFieldBlur
props.type: (variant: ProductVariantRow, field: ProductVariantEditableField, value: string, context: ProductVariantFieldChangeContext) => void
props.description:
Fires when an in-place field loses focus. Blur alone loses the value if the row is removed
mid-edit; pair it with `onVariantFieldChange` where that matters.

props.name: renderBulkActions
props.description:
Replaces the default pair of bulk actions. The context carries the selected rows, the
counts, and both `clearSelection` and `setSelectedIds`, so a custom bar can act and then
deselect.

Progress.description:
A `progressbar` with its real bounds. Omit `value` for indeterminate; the ARIA value
attributes are then dropped rather than reporting 0%.

props.name: value
props.description: 0–`max`. Non-finite values resolve to 0. Omit for indeterminate.

props.name: max
props.description: A finite positive upper bound; invalid values resolve to 100.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Semantic colour intent. Left unset the bar takes the primary tone — a progress bar that
changes colour at a threshold is the caller's decision, not the component's.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name. Required when no visible label describes the bar.

ProgressCircle.description:
A determinate ring with the reading inside it, for tiles, scores and grids of small
measures. Its size comes from `--progress-circle`; there is no size prop.

props.name: value
props.description:
0–`max`. Non-finite values resolve to 0; overflow fills rather than wrapping. There is
no indeterminate ring: a travelling band reads as unknown, a spinning circle reads as a
spinner.

props.name: max
props.description: A finite positive upper bound; invalid values resolve to 100.

props.name: tone
props.description: Semantic colour intent, as on `Progress`.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name. Required when no visible label describes the ring.

props.name: children
props.description:
What sits in the hole — a percentage, a count, a verdict glyph. The reason to draw a
ring at all.

props.name: value
props.description:
What the code encodes — a URL, a payment string, a token. An empty value renders
`emptyState`, or nothing at all when there is none.

props.name: foreground
props.description:
Overrides the dark modules. Defaults to the inverse background, dark in both themes.
Any CSS colour; it is converted to hex for the encoder.

props.name: background
props.description:
Overrides the light modules. Defaults to the inverse foreground, light in both themes.
Any CSS colour; it is converted to hex for the encoder.

props.name: robustness
props.description:
Error correction: how much of the symbol can be obscured and still decode — L ≈ 7%,
M ≈ 15%, Q ≈ 25%, H ≈ 30%. Higher needs a denser grid.

props.name: placeholder
props.description:
Shown while encoding. Defaults to this component's own `generating` string; a value
that cannot be encoded shows `strings.failed` instead.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this code's own copy — the two placeholder states and its name.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Shown when `value` is empty. Defaults to rendering nothing (it is not a loading state).

props.name: label
props.description: Announced in place of the symbol, which is meaningless to a screen reader.

QRCodeStrings.description: A QR code's copy: its pending and failed states, and the symbol's accessible name.

members.name: generating
members.description: While the symbol is being generated.

members.name: failed
members.description: When the value cannot be encoded at all.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the rendered symbol, by the value it encodes.

props.name: value
props.description: The count.

props.name: unit
props.description:
The noun, in the forms the locale may need — one, other, and the zero, two, few and
many some languages select. A bare string is used for every form.

props.name: zeroLabel
props.description:
Replaces the whole thing at zero — "no items" rather than "0 items". Off by default: in
a column the zero is the value being reported.

Radio.description:
One option: a native radio under the kit's styling. `checked` and `defaultChecked` are
its controlled and uncontrolled selection, and the group supplies the shared `name`.
`onChange` receives the native input event: read `event.target.value` for the selected
value.

props.name: label
props.description: Rendered beside the circle and wired to it, so the text is part of the target.

RadioGroup.description: Radios that exclude each other. The group supplies the shared `name` that does it.

props.name: name
props.description:
Groups the options: shared across every radio inside, which is what makes them
exclusive. A native radio group needs it to behave as one.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The direction the options run in.

props.name: from
props.description:
The low end. One end alone still renders — "from £10", with the caller's copy around
the value.

props.name: to
props.description: The high end. One end alone still renders, with the caller's copy around the value.

props.name: currency
props.description:
An ISO currency code. Renders the range as money: Intl repeats the symbol on both ends,
which is its considered answer to the ambiguity a single symbol creates.

props.name: unit
props.description:
A CSS-style unit identifier — `kilogram`, `day`. Renders the range with its unit.
Ignored when `currency` is set.

props.name: maximumFractionDigits
props.description: Caps the decimals on both ends.

RangeDatePicker.description: `DatePicker` with `mode="range"` fixed, so the value is always a `{ from, to }`.

props.name: id
props.description:
Applied to the trigger, the only labelable element. Its name comes from the chosen date,
so the field's label must reach it.

props.name: displayFormat
props.description: How the chosen value is written in the trigger: a date-fns pattern. The popup is unaffected.

props.name: invalid
props.description: The error surface. The message stays on the `FormField`.

props.name: clearable
props.description:
Adds a clear control to the trigger once something is chosen: a real button beside the
calendar glyph, named through `strings` — not an icon with a click handler.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this picker's own copy — the clear control and the calendar's captions. The
same object reaches the calendar inside the popup, so one override names the month
controls too.

props.name: presets
props.description:
Shortcuts down the side — "Last 30 days", "This month": the rail beside a range
calendar. `createRangePresets({ strings, weekStartsOn })` builds the built-in set in your
language and week.

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description:
How many months are shown side by side: two for a range, one otherwise. The header
becomes a range when more than one.

props.name: closeOnSelect
props.description:
Closes the popup as soon as a complete value is chosen. On by default for a single date
and off for a range, because a range is not chosen until both ends are.

props.name: header
props.description: A band above the calendar — a title, a mode switch. Use `DatePickerHeader`.

props.name: footer
props.description: A band below it — a summary, Clear and Apply. Use `DatePickerFooter`.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Styles the popup surface. `className` stays on the trigger.

props.name: minDate
props.description: Earliest selectable day, inclusive.

props.name: maxDate
props.description: Latest selectable day, inclusive.

props.name: disabledDates
props.description: Refuses individual days — weekends, holidays, days already booked.

RangeFilterEditor.description:
The editor for a `range` filter: a minimum, and a maximum for `between`. It stages the
bounds and commits them on Apply.

props.name: triggerSource
props.description: Only a toolbar-opened editor has a list to go back to.

props.name: value
props.description: The score. Shown to at most one decimal, so 4 stays 4.

props.name: max
props.description: The top of the scale. Five unless said otherwise, which is the common instrument.

props.name: hideMax
props.description:
Hides the scale, leaving the score alone.

For a surface that states the scale elsewhere — a column headed "Rating / 5", or a
row of stars that already shows it. Not the default, because "4.5" on its own is a
number a reader has to guess the meaning of.

props.name: strings
props.description: The connector — "out of".

members.name: outOf
members.description: Joins the score to the scale. "4.5 out of 5".

props.name: value
props.description: The count.

props.name: total
props.description: What the value is counted against. Without it the component renders the value alone.

props.name: format
props.description: `words` reads "3 of 10" (prose); `fraction` reads "3/10" (tables).

props.name: strings
props.description: The connectors — "of", and the fraction separator.

members.name: of
members.description: Joins the two numbers. "3 of 10".

members.name: fraction
members.description: The separator for `format="fraction"`.

RelativeTime.description:
"3 days ago" — for recency, where the exact timestamp is not the point. The precise
value stays available in the title attribute.

props.name: now
props.description:
The moment to measure against. Defaults to the clock.

Supply it wherever the render has to be reproducible — a server render whose
markup must match the client's, a test asserting the string, a visual snapshot.
Reading the clock inside the component makes all three of those flaky, and it
does not buy a live value in exchange: nothing re-renders it as time passes.

props.name: addSuffix
props.description:
"7 days ago" rather than "7 days". On by default, because a bare duration beside a
row of dates reads as a length rather than a moment.

props.name: includeSeconds
props.description:
Distinguishes "less than a minute" from "30 seconds". Only worth it for a feed measured
in seconds.

props.name: formatRelativeTime
props.description:
Replaces the wording for this one value. Falls back to the scope's
`dates.formatRelativeTime`, and then to date-fns, whose built-in wording the scope's
`dates.locale` translates: a date-fns locale OBJECT, since the locales are modules and
cannot be looked up from a BCP-47 tag without putting every language in every bundle.

props.name: value
props.description:
The moment to show: whatever the API returned — a Date, an ISO string or an epoch
number. Parsed once, here.

Repeater.description:
The chrome every list-style field shares: rows with an optional drag handle and remove
control, an empty state, and an add button. It never owns the array — you pass `items`
and the handlers, which keeps it usable with a form library or with plain state.

props.name: items
props.description: The rows. The repeater renders what it is given and nothing else.

props.name: getKey
props.description:
Stable identity per row. An index alone would re-key every row after a reorder and
lose focus.

props.name: children
props.description: Renders one row. `context` carries the row's `index` and whether it is `dragging`.

props.name: onAdd
props.description: Supplying it renders the add button.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Supplying it renders each row's remove button.

props.name: onMove
props.description:
Supplying it enables reordering and renders the drag handle; without it, no handle is
rendered. The handle is the drag source, not the row.

props.name: rowVariant
props.description: `card` wraps each row in a bordered surface, for multi-field rows.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this list's own copy — the add control and each row's remove. `remove` is a
function of the row index: every remove button in a list saying the same thing is a
column of controls a screen reader cannot tell apart.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Shown in place of the rows when `items` is empty. Replaces `strings.emptyState`.

props.name: showAdd
props.description:
Hides the add button while keeping the rows — for a list at its cap, a fixed set of
rows, or one whose entries come from elsewhere.

props.name: maxItems
props.description: Caps the list. The add button disables at the limit.

members.name: add
members.description: The control that appends a row.

members.name: moved
members.description:
Announced after a keyboard move. Optional so older complete strings objects still
type-check.

members.name: remove
members.description: Names each row's remove control, by its row.

members.name: reorder
members.description: Names the drag handle, including how to move it by keyboard.

members.name: emptyState
members.description:
Shown when the list is empty; the `emptyState` prop replaces it. Optional so older
complete strings objects still type-check.

ResizableHandle.description:
The grip between two panels: a real `role="separator"`. It is focusable and takes arrow
keys, so the split is adjustable without a pointer.

props.name: withHandle
props.description:
Draws a grip on the line, for a split with no other cue that it moves. The hit area is
wider than the 1px rule either way.

ResizablePanelGroup.description:
The split. `orientation` is its axis. Own the persistence: keep the layout in your state
with `onLayoutChanged` and hand it back through `defaultLayout`, so a reader who widened a
panel finds it wide next time.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Specifies the resizable orientation ("horizontal" or "vertical"); defaults to "horizontal"

ResolvedUIConfig.description: A config with every JS-side decision resolved. Token slices stay partial by design.

members.name: backdropBlur
members.description:
Blur behind a modal's scrim, in px (a number) or any CSS length. Off by default: a
backdrop filter repaints everything behind the surface each frame.

members.name: darkMenus
members.description:
Dropdown and context menus render in the dark scheme whatever the page is. Default
`true`; `false` lets them follow the scheme they are portalled into, like other popups.
A config value, not a CSS switch: Firefox lacks CSS `if()`.

members.name: scale
members.description:
Type-only override (`--text-scale`): multiplies every `--text-*` role, control labels
included, without changing geometry. Unset, type follows `scale`.

members.name: defaultTextSize
members.description:
Size components fall back to when they set none. 14px, not 16px: `base` is a deliberate
step up for a dense surface.

members.name: fonts
members.description: Font stack overrides.

members.name: sizes
members.description: Per-step size overrides, keyed without the `--text-` prefix.

members.name: money
members.description: `displayCurrency` stays optional: having none is the ordinary case, not a gap.

members.name: defaultCurrency
members.description: Used when a `<Money>` is given no currency.

members.name: displayCurrency
members.description: A converted currency shown beside the primary one.

members.name: dualPricingEnabled
members.description: The master switch. Off, a `secondary` passed at a call site still renders.

members.name: displayMode
members.description:
Whether a second currency shows. `dynamic` shows it only when the two codes differ;
`dual` would print a price twice when they match.

members.name: layout
members.description: Where the second value sits: beside the first, or under it.

members.name: formatMode
members.description:
How an amount is written. `with-symbol` is Intl's own placement, which varies by locale
and currency.

members.name: dates
members.description: `locale` and `formatRelativeTime` stay optional: English is built in.

members.name: weekStartsOn
members.description: First day of the week in calendars and pickers. 0 = Sunday.

members.name: format
members.description: date-fns pattern the date primitives fall back to.

members.name: timeFormat
members.description: date-fns pattern for a time of day. `"p"` uses the locale's own convention.

members.name: locale
members.description:
The date-fns Locale OBJECT — what actually translates month and weekday names, and the
built-in relative-time wording. It cannot be derived from a BCP-47 tag such as
`formatting.locale`: the locales are modules, and importing all of them to look one up
would put every language in every bundle, so the consumer imports the one it needs.

members.name: formatRelativeTime
members.description: Replaces the relative-time wording ("7 days ago", "in 2 hours").

members.name: theme
members.description: Radius, colour, palette and custom-property overrides.

members.name: motion
members.description: Duration overrides, and motion forced off.

members.name: forms
members.description: Form-control behaviour: the iPhone zoom guard.

members.name: defaults
members.description: Per-component prop defaults, keyed by family and merged over each component's own.

ResourceActionBar.description:
The verb row of an index or show screen, for a page that wants the shell's rhythm without its
whole frame.

props.name: children
props.description: Leading content, when `leading` is not given.

props.name: leading
props.description: Filters, a selection summary, the controls that act on the body.

props.name: sticky
props.description:
Pins the bar below the shell header, not the viewport top, as the body scrolls — for a bar
carrying a selection count or bulk actions, which is needed exactly when a static bar has
scrolled away.

ResourceCombobox.description:
A self-fetching picker: give it a `fetcher` and it owns debounce, abort and the race guard.
Browsable from the first keystroke, and preloaded on mount so the list is there on open. A
failed fetch replaces the list content, as `AsyncCombobox`'s `showListContent` does when
off, but keeps the selection and the query, for retry.

props.name: fetcher
props.description:
Fetches the options for a query. Debounce, abort, and the race guard are owned for you,
and the query arrives trimmed. Honour `signal`, so an abort does not surface as a failure.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled. Omit entirely to let the component own the selection.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The starting selection when uncontrolled. Ignored once `value` is passed.

props.name: searchValue
props.description: The query. Controlled (e.g. from the URL); omit to let the component own it.

props.name: defaultSearchValue
props.description: The starting query when uncontrolled.

props.name: onSearchValueChange
props.description: Every keystroke, with the raw untrimmed value.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: The popup's starting state when `open` is not controlled.

props.name: clearSearchOnClose
props.description: Clears the query when the popup closes. Defaults to `false`. A failed query is always kept for retry.

props.name: requestDelay
props.description:
A further wait before the fetcher runs, after the loading state is showing. For
rate-limited endpoints: the reader sees something is happening, and the request that
would have been refused is never made.

props.name: onError
props.description: Aborted and superseded requests never reach this.

props.name: getKey
props.description: Stable identity. Also decides which option reads as selected.

props.name: getDescription
props.description: Second line beside the label — what distinguishes two rows of one name.

props.name: getMeta
props.description: Third, quieter still.

props.name: renderOption
props.description: Replaces the whole option row. `getLabel` still supplies the input's text.

props.name: minSearchLength
props.description: Characters required before fetching. Defaults to `0` (unlike `AsyncCombobox`'s `3`); an empty input follows `preload`.

props.name: preload
props.description:
Fetches with an empty query as the popup opens, without waiting out the debounce, so
there is something to look at before typing. Off, an empty field asks the reader to type
instead of claiming there are no results.

props.name: id
props.description: Applied to the search input (not a wrapper), so a `FormField` label can target it.

props.name: portalContainer
props.description: Mounts the popup inside this element instead of the default portal root.

props.name: onSearch
props.description:
The server query: fires after `debounceMs` with the trimmed value, only at or above
`minSearchLength`. To clear results below the threshold, use `onSearchValueChange`.

props.name: debounceMs
props.description: The quiet period before `onSearch` fires, in milliseconds.

props.name: creatable
props.description: Offers an inline create row when nothing matches. Needs `onCreate` to do anything.

props.name: onCreate
props.description:
Receives the create row's text: a created entry arrives here, not as a selection. The row
is withheld while nothing is typed, below `minSearchLength`, and when the text matches an
existing label case-insensitively.

props.name: getItemGroup
props.description: Returns a group name per item. Absent means no grouping.

props.name: hasMore
props.description: Enables scroll-triggered pagination.

props.name: onLoadMore
props.description:
Asks for the next page once the list is scrolled 80% of the way down. A cooldown after
each request stops a second page being asked for while the first is in flight — the list
has not grown, so the scroll position is still past the threshold.

props.name: loadingMore
props.description: Shows that the next page is loading, and holds off asking for another.

props.name: getItemDisabled
props.description: Renders an option unselectable without hiding it.

props.name: highlightMatch
props.description: Emphasises the matched substring. Ignored when `renderItem` is set.

props.name: metadata
props.description:
Structured facts, before any free-form body content. `metadataColumns` is a ceiling; the
list steps down at narrow widths on its own.

props.name: metadataColumns
props.description: A ceiling. The list steps down at narrow widths on its own.

props.name: body
props.description: Structured content after the facts.

props.name: help
props.description: Quiet guidance after everything else.

props.name: headerEnd
props.description: Controls at the end of the title line.

props.name: titleSuffix
props.description: After the title, on the same line: a badge, a count.

props.name: footer
props.description: After the body.

props.name: padding
props.description: Inner spacing: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: surface
props.description: A ContentBlock surface. `plain` when this sits inside a frame that already has chrome.

ResourceEmptyState.description:
One of the three states the shells swap in for content. Loading, error and empty are
replacements rather than overlays — they take the space the content will take, so nothing
reflows when it arrives.

props.name: media
props.description: Icon or illustration: the visual.

props.name: mediaVariant
props.description:
The media's chrome. `none` renders the media raw; `icon` and `icon-soft` set a glyph in
a tile; `illustration` centres it with room below.

props.name: renderMedia
props.description: Media as a function of the variant, for a visual that changes with its chrome.

props.name: title
props.description:
Names the absence: "No invoices yet", not "Nothing here". Falls back to `strings.title`,
so a bare `<Empty />` still renders during scaffolding.

props.name: description
props.description:
Why it is empty, or what will fill it. `false` hides it, for a title that already tells
the whole story.

props.name: action
props.description:
Buttons or links offering the next step. An empty state that only explains is a dead
end.

props.name: footer
props.description: Quiet copy under the action — a hint, a learn-more, a shortcut.

props.name: padding
props.description:
Breathing room, on both axes: `sm` for panels and cells, `lg` for a whole page. The
inline padding is what keeps copy off a dashed edge.

props.name: border
props.description:
The dashed outline. Off by default; use it when the empty state stands in for a card's
body and the edge says "something goes here".

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this state's own copy: `title`, `description`, and `ariaLabel`. The region
announces through `role="status"`, so a list that empties out while the reader is on the
page says so.

ResourceHeader.description:
The title block of an index or show screen, for a page that wants the shell's rhythm without
its whole frame.

props.name: eyebrow
props.description: Quiet context above the title: the parent record, the section.

props.name: media
props.description:
The media, in full. Ordered, not exclusive: it takes precedence over `avatarUrl`, which
takes precedence over `icon`. A screen knows one of the three, and which one depends on
what the record is — a person has an avatar, a settings section has an icon.

props.name: avatarUrl
props.description: An avatar image, used when there is no `media`.

props.name: avatarFallback
props.description: Defaults to initials derived from a string title.

props.name: icon
props.description: Rendered in an IconBadge when there is no media and no avatar.

props.name: badges
props.description: Status or identity chips beside the title.

props.name: metadata
props.description: Compact facts below the description.

ResourceShellSlots.description:
Regions a screen can replace outright. Each has a generated default; replace it when the
header or empty state is not the generated shape.

members.name: header
members.description: Replaces the generated identity header.

members.name: toolbar
members.description: Replaces the toolbar region, including a tabbed shell's own tab row.

members.name: aside
members.description: Related context beside the primary column, when the container is wide enough.

members.name: footer
members.description: After the body.

ResourceStrings.description: Generic fallback copy for the shells; screens usually override it ("No invoices found").

members.name: tabsLabel
members.description: Names the tab row for a screen reader: "Resource sections", "Invoice sections".

RichText.description:
Renders stored rich text — the READ half of the rich-text editor — in `Text`'s styles. It
sanitises on the way in, with no opt-out, so content from a database or an API cannot carry
script or event handlers into the page.

props.name: html
props.description: Sanitised through the kit's allow-list before it reaches the DOM.

props.name: children
props.description: Nodes instead of markup. Takes precedence over `html` when both are given.

props.name: lineHeight
props.description: Defaults to `relaxed`, the editor's prose leading, so a body does not reflow once posted.

RichTextEditor.description:
An editing surface with a toolbar and an imperative handle. Content is controlled through
`value` and `onValueChange`; the handle covers what a prop cannot.

props.name: engine
props.description:
What edits the document. Defaults to TipTap with StarterKit and inline, atomic mentions;
supply a RichTextEngine for a custom schema or implementation, and the caller owns its
destruction. The chrome (toolbar, source view, counts, footer, strings) is
engine-independent. Install the family's documented TipTap peers when importing the
editor.

props.name: value
props.description:
The document, as HTML. Controlled: parent echoes preserve the selection, and actual
external changes update the document, including while it is focused. Output is normalized
to the active engine's schema.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the document, as HTML, after every edit.

props.name: placeholder
props.description:
Drawn over the first line of the empty document, because a contenteditable has no
placeholder attribute. Sitting over it rather than replacing the document means the caret
is already in the right place.

props.name: compact
props.description:
Tightens the toolbar and shortens the body, for a composer rather than a page: a line and a
half instead of a page — enough to look like it takes more than a word, without claiming a
screen for a one-sentence reply.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Where the body starts scrolling instead of growing.

props.name: showCounts
props.description: Shows the word and character counts under the body.

props.name: maxLength
props.description:
Shown as "n / max". Over the limit the count turns error-toned; input is NOT refused — a
composer that stops accepting characters mid-word loses what the writer was in the middle
of. The count reports, the form decides.

props.name: extraToolbarItems
props.description:
Appended after the built-ins, behind a rule. Each takes an icon, a label used for both the
accessible name and the tooltip, and an optional `isActive`.

props.name: toolbarTrailing
props.description:
Pinned to the end of the toolbar, usually the submit control. Inside the frame, like
`footerSlot`, so the composer reads as one control.

props.name: footerSlot
props.description:
Below the body: attachment chips, a hint. Inside the frame, like `toolbarTrailing`, so the
composer reads as one control.

props.name: onCaretChange
props.description:
Fires after every input AND every selection change; read `getCaretContext()` from the
handle in response. Two events, because a caret moves without the document changing — and
a trigger detector watching only input misses the writer moving back into a half-typed
mention.

props.name: ref
props.description:
The imperative handle: `focus`, `getHTML`, `setHTML`, `insertHTML`, `isEmpty`, `clear`,
`getCaretContext`, `replaceBeforeCaret`. A superset of MentionEditorHandle, so the two
plug together with no adapter.

RichTextEditorHandle.description:
The editor's imperative handle, for what a prop cannot do: caret context, and replacing text
before the caret. A superset of MentionEditorHandle, so the two plug together with no
adapter.

members.name: insertHTML
members.description: Inserts raw HTML at the caret.

members.name: replaceBeforeCaret
members.description:
Deletes the `length` characters before the caret and inserts `html` in their place, as
one operation, not a delete then an insert: the caret never visits an in-between state,
and undo gets one entry for what the writer experienced as one act.

members.name: editorLabel
members.description: Names the editable surface for a screen reader.

members.name: sourceLabel
members.description: Names the HTML source textarea.

members.name: toolbarLabel
members.description: Names the formatting toolbar as a whole.

members.name: toolbar
members.type: { bold: string; italic: string; strike: string; bulletList: string; orderedList: string; blockquote: string; undo: string; redo: string; sourceCode: string; }
members.description: Toolbar labels. Each is both the accessible name and the tooltip.

RichTextEditorToolbar.description:
The formatting row, exported so an editor can be mounted with the toolbar somewhere else — a
sticky bar above a long document, or a shared bar over two editors.

RichTextEditorToolbarItem.description: A control the consumer adds to the toolbar, after the built-ins.

members.name: mount
members.description: Attaches an engine-owned view and returns its actual editable element.

members.name: unmount
members.description: Detaches the view while retaining the document, selection, and undo history.

members.name: setEditable
members.description: Updates whether the engine-owned view accepts user edits.

members.name: getState
members.description:
The current state, returning the same object until something changes: the shell reads
it through `useSyncExternalStore`, and a fresh object per call re-renders forever.

members.name: insertHtml
members.description: Inserts HTML at the engine's selection through its document model.

members.name: getCaretContext
members.description: Reads a focused, collapsed caret after the last atom or line break in its text block.

members.name: replaceBeforeCaret
members.description: Replaces text before a collapsed caret without crossing its text block or inline atoms.

members.name: subscribe
members.description: Returns an unsubscribe. The shell reads through `useSyncExternalStore`.

members.name: destroy
members.description: Idempotent, including when already unmounted.

props.name: groups
props.description: Each group names an area and lists its permissions with a granted flag.

props.name: onEdit
props.description: Omit to hide the edit action.

members.name: granted
members.description: Announces a granted permission; the glyph beside it is decorative.

RoundingModeSelect.description:
The rounding policies as a control, offering exactly the modes `DecimalInput` accepts —
`round`, `floor`, `ceil`, and `half-even` when asked for. `strings` replaces the labels.

props.name: modes
props.description: Which modes to offer, in order. Include `half-even` for an accounting surface.

props.name: strings
props.description: Replaces the mode labels.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown while nothing is selected. Shorthand for `strings.placeholder`, and wins over it.

props.name: allowClear
props.description:
Prepends an option that clears the selection, for a field whose empty state is a real
answer.

props.name: invalid
props.description:
Applies the invalid treatment; the trigger only carries it. Pair it with a message on the
`FormField`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial value, for an uncontrolled select.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Shows the value but prevents choosing another.

props.name: required
props.description: Requires a value before the owning form submits.

props.name: name
props.description: Field name for the hidden native input.

props.name: form
props.description:
The owning form's id, when the select renders outside it. Like `name`, `autoComplete` and
`inputRef`, it is for the hidden native input that carries the value into a form submit.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: Autofill hint for the hidden native input that carries the value into a form submit.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: Ref to the hidden native input used for submission.

props.name: open
props.description:
Whether the popup is open, for a select driven from outside — a tour, a keyboard
shortcut.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the popup starts open, uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the popup opens or closes.

props.name: modal
props.description:
Isolates interaction with the rest of the page while open. Turn it off for a select
inside a surface that is already modal.

props.name: highlightItemOnHover
props.description: Pointer movement highlights options. Off, the highlight belongs to the keyboard alone.

props.name: side
props.description: Where the popup opens relative to the trigger.

props.name: align
props.description: How the popup lines up with the trigger along that side.

props.name: alignItemWithTrigger
props.description:
Positions the chosen option over the trigger, the native macOS behaviour. Off, the list
opens under the field: inside a form, a popup over the trigger covers the field's own
label.

props.name: renderOption
props.description: Replaces the default icon/label/description row.

props.name: renderValue
props.description:
Replaces what the trigger shows — what a select of avatars needs. Receives `undefined` in
the placeholder state.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Class for the popup surface. `className` stays on the trigger.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Called on the trigger, so a form library can track touched state.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Called on the trigger, so a form library can track touched state.

members.name: placeholder
members.description: Shown in the trigger while nothing is chosen.

members.name: clear
members.description: Names the control that empties the selection, when `allowClear` is set.

SavedViewTabs.description:
A compact select of saved views that is NOT filter-driven — for a consumer holding views
themselves. The caller controls the selected view and applies its state through
`onValueChange`. For filter-driven tabs, or a select with exact preset matching, use
DataView's `filtering.tabs` or FilterTabs.

SchemaForm.description:
Renders and validates a form described as data. `validate()` runs on submit, and a message
clears as soon as its field changes.

props.name: schema
props.description:
Sections and fields. A section names its fields explicitly or claims the ones carrying its
`sectionId`; whatever no section claimed lands in a leading default bucket.

props.name: value
props.description:
Controlled values. Under a controlled value the schema's own defaults still apply, so a
consumer holding two fields does not blank the rest.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Uncontrolled starting values. An explicit default outranks the schema's own.

props.name: errors
props.description:
Server-side messages, keyed by field. Merged over the form's own and not cleared by
typing.

props.name: layout
props.description:
One bordered surface with sections inside it, or one surface per section. The schema does
not change between them.

props.name: actionsSlot
props.description: Replaces the generated submit and reset pair.

props.name: showActions
props.description: Defaults to true when there is something for the actions to do.

props.name: submitting
props.description: Additional external busy state. An async onSubmit also sets busy automatically.

props.name: onFieldChange
props.type: (key: string, value: SchemaFormValue, values: SchemaFormValues) => void

props.name: onSubmit
props.type: (values: SchemaFormValues, helpers: SchemaFormSubmitHelpers, event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) => void | Promise<void>
props.description:
Runs only if validation passed. `helpers` carries `setFieldValue`, `setValues`, `reset`,
and `validate` — for a server response that has to write back into the form.

props.name: onError
props.description: Receives errors from submission and consumer predicates, validators, or parsers.

props.name: renderField
props.description:
Replaces how a field renders. It receives `defaultField`, so decorating is as easy as
replacing.

props.name: renderSection
props.description: Replaces how a section renders, with its fields already laid out.

SchemaFormActions.description:
The form's submit row, generated from the same schema; reset renders only when there is an
`onReset` for it to reach. Exported so a screen can place it somewhere the generated layout
does not — a drawer footer, a sticky bar.

SchemaFormFieldBase.description: The keys every field shares, whatever its `type`.

members.name: type
members.description: Picks the control. Omitted means `text`.

members.name: disabled
members.description:
The predicate form reads the whole value set, for a field only editable once a sibling
says so.

members.name: hidden
members.description:
A hidden field is not rendered AND not validated — blocking a submit on a required field
the reader cannot see is a dead end. The predicate form reads the whole value set, for a
field that only matters once a sibling says so.

members.name: sectionId
members.description: Puts the field in a section without listing it there.

members.name: width
members.description:
Column span inside the section grid, which is keyed to a container. A form in a 320px
drawer collapses to one column whatever the section asked for.

members.name: controlClassName
members.description: Merged onto the control rather than the field wrapper.

members.name: validate
members.description:
Return a string to fail. The first message wins: the rest are about a value already known
to be wrong.

members.name: formatValue
members.description:
Turns the stored value into what the control displays: with `parseValue`, the two halves
of a custom representation.

members.name: parseValue
members.description:
Turns what the control produced back into the stored value: with `formatValue`, the two
halves of a custom representation.

members.name: meta
members.description: Free-form payload, carried through to `renderField`.

SchemaFormFieldRenderer.description:
One field, resolved from its schema entry to a control, with FormField owning the label, hint
and message. Reach for it when a form is mostly generated but one field needs to be placed by
hand.

props.name: values
props.description: All of them, for a field whose behaviour depends on a sibling.

props.name: fieldId
props.description: The generated DOM id linking the control to its label.

members.name: fields
members.description: Field keys, in the order they should render. Without it, `field.sectionId` decides.

members.name: submitError
members.description: Shown when submission rejects; values remain available for retry.

members.name: defaultSectionTitle
members.description: Names the bucket that holds fields no section claimed.

members.name: validationError
members.description: Shown when a consumer's own validator throws rather than returning a message.

Scope.description:
`<Scope>` — a token boundary without the config machinery. Overriding a factor needs a
scope boundary, not just any element: derived tokens are declared at `:root`,
`[data-ui-scope]`, `[data-density]`, `[data-theme]`, `.light` and `.dark`, so a plain
`div` that sets `--density-scale` sets a variable nothing reads. Scope renders
`data-ui-scope`, which puts the element on that list. Use it when the change is purely
tokens, and `<UIProvider>` when JavaScript config changes too. `render` picks the element,
e.g. `render={<section />}`.

  <Scope vars={{ "--density-scale": 0.8 }}>
    <Toolbar />
  </Scope>

props.name: vars
props.description: Custom properties to set. Keys include the leading `--`.

props.name: transparent
props.description: Removes the element from layout with `display: contents`; custom properties still inherit.

props.name: render
props.description:
Allows you to replace the component's HTML element
with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

ScrollArea.description:
A scroll container with the kit's scrollbar treatment, contained so reaching the end
doesn't scroll the page behind. Give it a max height; it does not impose one.

SearchFilter.description:
One inline search box. A `search` filter never becomes a pill: typing is the interaction,
and burying a text field two presses deep is how a search box stops being used. It debounces
locally, so the URL is not rewritten on every keystroke.

SearchFilters.description: The inline search boxes, one per `search` filter. A search filter never becomes a pill.

SearchGlassIllustration.description:
A magnifier on a soft disc — for "nothing matches", not "nothing exists". Drawn from the
theme's own tokens rather than shipped as an image, so it follows a rebrand and costs no
request.

SearchInput.description:
Input with a leading magnifier and a clear control, and the native search clear
suppressed. It only pre-wires those two; everything else is Input's API.

props.name: onClear
props.description:
Called when the reader clears the field — a notification only, because Input does the
clearing itself. The clear control is always present once there is a value.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this field's own copy. It is Input's strings object with one default
narrowed: a search field's only copy is one word of Input's.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Say what is being searched, not just "Search".

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Glyph after the value, in its own lane so the text never runs under it.

props.name: startAddon
props.description:
Short text attached before the value, outside the text itself — a currency symbol, a
protocol, an at sign.

props.name: endAddon
props.description: Short text attached after the value, outside the text itself — a unit, a domain.

props.name: showCharacterCount
props.description: Shows "12 / 80" in the trailing lane. Requires `maxLength`.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Character cap, and the limit the count counts against. Input past it is refused.

props.name: clearable
props.description:
Shows a clear control once the field has a value. Clearing goes through the native
value setter, so React's value tracker stays in sync.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Replaces the trailing affordance with a spinner, which outranks every other trailing
affordance.

props.name: invalid
props.description:
Applies the invalid treatment. Pair it with FormField's error for the message, so the
border and the announcement cannot disagree.

props.name: returnValueWithAddons
props.description:
Includes string addons in the value reported by `onChange`. Off, because an addon is
presentation: a caller that stores "$" and the number has to strip it again on the way
out.

SecondaryValue.description:
The same value one step quieter, for one that supports the primary value — a subtitle, a
unit, a qualifier.

props.name: children
props.description: The value. `null`, `undefined` or an empty string renders the empty mark.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: Rendered when the value is absent.

props.name: truncate
props.description: Ellipsises the value at one line. Every flex box in the chain needs `min-width: 0` — see `Text`.

Section.description:
A semantic `<section>` and the vertical rhythm between its children. The gap is one
fixed rhythm token, not a per-section prop: it does not re-expose the spacing scale, since
a page whose sections each pick a gap has no rhythm.

props.name: items
props.description: The headings: an id, a label, and an optional depth for nesting.

props.name: rootMargin
props.description:
Which part of the viewport counts as "here". The default makes a heading current once
it reaches the upper quarter.

members.name: id
members.description: The element id this entry points at.

members.name: depth
members.description: Nesting depth. 1 is top level; deeper entries are indented.

props.name: options
props.description: The choices. Each carries a value, a label, and an optional description and icon.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown while nothing is selected. Shorthand for `strings.placeholder`, and wins over it.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this select's own copy — the placeholder and the clear row.

props.name: allowClear
props.description:
Prepends an option that clears the selection, for a field whose empty state is a real
answer.

props.name: invalid
props.description:
Applies the invalid treatment; the trigger only carries it. Pair it with a message on the
`FormField`.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value. Passing `undefined` explicitly keeps it controlled and clear.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial value, for an uncontrolled select.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with `undefined` when the selection is cleared.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Shows the value but prevents choosing another.

props.name: required
props.description: Requires a value before the owning form submits.

props.name: name
props.description: Field name for the hidden native input.

props.name: form
props.description:
The owning form's id, when the select renders outside it. Like `name`, `autoComplete` and
`inputRef`, it is for the hidden native input that carries the value into a form submit.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: Autofill hint for the hidden native input that carries the value into a form submit.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: Ref to the hidden native input used for submission.

props.name: open
props.description:
Whether the popup is open, for a select driven from outside — a tour, a keyboard
shortcut.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the popup starts open, uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the popup opens or closes.

props.name: modal
props.description:
Isolates interaction with the rest of the page while open. Turn it off for a select
inside a surface that is already modal.

props.name: highlightItemOnHover
props.description: Pointer movement highlights options. Off, the highlight belongs to the keyboard alone.

props.name: side
props.description: Where the popup opens relative to the trigger.

props.name: align
props.description: How the popup lines up with the trigger along that side.

props.name: alignItemWithTrigger
props.description:
Positions the chosen option over the trigger, the native macOS behaviour. Off, the list
opens under the field: inside a form, a popup over the trigger covers the field's own
label.

props.name: renderOption
props.description: Replaces the default icon/label/description row.

props.name: renderValue
props.description:
Replaces what the trigger shows — what a select of avatars needs. Receives `undefined` in
the placeholder state.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Class for the popup surface. `className` stays on the trigger.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Called on the trigger, so a form library can track touched state.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Called on the trigger, so a form library can track touched state.

SelectFilterEditor.description:
The editor for a `select` or `multi_select` filter. A multi-select STAGES its value and
commits on Apply — one that committed on each tick would be one request per tick; a single
select with `closeOnSelect` commits at once.

props.name: triggerSource
props.description: Only a toolbar-opened editor has a list to go back to.

SelectIconPrimitive.description: The unassembled icon behind `Select`: the trigger's chevron.

members.name: description
members.description: Second line under the label. Clamped to two lines.

SelectPopupContent.description:
The popup behind `Select`, public so every finite-option control — a phone country, a unit
