picker — renders the same popup and rows.

props.name: container
props.description:
Where the popup renders. Defaults to the nearest `UIPortalHost`, else the primitive's
own target.

props.name: side
props.description:
Which side of the anchor element to align the popup against.
May automatically change to avoid collisions.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description:
Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the distance to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

props.name: align
props.description: How to align the popup relative to the specified side.

props.name: alignOffset
props.description:
Additional offset along the alignment axis in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the offset to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

props.name: alignItemWithTrigger
props.description: Whether the positioner overlaps the trigger so the selected item's text is aligned with the trigger's value text. This only applies to mouse input and is automatically disabled if there is not enough space.

SelectPopupGroup.description: A division of the popup's options.

SelectPopupItem.description: One option row, with the mark that shows it is chosen.

SelectPopupLabel.description:
A group's caption. A label is not an item: it is not focusable and the arrow keys skip it,
which a styled item would get wrong.

SelectPopupSeparator.description: A rule between groups of options.

SelectRoot.description:
The unassembled root behind `Select`. Reach for these parts when the trigger has to be
something `Select` cannot express — an avatar and a name, a swatch, two lines — and keep
the popup and the keyboard behaviour rather than rebuilding them.

members.name: placeholder
members.description: Shown in the trigger while nothing is chosen.

members.name: clear
members.description: Names the control that empties the selection, when `allowClear` is set.

SelectTriggerPrimitive.description: The unassembled trigger behind `Select`, for a trigger `Select` cannot express.

SelectValuePrimitive.description: The unassembled value behind `Select`: what the trigger shows for the current choice.

props.name: action
props.description: The control that performs it — usually a destructive Button.

props.name: confirmation
props.description:
What will happen, stated before it does. Rendered `role="note"`, not as an error —
nothing has gone wrong yet.

props.name: title
props.description:
The heading. Either it or `description` renders the header; neither, and the block is a
bare surface.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting copy on its own row, so a long one wraps under the whole header.

props.name: titleSuffix
props.description: Content immediately after the title — a badge, a count.

props.name: headerEnd
props.description: Controls at the end of the title line.

props.name: surface
props.description:
Outer chrome. What separates `bordered` from `card` is the ground: a bordered block is a
ruled region and the page shows through it; a card block lifts off it.

props.name: flush
props.description:
Drops the surface's inset and clips to its radius, for content that runs to the edge
(divided cells, ruled rows); children pay their own inset. Only meaningful on a surface
that has an inset to drop.

members.name: ratio
members.description:
The unrounded fraction earned, for percentages: `score` is rounded to whole points and
can hide a small penalty. Always set by `calculateSeoScore`; optional so hand-built
checks stay valid, and readers fall back to `score / maxScore`.

members.name: actual
members.description: The measured length, so a card can show "62 / 60".

props.name: listing
props.description:
What the result will read as: title, description, permalink, baseUrl, keyword, and
optional limits. Scored on render unless a `score` is supplied.

props.name: score
props.description:
A score computed elsewhere — by an editor scoring as the user types. Without it the
card scores the listing itself.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting copy on its own row, so a long one wraps under the whole header.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading glyph on the title line.

props.name: titleSuffix
props.description: Content immediately after the title — a badge, a count.

props.name: headerEnd
props.description: Controls at the end of the title line.

props.name: surface
props.description:
Outer chrome. What separates `bordered` from `card` is the ground: a bordered block is a
ruled region and the page shows through it; a card block lifts off it.

props.name: flush
props.description:
Drops the surface's inset and clips to its radius, for content that runs to the edge
(divided cells, ruled rows); children pay their own inset. Only meaningful on a surface
that has an inset to drop.

members.name: permalink
members.description: The full URL, or just its path.

members.name: baseUrl
members.description: The origin the permalink sits on — scored for HTTPS.

members.name: keyword
members.description: What the copy is meant to rank for. Omit it and the check is not run.

members.name: formatMeasure
members.description: "62 / 60" — the measured length against its cap.

members.name: formatPercent
members.description: Inside a check's ring. A locale that writes percentages differently overrides it.

Separator.description:
A rule between content, horizontal or vertical; a vertical separator needs a height from
its container. An unlabelled separator exposes separator semantics: set `aria-hidden` to
hide a decorative rule from assistive technology.

props.name: variant
props.description:
How the rule is drawn. Structural, not semantic — a dashed rule is the same divider,
drawn as provisional.

props.name: thickness
props.description:
The rule's thickness: a CSS length, or a number in pixels. Overrides
`--separator-thickness` for this rule, e.g. a seam between panels.

props.name: label
props.description:
Text set into a gap in the rule — "OR", "More options". Horizontal only. It drops the
separator role, because the rule is then decoration around real text.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The orientation of the separator.

props.name: aria-hidden
props.description: Indicates whether the element is exposed to an accessibility API.

SharedResourceCard.description:
Shows the resource assigned to a record and how to change it. The card owns the shape —
panel, dialog, pending choice, awaited confirm; the picker is the consumer's, since every
assignment searches differently.

props.name: actions
props.description:
Extra overflow actions. Alone, the change action is a header button; alongside these it
joins them — two triggers side by side is worse than one menu holding both.

props.name: resource
props.description:
The persisted assignment. `null` is the only empty state; `hasResource` is derived from it
and never independently controlled.

props.name: selector
props.description:
The picker, its copy, and the write. Omit it and the card is read-only — no change action,
and an empty state that offers nothing.

props.name: sections
props.description:
Declarative body blocks, used when no content override is given: the last rung of the
assigned body's ladder, after `renderResourceContent` and `ResourceContentComponent`.

props.name: viewAction
props.description:
Router-neutral "open the resource" slot, shown only when one is assigned.
Takes precedence over `viewLink`.

props.name: viewLink
props.type: { href: string; label: ReactNode; className?: string; }
props.description:
The native-anchor convenience, for an app with no router in the way. Like `viewAction`, it
renders only when a resource is assigned.

props.name: ResourceContentComponent
props.description:
The assigned body as a component: the second rung of the ladder, after
`renderResourceContent` and before `sections`. A component is reusable.

props.name: renderResourceContent
props.description:
The assigned body, most specific first: this, then `ResourceContentComponent`, then
`sections`. A render prop closes over local state, a component is reusable, and sections
are data — each rung exists because the one below it is wrong for someone.

members.name: hasResource
members.description: Derived from `resource !== null`. Never independently controlled.

SharedResourceCardSection.description: One block of the assigned resource's body, shown when its predicate says so.

members.name: actionLabel
members.description: Names the change action. Alone it is a header button; with other actions it joins the overflow menu.

members.name: mapInitialSelected
members.description:
Turns the persisted resource into a starting choice for the picker, so “Change” opens on
what the record holds.

members.name: getSelectionLabel
members.description:
How the pending choice reads in the summary above the buttons. Without it the card looks
for a string `label` field, which is a guess — a cheap and usually right one.

members.name: onConfirmSelection
members.description:
Persists it. A returned promise is awaited and drives the confirming state; a rejection
keeps the dialog open and reaches `onError`.

members.name: SelectorComponent
members.description:
The picker. Yours: it receives `selected`, `onSelect`, and `inModal` — a picker that adapts
inside a dialog can read the last one.

members.name: isConfirmDisabled
members.description:
Refuses a pending choice — an inactive venue, a room that is full or too small. The confirm
stays disabled rather than failing after the press.

members.name: onDialogOpen
members.description: Fires once per closed-to-open cycle, with the choice the dialog opened on.

members.name: value
members.description: Controlled pending choice. Authoritative on every open.

members.name: defaultValue
members.description: Uncontrolled starting choice. Authoritative on the first open only.

members.name: noResourceContent
members.description: Shown when a resource is assigned but the consumer supplied no content for it.

SheetContent.description:
OverlayContent at an edge. `side` is OverlayContent's `placement` minus centre — logical,
so it follows the writing mode — and the sheet adds a default shape: `side="inline-end"`,
`size="md"`, `length="full"` and `inset={false}`. `UIProvider`'s `defaults.sheet` takes
the same four, for a product that decides the shape once.

`modality`, `surface`, `dismissal`, `initialFocusRef` and `showCloseButton` pass through
unchanged, with the Overlay defaults. A sheet is where `non-modal` earns its place: an
inspector you keep working beside.

props.name: side
props.description: The edge it enters from, as a logical side. `UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: size
length
props.description:
Along-axis extent, for an edge placement. Less than full detaches the panel and centres
it on that axis. It is measured against the space the inset leaves rather than the
viewport: 70% of an inset panel is 70% of what is between the offsets, and the rest is
split between the two ends. Full needs no inset to look right, which is why a
corner-anchored sheet sets only `inset`.

props.name: inset
props.description:
The gap to the viewport edges. `false` is flush — a sheet welded to the side; `true`
uses the kit's gap; any CSS length sets your own. One offset, spent on every side the
panel does not run to, so an inset side panel sits the same distance from the top, the
side and the bottom. Any gap detaches it, rounds all four corners and gives it a full
border.

props.name: modality
props.description:
How much of the page the surface takes hostage: scrim, inert background and scroll
lock (`modal`), focus alone (`trap-focus`), or neither (`non-modal`).

props.name: surface
props.description: `bare` drops the region dividers, for content that draws its own chrome.

props.name: dismissal
props.description:
Each route out, separately. Off for a decision that must be answered, or for work in
progress. AlertDialogContent fixes both off.

props.name: initialFocusRef
props.description: Element to focus on open, instead of the first tabbable node.

props.name: showCloseButton
props.description: Renders the corner dismiss control. AlertDialogContent turns it off.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this surface's own copy — the corner dismiss control's name.

props.name: items
props.description: Flat entries. Mutually exclusive with `groups`.

props.name: groups
props.description:
Captioned blocks of entries, each of which can be collapsible. Mutually exclusive with
`items`.

props.name: currentPath
props.description:
The path considered current. Matched by longest prefix, so exactly one entry is
current: `/settings/members` marks the members entry, not the `/settings` index.

props.name: renderLink
props.description:
Routes entries through the app's router, as every component's `renderLink` does.
Without it, entries are plain anchors — the kit never imports a router.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides the rail's own copy — the collapse control's name.

members.name: id
members.description: Stable identity, used for the collapsed set.

members.name: label
members.description: Caption above the entries. Omit for an uncaptioned block.

members.name: href
members.description: Destination.

members.name: badge
members.description:
A count or a status beside the label. A string or number is wrapped in a neutral
`Badge`; pass a node to choose the tone.

Sidebar.description: The panel: a header, scrolling content and a footer, against one edge of the shell.

props.name: side
props.description: Which edge the panel occupies, for the rail and the mobile sheet alike.

props.name: variant
collapsible
props.description:
How it gets out of the way: slid away entirely (`offcanvas`), reduced to a rail of
glyphs (`icon`), or pinned open, never collapsing (`none`). On a narrow viewport a
collapsible panel becomes a sheet.

props.name: surfaceClassName
props.description: Class for the visible panel surface, separate from the positioning container.

props.name: mobileTitle
props.description: Accessible name for the mobile sheet.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this sidebar's own copy, including the two above.

SidebarContent.description: The scrolling region between the header and the footer.

members.name: strings
members.description: Resolved copy, so every part of the sidebar reads the same override.

members.name: handle
members.description: Stable id. Keys the entry and looks up its live badge.

SidebarFooter.description: The panel's bottom region. It holds its edge while the content scrolls.

SidebarGroup.description:
A titled section of the panel, with an optional control on the label's line — an add, a
filter.

SidebarGroupAction.description: A control on the section title's line — an add, a filter.

SidebarGroupContent.description: The section's body, under its label.

SidebarHeader.description:
The panel's top region. It holds its edge while the content scrolls, so a long navigation
never scrolls its own search box away.

SidebarIcon.description:
Resolves an icon that may be a name (looked up in `iconMap`), a component or a node.
Exported because a caller supplying `renderItem` still wants the same resolution — a row
rendered by hand should not need its own copy of “string means look it up, component
means render it, node means use it”.

SidebarInset.description:
The page beside the panel. Renders `<main>`, so it is the document's main landmark rather
than another div; a shell embedded in a host page that already has one should pass
`render={<div />}`.

props.name: render
props.description:
Allows you to replace the component's HTML element
with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

props.name: sidebar
props.description: The navigation panel — usually an `<AppSidebar />`.

props.name: toolbar
props.description: The row above the content. `false` removes it, for a shell with no chrome at all.

props.name: toolbarEnd
props.description: Rendered at the toolbar's trailing edge — a search field, an account menu.

props.name: showTrigger
props.description:
Shows the panel toggle, the toolbar's collapse control. On mobile it is the only way to
open the panel; turn it off for a shell whose navigation is opened from somewhere else.

props.name: boundContent
props.description:
Caps the content at a reading measure instead of letting it run the shell's full width,
so a wide monitor does not stretch prose across the page.

props.name: contained
props.description:
Bounds the shell to its parent instead of the viewport. The panel is fixed by default,
which is right for a shell that owns the screen and wrong everywhere else.

props.name: sidebarProviderProps
props.description:
Passes `open`/`onOpenChange`, `persist`, `keyboardShortcut` and `strings` to the
shell's provider: controlled state, persistence, shortcuts and translated sidebar
controls. Disable persistence and shortcuts in independent embedded examples.

props.name: toolbarClassName
props.description:
Styles the toolbar without wrapping it. The shell owns the grid, so a wrapper around a
region would break the sticky rows.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description:
Styles the content region without wrapping it. The shell owns the grid, so a wrapper
around a region would break the sticky rows.

props.name: contentRender
props.description:
Replaces the element the content region is drawn as (`<main>` by default). Pass
`contentRender={<div />}` when embedded in a page that owns the main landmark.

props.name: ruledToolbar
props.description: `false` when the content below sits on its own plane — an inset sidebar.

SidebarLogo.description:
The product mark in the rail’s header. It swaps to the compact mark when the rail
collapses to icons rather than scaling the full one down, because a squeezed wordmark is
unreadable at rail width.

props.name: logo
props.description: Shown while the rail is expanded.

props.name: collapsedLogo
props.description: Shown while it is collapsed. Without one the header is empty there.

SidebarMenu.description:
The rows: a real `<ul>`, so the navigation announces as a list and its length is
spoken.

SidebarMenuAction.description:
A secondary control on a row, positioned so it neither displaces the label nor steals the
row's press target.

props.name: showOnHover
props.description:
Reveals the action on hover or keyboard focus rather than showing it always. Focus
counts through `focus-within`, so the action stays reachable without a pointer.

SidebarMenuBadge.description:
A count on a row, positioned so it neither displaces the label nor steals the row's press
target.

props.name: inline
props.description: Renders in normal flow instead of over the row — for a button laying out its own parts.

SidebarMenuButton.description: The row's control: a button, or through `render` a router link.

props.name: size
props.description:
The row's height, as a shape rather than a density: `lg` is the workspace switcher, `sm`
a secondary row. A size prop here, because a navigation row is not on the control
ladder that density scales.

props.name: active
props.description: Marks the row as the current page.

props.name: variant
props.description: `outline` gives the row its own frame — for a switcher that must read as a control.

props.name: render
props.description:
The element this row becomes instead of a `button` — usually a router link, so the row
navigates the app's own way. `children` stays the row's content.

props.name: closeOnSelectMobile
props.description:
Dismisses the mobile sheet when the row is activated. Turn it off for a row that opens
something else (a switcher, a submenu toggle).

props.name: tooltip
props.description:
The row's name, shown beside it while the sidebar is collapsed to its icon rail, where
the label is clipped away. Ignored while expanded and on phones.

SidebarMenuItem.description: One row: a real `<li>`, holding the row's button and anything beside it.

SidebarMenuSkeleton.description:
Reserves a row's exact box while the navigation loads, so the panel does not reflow when
it lands.

props.name: showIcon
props.description: Reserves the row's icon as well as its label.

SidebarMenuSub.description: A nested level under a row, indented against the parent's rail.

SidebarMenuSubButton.description:
A nested row's control: a link when it has an `href`, otherwise a button, or through
`render` a router link.

props.name: size
props.description: The nested row's height.

props.name: active
props.description: Marks the row as the current page.

props.name: closeOnSelectMobile
props.description: Dismisses the mobile sheet when the row is activated. See SidebarMenuButton.

props.name: render
props.description:
The element this row becomes instead of an `a` or `button` — usually a router link, so
the row navigates the app's own way. `children` stays the row's content.

SidebarMenuSubItem.description: One row of a nested level.

SidebarProvider.description:
Holds the panel's state above both the trigger and the rail, so the two cannot disagree,
and shares it with every part inside.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides the sidebar's own copy for every part (it travels through the context).

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial expanded state when uncontrolled.

props.name: open
props.description:
Controlled expanded state. It is held here, above both the trigger and the rail, so the
two cannot disagree.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the next expanded state.

props.name: persist
props.description:
Remembers the expanded state across reloads, in `localStorage`. It is read during the
first render, so the shell does not flash open and then snap shut.

props.name: keyboardShortcut
props.description: Enables the ⌘B / Ctrl-B toggle shortcut.

props.name: contained
props.description:
Bounds the shell to this element instead of the viewport — for a shell that does not
own the screen (inside a tab, a preview, a nested editor). The panel is
`position: fixed` by default, which is correct for a real shell and the reason a demo
of one has to opt out.

SidebarRail.description:
The strip along the panel's edge, which toggles it too. It reads the provider, so it works
from anywhere inside it. Not a tab stop: it duplicates the trigger.

members.name: toggle
members.description: Names the collapse control in both states — it is icon-only in both.

members.name: mobileTitle
members.description: Title and description of the off-canvas sheet the rail becomes on a phone.

SidebarTrigger.description:
The button that toggles the panel. It reads the provider, so it works from anywhere
inside it; pair it with the rail, which does the same job from the panel's edge.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Semantic colour intent. Resolves through the provider when omitted, so `UIProvider`
defaults can change it.

props.name: buttonStyle
props.description: Fill treatment, independent of `tone`. `UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description: Square button sized to its height. The label becomes the accessible name.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretches the button to its container's width.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a spinner and blocks interaction. The label keeps its space so the button does
not resize mid-action.

props.name: render
props.description:
The element this button becomes — an anchor, a router link, a label. `children` stay
the content and keep the button's label wrapper, so a link still sizes like a button.
`render` is how every kit component changes its element, the contract Base UI's parts
already take.

  <Button render={<a href="/settings" />}>Settings</Button>

SidebarUser.description:
The account row at the foot of the rail. Its menu opens to the RIGHT when the rail is
collapsed and ABOVE when it is not, because a menu that always drops down is off-screen at
the bottom of a full-height panel.

members.name: avatar
members.description: Image URL. Without one the shell derives initials from the name.

members.name: role
members.description: A job title or a role name, shown where there is room for a third line.

props.name: customContent
props.description: Replaces the menu body, as in HeaderUserMenu.

props.name: renderTrigger
props.description: Replaces the row's content, keeping the button and the menu.

members.name: trigger
members.description: Names the trigger when the rail is collapsed to icons and the name is hidden.

SidebarWorkspace.description:
The rail’s header as a workspace switcher. The whole header row is the trigger, not a
chevron beside a decorative name — the name is what a reader aims at.

props.name: workspaceLinks
props.description: The destinations. With none, use SidebarLogo — a menu of nothing is a dead control.

props.name: renderLink
props.description: Renders links through the application's router; without it, plain anchors.

members.name: select
members.description: Names the trigger, which is a logo and a chevron with no text of its own.

members.name: label
members.description: Captions the group of destinations in the menu.

SingleDatePicker.description:
`DatePicker` with `mode="single"` fixed, so the value type is fixed with it: a `Date`. The
generic picker has to widen its callback to cover every mode, which pushes a cast into
every call site.

props.name: id
props.description:
Applied to the trigger, the only labelable element. Its name comes from the chosen date,
so the field's label must reach it.

props.name: displayFormat
props.description: How the chosen value is written in the trigger: a date-fns pattern. The popup is unaffected.

props.name: invalid
props.description: The error surface. The message stays on the `FormField`.

props.name: clearable
props.description:
Adds a clear control to the trigger once something is chosen: a real button beside the
calendar glyph, named through `strings` — not an icon with a click handler.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this picker's own copy — the clear control and the calendar's captions. The
same object reaches the calendar inside the popup, so one override names the month
controls too.

props.name: presets
props.description:
Shortcuts down the side — "Last 30 days", "This month": the rail beside a range
calendar. `createRangePresets({ strings, weekStartsOn })` builds the built-in set in your
language and week.

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description:
How many months are shown side by side: two for a range, one otherwise. The header
becomes a range when more than one.

props.name: closeOnSelect
props.description:
Closes the popup as soon as a complete value is chosen. On by default for a single date
and off for a range, because a range is not chosen until both ends are.

props.name: header
props.description: A band above the calendar — a title, a mode switch. Use `DatePickerHeader`.

props.name: footer
props.description: A band below it — a summary, Clear and Apply. Use `DatePickerFooter`.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Styles the popup surface. `className` stays on the trigger.

props.name: minDate
props.description: Earliest selectable day, inclusive.

props.name: maxDate
props.description: Latest selectable day, inclusive.

props.name: disabledDates
props.description: Refuses individual days — weekends, holidays, days already booked.

Skeleton.description: The primitive box. Size it with `style` or a class; the composed skeletons are built from it.

SkeletonStrings.description: What a skeleton announces while there is nothing to read. `label` overrides per instance.

members.name: loading
members.description: A region of content.

members.name: loadingPage
members.description: A whole page's worth.

members.name: loadingTable
members.description: A table, where the shape being loaded is worth naming.

Slider.description:
The bare control: `SliderField` without the value readout (`showValue`, `unit`) — for a
slider inside a toolbar, a popover or a canvas control, where the surrounding surface
already says what it adjusts.

props.name: value
props.description:
Controlled value. An array makes it a range, one thumb per entry. Handlers report back
in the same shape: a number in, a number out.

props.name: min
props.description: The lower bound.

props.name: max
props.description: The upper bound.

props.name: step
props.description: The increment between values.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Applies the invalid treatment. The message stays on the FormField.

props.name: orientation
props.description:
The track's direction. A vertical slider takes its height from
`--slider-vertical-min-h`, because a slider has no content to size it.

props.name: size
props.description:
Track and thumb size: `md` is a larger drag target (touch, media controls). A slider is
dragged, which is why this one keeps a size prop.

props.name: onChange
props.type: (event: SliderChangeEvent<TValue extends number ? number : TValue>) => void
props.description: Native-shaped handler, for form libraries.

props.name: onValueChange
props.type: (value: TValue extends number ? number : TValue) => void
props.description: The value on its own, for everything else.

props.name: onValueCommitted
props.type: (value: TValue extends number ? number : TValue) => void
props.description: Fires once on pointer release or keyboard commit, not on every step.

props.name: formatValue
props.description:
How the readout writes ONE value. A range formats each end and joins them with an en
dash.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this slider's own copy: each range thumb's name and the fallback name.
`thumb` is a function of the thumb's index, defaulting to "Minimum" and "Maximum" — two
handles called the same thing are two handles a screen reader cannot tell apart, and a
range may have more than two.

SliderField.description:
One number on a track, or a range when the value is an array. It emits both a bare value
and a native-shaped change event, because a form library registers a field by handing it
an `onChange` and reading `event.target.value`.

props.name: value
props.description:
Controlled value. An array makes it a range, one thumb per entry. Handlers report back
in the same shape: a number in, a number out.

props.name: min
props.description: The lower bound.

props.name: max
props.description: The upper bound.

props.name: step
props.description: The increment between values.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Applies the invalid treatment. The message stays on the FormField.

props.name: orientation
props.description:
The track's direction. A vertical slider takes its height from
`--slider-vertical-min-h`, because a slider has no content to size it.

props.name: size
props.description:
Track and thumb size: `md` is a larger drag target (touch, media controls). A slider is
dragged, which is why this one keeps a size prop.

props.name: onChange
props.type: (event: SliderChangeEvent<TValue extends number ? number : TValue>) => void
props.description: Native-shaped handler, for form libraries.

props.name: onValueChange
props.type: (value: TValue extends number ? number : TValue) => void
props.description: The value on its own, for everything else.

props.name: onValueCommitted
props.type: (value: TValue extends number ? number : TValue) => void
props.description: Fires once on pointer release or keyboard commit, not on every step.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Shows the current value beside the track.

props.name: formatValue
props.description:
How the readout writes ONE value. A range formats each end and joins them with an en
dash.

props.name: unit
props.description: Suffix on the displayed value — "px", "%", "mm". Ignored when `formatValue` is given.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this slider's own copy: each range thumb's name and the fallback name.
`thumb` is a function of the thumb's index, defaulting to "Minimum" and "Maximum" — two
handles called the same thing are two handles a screen reader cannot tell apart, and a
range may have more than two.

members.name: thumb
members.description: Names each thumb of a range, by index.

members.name: label
members.description:
Names a single-thumb slider given no `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Optional so
older complete strings objects still type-check.

Slot.description:
Merges its props onto its single child element and composes refs. The child's props win,
except that classes join, both handlers run (the child's first) and styles merge (the
child's over the slot's). Renders nothing unless given exactly one element. The kit's own
components take `render`, which is built on this merge; `Slot` is for composing components
of your own.

props.name: value
props.description:
The source text; the field shows its slugified form. Controlled — the slug is derived,
never held.

props.name: transform
props.description:
Replaces the built-in derivation entirely. The default lower-cases, strips accents,
keeps letters and numbers in any script, and collapses every other run to a single
separator.

props.name: prefix
props.description:
Rendered before the slug, inside the field — a domain or a path prefix. Not part of the
value.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Glyph before the value, in its own lane so the text never runs under it.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Glyph after the value, in its own lane so the text never runs under it.

props.name: startAddon
props.description:
Short text attached before the value, outside the text itself — a currency symbol, a
protocol, an at sign.

props.name: endAddon
props.description: Short text attached after the value, outside the text itself — a unit, a domain.

props.name: showCharacterCount
props.description: Shows "12 / 80" in the trailing lane. Requires `maxLength`.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Character cap, and the limit the count counts against. Input past it is refused.

props.name: clearable
props.description:
Shows a clear control once the field has a value. Clearing goes through the native
value setter, so React's value tracker stays in sync.

props.name: onClear
props.description: Called after the clear control empties the field.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Replaces the trailing affordance with a spinner, which outranks every other trailing
affordance.

props.name: invalid
props.description:
Applies the invalid treatment. Pair it with FormField's error for the message, so the
border and the announcement cannot disagree.

props.name: returnValueWithAddons
props.description:
Includes string addons in the value reported by `onChange`. Off, because an addon is
presentation: a caller that stores "$" and the number has to strip it again on the way
out.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this field's own copy — the clear label, the character-count format.

props.name: separator
props.description: Character joining words.

props.name: lowercase
props.description: Lower-cases the slug.

props.name: trim
props.description: Strips leading and trailing separators.

Sparkline.description:
A trend line with no axes, no grid and no tooltip — the shape of a series beside the figure
it belongs to. Not a small `ChartContainer`: it draws no chrome, so it can sit inside a table
cell or a metric tile.

props.name: data
props.description: The series, in chronological order.

props.name: tone
props.description: Colours the stroke and its fade.

props.name: animated
props.description: Off by default: many sparklines animating at once reads as a malfunction.

props.name: label
props.description: What the shape says. Without it the chart is decorative and hidden from readers.

props.name: size
props.description:
The ring's size: `sm`, `md` or `lg`. The one place a size prop survives: a spinner has
no content to scale with.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Borrows the button tone contract, so a spinner inside or beside an action matches it
rather than sitting on it in the primary hue.

props.name: label
props.description:
Visible label beside the ring, and the announced status. Without one the spinner is
decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: side
props.description:
Which visual column is the fixed one. The DOM order never changes with it: the first
child is the main content and the second the side on both settings, so a reader
tabbing through reaches the content first either way.

props.name: sideWidth
props.description:
The fixed column's width — a step or any CSS length. A maximum rather than an exact
size, so a narrow viewport shrinks the rail instead of squeezing the content beside it
to nothing.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between the two columns.

props.name: collapseBelow
props.description:
Below this breakpoint the two columns become one. `never` keeps them side by side at
every width.

props.name: direction
props.description: Main axis.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between children, on the semantic spacing scale.

props.name: align
props.description: Cross-axis alignment.

props.name: justify
props.description: Main-axis distribution.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Allows children to flow onto more than one line.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description:
Caps the box's width — a content step (`sm` to `2xl`, `full`, `none`) or any CSS
length, such as a form's `26rem`. A field measure is a control decision rather than a
content one, which is why a raw length is allowed beside the scale.

members.name: id
members.description: Stable identity. Falls back to the name when absent.

members.name: initials
members.description: Overrides the derived initials.

StackedAvatars.description: People as overlapping avatars, capped with a count of the rest.

props.name: users
props.description: The people in the row, in order.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this group's own copy — its accessible name, and the overflow chip.

props.name: max
props.description: How many faces to show. Beyond it, the remainder becomes a count.

props.name: showOverflow
props.description: Shows the "+N" tile. Turn it off for a group where the total does not matter.

props.name: overflowFormatter
props.description:
How the remainder reads on the overflow tile — "+12", "+12 more". Defaults to
`strings.overflow`, which reads "+N".

StackedAvatarsStrings.description:
What a stack of avatars announces. Plurals are functions a consumer replaces whole:
most languages have more than two forms.

members.name: people
members.description: Names the group, by how many people are in it.

members.name: overflow
members.description: The overflow chip at the end of the stack ("+3"). `overflowFormatter` replaces it.

StackedCardsIllustration.description:
Three stacked cards fading out — the generic "no records". Drawn from the theme's own
tokens rather than shipped as an image, so it follows a rebrand and costs no request.

props.name: header
props.description: The header row — a mark, navigation, an account menu.

props.name: contained
props.description: Fit a parent with a definite height and scroll the content below the header.

props.name: boundContent
props.description:
Caps the reading width. Set false for wide tables and composed workspaces that use the
full content width.

props.name: headerClassName
props.description:
Styles the header row without wrapping it. The shell owns the grid, so a wrapper around
a region would break the sticky rows.

props.name: contentRender
props.description:
Replaces the element the content region is drawn as (`<main>` by default). Pass
`contentRender={<div />}` when embedded in a page that owns the main landmark.

StatusClusterCell.description:
Several status chips in one cell, e.g. overdue and partially paid; a status is a Badge. One of
the cells every admin table has, so a page does not rewrite it per column: a thin arrangement
over the kit's primitives that adds the cell's part — the alignment, the truncation, the empty
case.

members.name: timestamp
members.description: Already formatted.

members.name: content
members.description: Hangs under the step in the vertical form.

Stepper.description:
A numbered sequence the reader is partway through: a marker per step — a numeral that
becomes a tick — connectors, and a label with an optional hint.

props.name: steps
props.description: The steps, in order. Rendered as an `<ol>`, because the order is the meaning.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Which drawing. `bar`: labels under ringed markers in equal columns, with the connector
through the marker row. `trail`: labels beside filled markers and a rule taking the
rest of the row; below `lg` the labels are visually hidden and only the markers show.

props.name: onStepClick
props.description:
Makes each step a button: completed steps and the current one are reachable, upcoming
ones disabled. Without it the steps are plain list items.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this stepper's own copy: `position(index, total)` names what the numeral
counts, and `completed` and `current` are said with those steps.

members.name: id
members.description: Stable identity for the step, handed back to `onStepClick`.

members.name: label
members.description: What the step is called.

members.name: hint
members.description: A second, quieter line under the label.

members.name: status
members.description:
Where the step stands. `completed` is the canonical spelling; `complete` is accepted as
the same state and normalised, so the DOM only ever says `completed`.

members.name: accessibleName
members.description:
The step's whole accessible name, worded by the caller. It replaces the announced
position, label, hint and state rather than joining them; `aria-current` still marks
the current step.

StepperStrings.description: The stepper's copy — all for screen readers, since the markers are decoration.

members.name: position
members.description: Says what the marker's numeral counts — "Step 2 of 4".

members.name: completed
members.description: Said with a finished step, so the tick and its tone are not the only sign of it.

members.name: current
members.description: Said with the step the reader is on, alongside `aria-current`.

Steps.description: The vertical form: the shared rail, with each step's content hanging under it.

props.name: steps
props.description:
`status` is completed | current | upcoming. The vertical form also takes per-step
`content`.

StepsBar.description:
The horizontal form: numbered markers with connectors, over base's `Stepper`. Scrolls
rather than clipping.

props.name: steps
props.description:
`status` is completed | current | upcoming. The vertical form also takes per-step
`content`.

members.name: stepLabel
members.description: Names each dot in the horizontal bar, which shows a numeral rather than a word.

members.name: completed
members.description:
Said with a finished step in the horizontal bar, so the tick is not the only sign of
it. Optional for existing complete translations; the stepper's default fills in.

members.name: current
members.description: Said with the step the reader is on in the horizontal bar. Optional, as above.

StringRepeater.description: An ordered list of plain strings — alternate names, allowed domains, recipients.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this list's own copy — the add control and each row's remove.

props.name: sortable
props.description: Adds the drag handle and arrow-key reordering.

SubmitStateButton.description:
A submit button that says what it is doing. The label stays visible beside the spinner
(unlike Button's `loading`). While submitting it is `aria-disabled`, keeping focus while
blocking a second submission; "Saved" carries a check.

props.name: state
props.description:
Drives the label and the disabled state. The label is the message, so a spinner never
replaces the answer.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Semantic colour intent. Resolves through the provider when omitted, so `UIProvider`
defaults can change it.

props.name: buttonStyle
props.description: Fill treatment, independent of `tone`. `UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description: Square button sized to its height. The label becomes the accessible name.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretches the button to its container's width.

props.name: render
props.description:
The element this button becomes — an anchor, a router link, a label. `children` stay
the content and keep the button's label wrapper, so a link still sizes like a button.
`render` is how every kit component changes its element, the contract Base UI's parts
already take.

  <Button render={<a href="/settings" />}>Settings</Button>

SuggestionsCombobox.description:
`useSuggestions` behind the kit's combobox: the same engine as `ResourceCombobox` in the
hook's words — `fetchData(query, { signal })`, `itemKey`, `itemText`,
`query`/`onQueryChange` — and with its defaults: one character before a request, and no
preload.

props.name: id
props.description: Applied to the search input, so a `FormField` label can address it.

props.name: itemKey
props.description: Stable identity for an item.

props.name: itemText
props.description: The item's label: what its row and the chosen value show.

props.name: clearInputOnClose
props.description: Resets the query when the list closes. A query that failed is kept, for the retry.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name, for native form submission.

props.name: portalContainer
props.description: Mounts the popup inside this element instead of the default portal root.

props.name: highlightMatch
props.description: Emphasises the matched substring. Ignored when `renderItem` is set.

props.name: fetchData
props.description:
Fetches the suggestions for a query, as an array or a promise of one. Pass
`context.signal` to the request: it aborts when a newer query starts.

props.name: minQueryLength
props.description:
Characters required before a request is issued, not counting surrounding whitespace.
Defaults to 1.

props.name: debounceMs
props.description: The quiet period that collapses a burst of typing into one request. Defaults to 300.

props.name: requestDelay
props.description:
A further wait before the fetcher runs, after the loading state is showing (unlike
`debounceMs`, which delays deciding to fetch). For rate-limited endpoints.

props.name: preload
props.description: Fetches the empty query, so there is something before typing. Not debounced.

props.name: value
props.description: `null` is an explicit empty selection; `undefined` means uncontrolled.

props.name: onError
props.description: Aborts never reach this.

SuggestionsStrings.description: The copy `SuggestionsCombobox` speaks, mapped onto `AsyncComboboxStrings` inside it.

members.name: startTypingMessage
members.description: Shown before anything has been typed.

members.name: formatTypeMore
members.description:
Shown when something but not enough has been typed (`minQueryLength` above one). Takes
the characters still missing. Optional; when absent a supplied `startTypingMessage` is used.

members.name: note
members.description: A middle column — "3 items", "20%" — so counts and rates align down a stack.

members.name: amount
members.description: Already formatted, including its currency.

members.name: deduction
members.description: Money off the customer's total.

SummaryPanel.description:
The money ledger — the shape almost every commerce surface is made of: a tinted block of
label/amount rows, a rule, and one row that matters more than the rest. A cart, a tax
breakdown, an invoice and a subscription all draw it, and each rebuilding it inline is how
one of them ends up emphasising its total differently from the others.

props.name: children
props.description: A quieter ground than the card it sits in, so the rows read as a sub-total block.

Switch.description:
An immediate on/off; a checkbox means "include when I submit". The same hidden native
checkbox as `Checkbox`, announced as a switch. `checked` and `defaultChecked` are its
controlled and uncontrolled state, and `onChange` receives the native change event: read
`event.target.checked` for the next state.

props.name: label
props.description: Rendered beside the track and wired to it.

SwitchCard.description:
The top-of-list feature switch: a bordered card with an icon, a title, an optional
description and hint, and a trailing switch; the whole card toggles. A `ToggleField`
preset with `surface="card"`, a switch, and an off value that still submits: `"0"`.

props.name: label
props.description: Card title, and the switch's accessible name.

props.name: description
props.description: The row's supporting sentence.

props.name: hint
props.description: Quieter, short guidance under the description.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading glyph, drawn in a medallion. Most at home on `surface="card"`.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled state.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial state, uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the next state.

props.name: invalid
props.description: The error surface. The message stays on the `FormField`.

SyncRangeForm.description:
The body of a "reconcile the last N hours" dialog. It renders no buttons: the overlay's
footer submits it through `formId`, so native validation runs first.

props.name: formId
props.description:
Set on the `<form>` so the overlay's footer, outside it, can submit it. That is why this
takes an id rather than rendering its own buttons.

props.name: options
props.description: The windows offered.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled.

props.name: transformSubmit
props.description:
Maps the form's values to the consumer's payload. Replaces the numeric default, which
THROWS rather than coercing — `Number("since-last-run")` is NaN, and an API asked to
reconcile NaN hours does something unpredictable.

props.name: resetKey
props.description: Changing it resets an uncontrolled form, e.g. after a mutation or for a new record.

props.name: errors
props.description: Server-side messages by field. An array is reduced to its first entry.

members.name: hoursRequired
members.description: Shown when no window is chosen and the form is submitted.

members.name: hours
members.description: The chosen window's id. Numeric strings work with the default transform.

members.name: options
members.description: Every ticked option, in the order the group reports them.

Tab.description: One tab. Only the selected tab is in the tab sequence; the arrows move between the rest.

props.name: value
props.description: Names the tab: the value `Tabs` selects, and the one its `TabPanel` shares.

TabList.description:
The row of tabs. It scrolls rather than wrapping, because a second row of tabs reads as a
second level of navigation, which it is not.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Structural presentation: a rule with an indicator, a tinted rail, or filled chips with
no rule. `pill` is for a row that picks what one list shows rather than switching
panels — saved views, result types — and is what OverflowTabBar draws.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the tab set.

props.name: edgeFade
props.description:
Fades only the edges that have hidden tabs beyond them. Updates while scrolling and
follows the writing direction, so it works in RTL.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Accessible names for the previous and next scroll controls that appear when the tabs
overflow.

TabPanel.description: The content for one tab, rendered while that tab is selected.

props.name: value
props.description: Which tab the panel belongs to: that tab's `value`.

TabbedResourceShell.description: A show screen with a tab row in its toolbar.

props.name: tabs
props.description: The tab row. It goes into the toolbar slot, so `slots.toolbar` still wins outright.

props.name: activeTab
props.description: Controlled active tab.

props.name: children
props.description: The screen's own content. Replaced while loading, failed, or empty.

props.name: title
props.description:
Generated header title. With `description` and `actions` it feeds the generated header;
omit them and pass `slots.header` when the header is not a title and a description.

props.name: description
props.description: Generated header description.

props.name: actions
props.description: Generated header actions.

props.name: toolbar
props.description: Between the header and the body.

props.name: empty
props.description:
Replaces the body with the empty state. A boolean rather than an inference from
`children`: a screen with a header row and no data still has children, and only the screen
knows "no records" from "no records MATCHING".

props.name: loading
props.description: Replaces the body with the loading state.

props.name: error
props.description:
Anything truthy replaces the body. An `Error`, string or number becomes the generated error
state's description; any other node is rendered as the error state itself.

props.name: onRetry
props.description:
Wiring this puts a retry control on the generated error state. Without it there is nothing
to offer.

props.name: slots
props.description:
`header`, `toolbar`, `aside`, `footer`, `loading`, `empty`, `error`. Every one has a
generated default; the slot is for the screen where configuring that default prop by prop
is worse than replacing it.

Table.description:
The table, inside its own scroll container. The container becomes a tab stop only while it
scrolls, so a wide table can be scrolled from the keyboard.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class for the scroll container rather than the `<table>` itself.

props.name: stickyHeader
props.description: Pins the header while the body scrolls. Only meaningful when the container is bounded.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this table's own copy — the scroll region's name and `TableEmpty`'s message.

TableAction.description:
A row action: the kit's `ContextAction`, bound to the row. `onClick`, `visible` and
`disabled` receive the row; everything else is an `ActionDefinition` field.

members.name: href
members.description: Carried as data; the table never navigates. Route with your own router in `onClick`.

members.name: onClick
members.description: Receives the subject the set was resolved against.

members.name: visible
members.description: `false`, or a predicate returning false, omits the action for that subject.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Worked out per subject, so a locked row shows the action greyed rather than missing.

members.name: placement
members.description:
Forces this entry to one side when the set is split between buttons and a menu:
`inline` stays a button whatever `max` is, `menu` always overflows, and `auto` fills
the buttons in order up to `max`.

members.name: id
members.description: Stable key. Falls back to a string `label`, then the index.

members.name: type
members.description: `checkbox` renders a toggle driven by `checked` / `onCheckedChange`.

members.name: description
members.description: Second line under the label.

members.name: shortcut
members.description: Trailing content — a keyboard shortcut, rendered in the shortcut treatment.

members.name: trailing
members.description: Trailing content beside the shortcut — a badge, a count.

members.name: group
members.description:
Starts a new group, ruling off above this entry. A string also captions it; `true`
rules off without a heading (e.g. to set apart a sign-out or delete).

members.name: tone
members.description: Semantic intent. `destructive` also moves the entry last and separates it.

members.name: buttonStyle
members.description: Treatment when the action renders as a button. `link` is a ghost that underlines.

members.name: closeOnSelect
members.description: Overrides the menu's `closeOnSelect` for this entry.

members.name: render
members.description: Replaces the rendered entry — a framework `<Link>`, for instance.

TableCaption.description:
Names the table for assistive technology, and the scroll container with it. Rendered
below the table.

TableCell.description: A cell. A plain string is wrapped in `Text`; a node is left exactly as passed.

props.name: align
props.description: Column alignment. Numeric columns belong at the end.

props.name: wrap
props.description:
Lets the cell wrap. Cells are nowrap by default so columns stay aligned — a column that
holds prose opts out here rather than the whole table losing its alignment.

TableEmpty.description:
The "no rows" row: it spans every column and states that there are none. A table with a
header and no body reads as broken; this is what says it is empty on purpose.

props.name: colSpan
props.description: How many columns the table has, so the message spans all of them.

props.name: children
props.description: The message. Defaults to the table's `strings.empty`.

TableHead.description: A column's head cell, and with `sortable` its sort control.

props.name: align
props.description: Column alignment. Numeric columns belong at the end.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Lets the head cell wrap. Cells are nowrap by default so columns stay aligned.

props.name: sortable
props.description:
Renders the label as a sort control and puts `aria-sort` on the `<th>`. Pair with
`sortDirection` and `onSort`.

props.name: sortDirection
props.description: This column's current direction, or `null` when another column is the sort.

props.name: onSort
props.description: Fires on activation. The table does not sort — the caller owns the data.

TableRow.description:
A row: a plain `<tr>`. Mark a selected row with `data-state="selected"` — a data
attribute, not a prop, because rows are plain elements.

TableSkeleton.description:
A table's geometry before the data lands: the real row and head heights, a wide first
column, a right-aligned last one.

props.name: rows
props.description: Body rows, at the real row height.

props.name: columns
props.description: Match the real table, or the placeholder reflows when the data lands.

props.name: showHeader
props.description: A head row above the body, at the real head height.

props.name: framed
props.description:
Draws the table's own edge and corner, as DataView does. Off when it stands in for a
table inside a card that already draws one.

props.name: label
props.description: Announced while loading, in place of the shapes.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides the default announcement. `label` still wins for one instance.

members.name: scrollRegion
members.description:
Names the scroll container while the table overflows it. Unset, it takes the table's
`aria-label` or caption; with none, it is a focusable scroller with no role.

members.name: empty
members.description: `TableEmpty`'s message when it is given no children.

Tabs.description: The root: holds which tab is selected, for the list and the panels inside it.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled selection: the `value` of the selected tab. Pair with `onValueChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The tab selected first, when uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the `value` of the tab the reader selects.

TagsFilterEditor.description: The editor for a `tags` filter. It stages the tags and commits them on Apply.

props.name: triggerSource
props.description: Only a toolbar-opened editor has a list to go back to.

props.name: value
props.description: The chips, controlled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the next list of tags.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Applies the invalid treatment. The message stays with FormField.

props.name: maxTags
props.description: Cap on the number of tags. Entry is refused once it is reached.

props.name: showCount
props.description: Shows a "3 / 5" summary under the field. Requires `maxTags`.

props.name: showClearAll
props.description: Shows a clear-all control under the field.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this field's own copy — clear-all, and each tag's remove, named after the tag
it removes.

props.name: allowDuplicates
props.description: Lets the same string appear twice.

props.name: caseSensitive
props.description: Duplicate detection is case-insensitive unless this is set.

props.name: sortTags
props.description: Keeps the list sorted as tags are added.

props.name: minLength
props.description: The shortest tag accepted.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: The longest tag accepted.

props.name: validate
props.description:
Rejects a tag when this returns false. Runs after the length checks — the field refuses
the tag rather than accepting a bad one and reporting it later.

props.name: delimiter
props.description:
Splits pasted and typed input into several tags — which is what a column copied out of
a spreadsheet looks like. Defaults to a comma or a newline.

props.name: addOnBlur
props.description: Commits whatever is typed when the field loses focus.

props.name: renderTag
props.type: (tag: string, index: number, remove: (index: number) => void) => ReactNode
props.description: Replaces the chip, for a tag that carries an avatar or a colour.

props.name: id
props.description: Goes on the text input, not the wrapper, so a `FormField` label names it.

members.name: clearAll
members.description: The control that empties the field.

members.name: removeTag
members.description: Names each tag's remove control, by the tag it removes.

members.name: placeholder
members.description: The empty field's prompt. The `placeholder` prop overrides it for one instance.

members.name: notAdded
members.description:
Announced when a commit leaves entries it could not add (duplicate, refused, full).
Optional so older complete strings objects still type-check.

members.name: clear
members.description: Accessible name for the inline clear action.

members.name: characterCount
members.description: Accessible description of the character counter, e.g. "12 of 80 characters".

props.name: content
props.description: Text as a plain string. Equivalent to passing it as `children`.

props.name: type
props.description:
Semantic role, which selects the colour token. `main` for primary copy, `secondary`
for supporting copy (descriptions, captions, metadata). `inherit` selects none and takes
the parent's, for text inside a surface that already sets its own — a solid tab, a
tooltip, a coloured chip. Without it those places would drop Text and hand-roll a span,
which is how a kit ends up with two ways to set type.

props.name: size
align
props.description: Horizontal alignment.

props.name: lineHeight
props.description:
Leading, on the shared tier. Unset, each size step carries the leading paired with it
(`--text-<step>--line-height`); a value here overrides that. `tight` and `none` suit
dense rows and single-line values; `relaxed` suits prose.

props.name: numeric
props.description: Tabular figures, so digits align in a column. Use for any value in a table.

props.name: truncate
props.description:
Ellipsises the text at one line rather than wrapping. Makes the element a block with
`min-width: 0`, for the same reason `align` does; every flex box between it and the
constrained width also needs `min-width: 0` (`Stack` and `Grid` set it; a hand-rolled
flex div does not). `Heading` and every `primitives` value take it too.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight.

props.name: children
props.description: Text content. Takes precedence over `content`.

props.name: tag
props.description:
Element to render: `span` inline, `p` for prose, `div` when it wraps blocks, `label`
for a form label. For headings use `Heading`.

TextButton.description:
A button that reads as a link, for actions on this page: announced as a button and
activated by Space. Anything that navigates should be a real anchor. It carries its own
`data-slot`, so nothing downstream mistakes it for a ghost button that should line up
with controls — it is inline prose.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a spinner and blocks interaction. The label keeps its space so the button does
not resize mid-action.

props.name: render
props.description:
The element this button becomes — an anchor, a router link, a label. `children` stay
the content and keep the button's label wrapper, so a link still sizes like a button.
`render` is how every kit component changes its element, the contract Base UI's parts
already take.

  <Button render={<a href="/settings" />}>Settings</Button>

props.name: tone
props.description:
Semantic colour intent. A text button always sets it, so the provider's button defaults
do not reach it.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides the character-count and clear copy.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Character cap, also the denominator of the count.

props.name: showCharacterCount
props.description: Shows the current and maximum character count.

props.name: clearable
props.description:
Shows a clear control in the trailing lane once the field has a value. `strings.clear`
is its accessible name.

props.name: onClear
props.description: Called after the clear control empties the field.

props.name: loading
props.description: Replaces the trailing affordance with a loading indicator.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Applies the invalid styling, the same as Input. Validation copy stays with FormField.

props.name: rows
props.description:
Visible lines. Without `minRows` it is the floor the field grows from; `maxRows` sets
where it stops growing and scrolls.

props.name: minRows
props.description: The floor when the field grows with its content: its smallest height, in rows.

props.name: maxRows
props.description:
Height at which the field stops growing and starts scrolling. Without a ceiling a long
note pushes the submit button off the screen.

ThemeConfig.description: Theme overrides. Token names are generated from the stylesheet, so a typo is a type error.

members.name: radius
members.description: The container radius — cards, dialogs, popovers, menus. Writes `--radius`.

members.name: radiusSm
members.description:
The inner radius — controls, rows, chips, badges, tooltips. Writes `--radius-sm`.
Not derived from `radius`: set both.

members.name: colors
members.description: Semantic colour overrides. Prefer these to `palette`.

members.name: palette
members.description: Primitive ramp overrides: moves every semantic resolving through the step.

members.name: vars
members.description: Escape hatch for custom properties the kit does not define. Keys omit `--`.

ThemeDefinition.description: Serializable, and the only state ThemeScope and ThemeTweaker share.

members.name: mode
members.description: Which bucket the mode-scoped edits go to, and which the preview shows.

members.name: shared
members.description: Typography, density, structure, radius: everything both themes share.

ThemeScope.description:
Applies a theme to an intentionally isolated subtree: one DOM node carrying the theme's
variables and its mode. An app-wide theme belongs on the shared root instead, through
useAppliedTheme.

props.name: mode
props.description: Overrides the stored mode without changing the definition.

members.name: shared
members.description: Receives the mode-independent variables.

members.name: light
members.description: Explicit light: a `.light` or `data-theme="light"` element and the boundaries inside it.

members.name: dark
members.description: Explicit dark: a `.dark` or `data-theme="dark"` element and the boundaries inside it.

members.name: systemLight
members.description: Light by OS preference (no explicit theme), emitted under `prefers-color-scheme: light`.

members.name: systemDark
members.description: Dark by OS preference (no explicit theme), emitted under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`.

ThemeTweaker.description:
Edits the kit's public theme contract live and exports the result. Controlled through
`value` / `onValueChange` for the theme and `config` / `onConfigChange` for the provider
settings. Set `apply={false}` when the application owns theme application; `preview={false}`
edits the actual app without a sample preview.

props.name: fields
props.description: The catalog of editable variables. Defaults to the kit's whole public surface.

props.name: target
props.description:
`self` themes only the editor and its preview; `document` themes the whole app while
mounted, so portaled menus and dialogs inherit the edit too.

props.name: apply
props.description:
Writes the edited theme onto the target. Set `false` when the application owns theme
application, as with useAppliedTheme at its root.

props.name: manageModeClass
props.description: Manages `.light` / `.dark` on a non-self target. Off when a theme manager owns it.

props.name: preview
props.description:
The sample the edit is shown on. `false` hides it, so the editor edits the actual app
without a sample preview; a node replaces the built-in one.

props.name: showIntro
props.description: Off when an owning drawer supplies the title.

props.name: onExport
props.description: Replaces the browser download with the consumer's own persistence.

props.name: onError
props.description: Receives clipboard, export, and serialization failures.

members.name: control
members.description: Without one the field is a raw CSS text box, which every variable falls back to.

ThemeTweakerRangeControl.description: A slider and a numeric box, for a variable with real bounds.

members.name: unit
members.description: Appended to committed values. Omit for a unitless token.

members.name: fallback
members.description: Shown while the variable is unset — a factor that falls back to another reads as empty.

members.name: mixedScope
members.description: For a section whose fields do not all share one scope.

members.name: inheritValue
members.description: The placeholder in a field with no override — what it falls through to.

Time.description:
The same value as a time of day. Three components rather than a granularity prop, because
a column shows one of them and never switches.

props.name: value
props.description:
The moment to show: whatever the API returned — a Date, an ISO string or an epoch
number. Parsed once, here.

props.name: pattern
props.description:
A date-fns pattern, when the default is not what this column needs. `DatePrimitive`
falls back to the scope's `dates.format`, `Time` to its `dates.timeFormat`, and
`DateTime` to the two joined.

props.name: id
props.description:
Applied to the hours segment, the one a `FormField` label addresses; each segment keeps
its own part name.

props.name: value
props.description: The time: `{ hours, minutes }`, not a `Date`, because a time of day has no date.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the new time.

props.name: withSeconds
props.description:
Adds a third segment, for seconds. Most times of day do not have one, and an empty
seconds box invites a value nobody wanted.

props.name: minuteStep
props.description: The minute increment: minutes snap to it. 15 gives a quarter-hour picker.

props.name: invalid
props.description: The error surface. The message stays on the `FormField`.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this picker's own copy — the group and the three segments.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The field's caption. `FormField` supplies it; each segment is then named "{caption} {part}".

members.name: label
members.description: Names the group of segments. The three boxes are one value.

members.name: hours
members.description: Each segment. They are unlabelled boxes, so this is the only name they have.

TimeValue.description: A time of day: `{ hours, minutes }`, not a `Date`, because a time of day has no date.

Timeline.description: An ordered run of events on one rail — changelogs, milestones, an order's progress.

props.name: items
props.description:
The entries, in the order they should be read. Rendered as an `<ol>`, because these
have an order and a screen reader should say so.

TimelineItem.description: One entry of a `Timeline`. Everything an entry needs travels in the item.

members.name: id
members.description: Stable identity for the row.

members.name: title
members.description: What happened.

members.name: description
members.description: Supporting copy under the title.

members.name: timestamp
members.description: Already formatted — the kit's date primitives decide the format, not this component.

members.name: trailing
members.description:
The title row's trailing lane when what belongs there is not a time — an amount, a
count. It replaces `timestamp` rather than joining it: there is one lane.

members.name: icon
members.description: Decorative glyph inside the dot.

members.name: status
members.description:
Colours the dot, and the connector that runs from it to the next entry. `progress` and
`completed` are not the same thing: a step you walked past is a position, so it takes
the same primary tone as the step you are on and a sequence reads as one journey in one
colour; `completed` is an outcome, a milestone that landed. A bare `progress` dot is
hollow where `current` is solid, because on a rail with no glyphs the card still has to
say where the thing is.

members.name: children
members.description: Anything the entry carries below its description — a card, a diff, an action row.

ToastAction.description: A button on a toast's pill.

members.name: label
members.description: The button's text.

members.name: onClick
members.description: Runs on press, before the toast is dismissed.

ToastOptions.description: What a toast carries beyond its title, passed as `toast(title, options)`.

members.name: id
members.description: Reusing an on-screen id updates that toast in place rather than stacking a second one.

members.name: description
members.description: A second line under the title.

members.name: icon
members.description: Replaces the status glyph.

members.name: duration
members.description:
Lifetime in milliseconds before auto-dismissal. `Infinity` pins it open. Falls back to
the Toaster's `duration`.

members.name: action
members.description:
A button on the pill — the undo for something that already happened. It dismisses the
toast after running.

members.name: cancel
members.description: A second, quieter button on the pill. Dismisses the toast after running.

members.name: onDismiss
members.description: Called after the toast leaves, whichever way it left.

ToastStore.description: One queue of toasts, its timers, and the `toast()` bound to it.

members.name: toast
members.description: Raise a toast on this store. `toast` is the ergonomic form of the same thing.

members.name: pauseAll
members.description: Pause every running timer — pointer-enter and focus-within.

members.name: applyDefaultDuration
members.description: Give the Toaster's configured default to anything queued without one.

Toaster.description:
Mount once, near the application root. The store lives at module scope so `toast()` works
from anywhere; this component is only the view.

props.name: position
props.description:
One of six: top or bottom, crossed with start, center, or end. Bottom stacks grow
upward so the newest is nearest the edge. `UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: duration
props.description:
Default lifetime in ms. A toast with its own `duration` still wins. `UIProvider`
defaults can change it.

props.name: visibleToasts
props.description:
Maximum toasts on screen — a cap on the render, not the store: older ones are dropped
from the render, and a capped toast still runs its timer and `onDismiss`. `UIProvider`
defaults can change it.

props.name: closeButton
props.description: Shows each toast's dismiss control. `UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this region's own copy — its name, and each toast's dismiss.

props.name: store
props.description:
The queue this Toaster renders, dismisses and pauses. Defaults to the singleton
`toast()` writes to; pass a `createToastStore()` instance to isolate it — a host app and
an embedded widget.

props.name: container
props.description:
Where the toast region renders. Defaults to the nearest `UIPortalHost`, else
`document.body` — so toasts raised inside a scoped region are drawn with that region's
density and theme.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the live region the toasts are announced from.

members.name: dismiss
members.description: Names each toast's dismiss control, which is icon-only.

Toggle.description:
A control that stays engaged, reported with `aria-pressed`: `pressed` and
`defaultPressed` hold its state, controlled and uncontrolled, and `onPressedChange` fires
with the next one. Inside a `ToggleGroup`, `value` names the toggle, and the group reads it
into its own value; outside a group it is unused.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Sunk when engaged, or outlined. Match whatever sits beside it in the row — `outline`
for a lone control, `ghost` inside a group.

props.name: pressed
props.description:
Whether the toggle button is currently pressed.
This is the controlled counterpart of `defaultPressed`.

props.name: defaultPressed
props.description:
Whether the toggle button is currently pressed.
This is the uncontrolled counterpart of `pressed`.

props.name: onPressedChange
props.description: Callback fired when the pressed state is changed.

props.name: value
props.description:
A unique string that identifies the toggle when used
inside a toggle group.

ToggleField.description:
A clickable label-and-control row for a switch or a checkbox: a plain settings row, or with
`surface="card"` a bordered card with an optional icon and hint. The whole row is the
target.

props.name: label
props.description: The row's label.

props.name: description
props.description: The row's supporting sentence.

props.name: hint
props.description: Quieter, short guidance under the description.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading glyph, drawn in a medallion. Most at home on `surface="card"`.

props.name: kind
props.description:
Which control renders: a checkbox for a preference that is saved with the form, a switch
for state that applies immediately.

props.name: surface
props.description:
`row` is a plain settings row; `card` is a bordered card that takes the checked
colour — the form `SwitchCard` presets.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled state.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial state, uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the next state.

props.name: invalid
props.description: The error surface. The message stays on the `FormField`.

props.name: uncheckedValue
props.description:
What the field submits when off. Unset, an unchecked control submits nothing (the
platform rule). Set, a hidden input always submits `"1"` when on and this when off.
`SwitchCard` sets `"0"`.

props.name: controlPosition
props.description: Puts the control on the leading edge instead of the trailing one.

ToggleGroup.description:
A set of `Toggle`s (each given a `value`) sharing one value. `multiple` allows several at
once rather than one: a view switch is one, text styles are several. The value is always
an array, even when only one may be pressed, so switching `multiple` does not change its
shape.

props.name: attached
props.description:
Joins the toggles into one framed control with internal rules. Off leaves them as
separate buttons in a row.

props.name: value
props.description:
The pressed state of the toggle group represented by an array of
