the values of all pressed toggle buttons.
This is the controlled counterpart of `defaultValue`.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Callback fired when the pressed states of the toggle group changes.

props.name: multiple
props.description:
When `false` only one item in the group can be pressed. If any item in
the group becomes pressed, the others will become unpressed.
When `true` multiple items can be pressed.

Toolbar.description:
A named set of related controls: `role="toolbar"`, with one roving tab stop and
orientation-aware arrow navigation. `orientation`, `disabled` and `loopFocus` come from
Base UI's toolbar root. Supply `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` whenever no visible label
names the set.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The orientation of the toolbar.

props.name: loopFocus
props.description: If `true`, using keyboard navigation will wrap focus to the other end of the toolbar once the end is reached.

ToolbarButton.description:
A toolbar item rendered through the kit Button: Base UI owns the navigation behaviour, the
Button its look. It takes `tone`, `buttonStyle`, `iconOnly`, `loading` and `render`.

props.name: render
props.description: Replaces the kit Button while retaining toolbar navigation behavior.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Semantic colour intent. Resolves through the provider when omitted, so `UIProvider`
defaults can change it.

props.name: buttonStyle
props.description: Fill treatment, independent of `tone`. `UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description: Square button sized to its height. The label becomes the accessible name.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretches the button to its container's width.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a spinner and blocks interaction. The label keeps its space so the button does
not resize mid-action.

ToolbarButtonConfig.description: The shape the toolbar renders. Built-ins and consumer items resolve to this.

ToolbarGroup.description: Groups related items, and can disable the group as one unit.

props.name: disabled
props.description: When `true` all toolbar items in the group are disabled.

ToolbarInput.description: A native input item that joins the same roving-focus order.

ToolbarLink.description: An anchor item that joins the same roving-focus order.

ToolbarSeparator.description: A rule between items. It takes the orientation opposite to the toolbar's.

TooltipButton.description:
A button with a tooltip. For an icon-only button the tooltip text is also the accessible
name, so it is not unnamed to anyone not using a mouse.

props.name: tone
props.description:
Semantic colour intent. Resolves through the provider when omitted, so `UIProvider`
defaults can change it.

props.name: buttonStyle
props.description: Fill treatment, independent of `tone`. `UIProvider` defaults can change it.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description: Square button sized to its height. The label becomes the accessible name.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretches the button to its container's width.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a spinner and blocks interaction. The label keeps its space so the button does
not resize mid-action.

props.name: render
props.description:
The element this button becomes — an anchor, a router link, a label. `children` stay
the content and keep the button's label wrapper, so a link still sizes like a button.
`render` is how every kit component changes its element, the contract Base UI's parts
already take.

  <Button render={<a href="/settings" />}>Settings</Button>

props.name: tooltip
props.description:
Shown on hover and focus. It is also the accessible name when the button has no text
of its own, and that pairing is the point: an icon button with a tooltip and no
`aria-label` is unnamed to everyone not using a mouse. Beside a visible label it is the
description.

props.name: side
props.description: Where the tooltip opens.

TooltipContent.description: The tip. Short — a sentence, not a paragraph.

props.name: container
props.description: Where the popup renders. Defaults to the nearest `UIPortalHost`, else the primitive's own.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description:
Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the distance to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

props.name: align
props.description: How to align the popup relative to the specified side.

props.name: alignOffset
props.description:
Additional offset along the alignment axis in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the offset to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

props.name: side
props.description:
Which side of the anchor element to align the popup against.
May automatically change to avoid collisions.

TooltipProvider.description:
Shares one open delay, `delay`, across every tooltip inside it. Wrap the app once rather
than each tooltip.

props.name: delayDuration
props.description: `delay` under another name, in milliseconds. It wins when both are given.

props.name: delay
props.description: How long to wait before opening the tooltip on hover. Specified in milliseconds.

TooltipTrigger.description:
What the tip anchors to, passed as `render`. It must be a real focusable element, so the
tip opens on keyboard focus and not only on hover.

props.name: render
props.description:
Allows you to replace the component's HTML element
with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

TopbarSidebarLayout.description:
The header-first admin shell. The header spans the full width and owns the brand, the
search and the account; the sidebar and the content share the height below it. The only
difference from SidebarInsetLayout is where the LOGO lives — and that decides the whole
frame, which is why it is two components rather than a boolean.

props.name: sidebarSide
props.description: Which side the rail sits on. Match the Sidebar's own `side` to it.

props.name: mobileSidebarMode
props.description:
`drawer` hides the sidebar column below md and uses the Sidebar's mobile sheet, which
the trigger opens. `inline` stacks static navigation above the content; pair it with
`collapsible="none"` and `sidebarTrigger={false}`.

props.name: headerHeight
props.description: Any CSS length. Falls back to the shell's own token.

props.name: sidebarTrigger
props.description: Shorthands for the matching `slots` entry, for a shell with only a few regions.

props.name: sidebar
props.description:
The rail: a Sidebar or AppSidebar with `icon` or `offcanvas` collapse, which becomes
the mobile drawer. Omit it for a full-width body.

props.name: contentRender
props.description:
Replaces the content column's element (`<main>` by default). Pass
`contentRender={<div />}` when embedded in a page that owns the main landmark.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: The sidebar's initial uncontrolled open state.

props.name: contained
props.description:
Fits a parent with a definite height instead of owning the viewport. Either way the
sidebar and content scroll below the header.

props.name: sidebarProviderProps
props.description:
Passes `open`/`onOpenChange`, `persist`, `keyboardShortcut` and `strings` to the
shell's provider: controlled state, persistence, shortcuts and translated sidebar
controls. Disable persistence and shortcuts in independent embedded examples.

members.name: header
members.description: Replaces the header's whole inner row.

members.name: sidebarTrigger
members.description: Before the logo — the sidebar trigger, usually.

members.name: headerStart
members.description: After the logo.

members.name: headerCenter
members.description: The middle, usually search. Hidden below md, where there is no room for it.

members.name: headerActions
members.description: Before the trailing cluster.

members.name: headerEnd
members.description: The trailing cluster — notifications, account.

members.name: content
members.description: Replaces `children`.

members.name: amount
members.description: The magnitude, already formatted. The sign comes from the kind.

members.name: processedAt
members.description: Already formatted.

members.name: method
members.description: How it was taken — "Visa ending 4417", "PayPal".

members.name: reference
members.description: The gateway's own id. Mono: it is compared and copied, not read.

TwoColumnLayout.description:
Main and aside in a stable DOM order: the aside is always second, so keyboard and
screen-reader users meet the primary content first. Visual order is the grid's.

props.name: header
props.description: Spans both columns, before the work regions.

props.name: main
props.description: The primary work region: detail, form, or index content.

props.name: aside
props.description: The secondary work region: summary, support, or action rail. Always second in the DOM.

props.name: footer
props.description: Spans both columns, after the work regions.

props.name: stickyAside
props.description:
Keeps the aside in view while the page scrolls. Opt-in: an aside taller than the
viewport must be able to scroll away.

props.name: asidePosition
props.description:
Which side the aside is drawn on. Default `end`. Only the grid columns move; the
aside stays second in the DOM.

TwoColumnPageSkeleton.description: A detail page: a title over the record's panel, and beside it its owner and facts.

props.name: label
props.description: Announced while loading, in place of the shapes.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides the default announcement. `label` still wins for one instance.

TypographyConfig.description: `UIConfig`'s `typography` slice: the type factor, the default size, fonts and sizes.

members.name: scale
members.description:
Type-only override (`--text-scale`): multiplies every `--text-*` role, control labels
included, without changing geometry. Unset, type follows `scale`.

members.name: defaultTextSize
members.description:
Size components fall back to when they set none. 14px, not 16px: `base` is a deliberate
step up for a dense surface.

members.name: fonts
members.description: Font stack overrides.

members.name: sizes
members.description: Per-step size overrides, keyed without the `--text-` prefix.

UIConfig.description:
The configuration `UIProvider`, `UIRoot` and `UIScope` take. A scope names only what it
changes; everything else inherits from the scope around it.

members.name: colorScheme
members.description: Colour scheme. `system` follows `prefers-color-scheme`.

members.name: theme
members.description: Radius, colour, palette and custom-property overrides.

members.name: density
members.description:
Named spacing and control-geometry preset: `compact`, `default` and `comfortable` scale
by 0.941176 (32px actions), 1 and 1.075. Readable typography is unchanged.

members.name: scale
members.description:
Master factor (`--scale`). Geometry, spacing, icons and the type ramp follow it by
default; use `density` or `typography.scale` to move only one of them.

members.name: typography
members.description: The type factor, the default text size, font stacks and per-step sizes.

members.name: motion
members.description: Duration overrides, and motion forced off.

members.name: overlay
members.description: The modal scrim's blur, and whether menus render dark.

members.name: forms
members.description: Form-control behaviour: the iPhone zoom guard.

members.name: formatting
members.description: The locale every formatter uses.

members.name: money
members.description: The store's currency policy: the default and display currencies, and how a pair shows.

members.name: dates
members.description: The week start, date patterns, the date-fns locale and relative-time wording.

members.name: defaults
members.description: Per-component prop defaults, keyed by family and merged over each component's own.

UIConfigContext.description:
The context itself. Exported for a consumer building a provider of their own; the hooks
are the supported way in.

UIConfigSettings.description:
The provider settings editor — the non-CSS half of a theme, which ThemeTweaker includes under
Provider. Connect its controlled `config` to your root UIProvider to update mounted
consumers.

members.name: boundaryDescription
members.description: Says why these settings behave differently from the CSS ones.

members.name: summary
members.type: { locale: string; currency: string; density: string; textSize: string; }

members.name: sections
members.type: { regional: { title: string; description: string; }; presentation: { title: string; description: string; }; money: { title: string; description: string; }; }

members.name: options
members.description: Display names for enum values, keyed by the value itself.

UINestedContext.description:
Whether a root or scope is above this point. `UIProvider` uses it to decide between
owning the document (outermost) and scoping its own subtree (nested), which is how nested
providers avoid fighting over the document.

UIPortalHost.description:
Keeps popups inside this subtree, so they inherit the scope's custom properties and
`[data-density]` / `[data-theme]` attributes instead of the root's. It renders one
`display: contents` element as the portal target — a box would become a flex or grid item
in whatever laid the scope out. Pass `container` to use an element the application
already manages, such as a shadow root or its own overlay layer.

  <UIScope config={{ density: "compact", colorScheme: "dark" }}>
    <UIPortalHost>
      <DropdownMenu>…</DropdownMenu>
    </UIPortalHost>
  </UIScope>

Opt-in per region; without a host, popups portal to the document as usual. A popup's own
`container` prop — DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, Select, Tooltip, HoverCard, Popover,
NavigationMenu and Toaster each accept one — wins over the scoped host. With no host and
no prop, each primitive keeps its own default.

props.name: container
props.description: Portal into this element (a shadow root, an app-managed layer) instead of one the host renders.

UIRoot.description:
`<UIRoot>` — the application's configuration, once. Renders no element; region scoping
is `UIScope`, which does.

It restores, never removes: it captures what each attribute was before it mounted and
puts it back on unmount. Deleting them instead would take an app's own theme with it
whenever a provider unmounted inside that app.

One owner, handed on: two independent React roots — a host app and an embedded widget —
both think they are the top. Each asks for the document and the OLDEST root still mounted
owns it; the rest leave it alone. When the owner unmounts the document goes to the next
root in line rather than reverting, so a widget still on the page is still honoured.
`body` and `documentElement` are tracked separately, and a final unmount restores what
was there before the first root arrived — not what the previous owner wrote.

component that reaches for the document unasked fights the next React root, the next
test, and any app already managing its own `data-theme`.

— Base UI's contract, the same one Item and Stack use — e.g. `<UIScope render={<aside />}>`,

from both.

props.name: render
props.description:
An element to render instead of the span, taking the hidden styles — e.g. a real
`<button>` that a Base UI trigger requires.

WeightInput.description:
A weight: the number and its unit in separate channels, as `CurrencyInput` keeps the
currency — "1.5 kg" in one string is ambiguous to parse.

props.name: id
props.description:
Applied to the first numeric input, which a `FormField` label addresses; each input
keeps its own `aria-label` for its part.

props.name: strings
props.description:
Overrides this field's own copy — the unit selector's name. Like every other piece of
copy, each string can be overridden on its own.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled amount: the number, as a plain string.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The starting amount, for an uncontrolled field.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with a change event shaped like a native one, carrying the amount.

props.name: unit
props.description: Controlled unit, apart from the number. Switching unit does not convert — it relabels.

props.name: defaultUnit
props.description: The unit the field starts in.

props.name: onUnitChange
props.description: Called with the new unit. Switching relabels rather than converting — the number is the caller's.

props.name: units
props.description: Which units the selector offers.

props.name: decimalPlaces
props.description: Digits after the separator.

props.name: min
props.description: The lower bound.

props.name: max
props.description: The upper bound.

props.name: step
props.description: The increment for the − / + controls.

props.name: showUnitSelector
props.description: Shows the unit selector. Turn it off for a field with one fixed unit.

props.name: disableUnitSelector
props.description: Shows the unit selector read-only, for a value whose unit is decided elsewhere.

props.name: invalid
props.description: The error surface. The message stays on the `FormField`.

WorkspaceLayout.description:
The frame a single RECORD is edited in. Not an app shell — it sits inside one: a record
with many sections needs its own navigation, and nesting a second shell is how a page ends
up with two sidebars.

props.name: sidebar
props.description: The section navigation — usually a `<WorkspaceNav />`.

props.name: rail
props.description: A second, wider column of context beside the content.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the region, for a page holding more than one.

props.name: contentRender
props.description:
Replaces the element the content region is drawn as (`<main>` by default). Pass
`contentRender={<div />}` when embedded in a page that owns the main landmark.

members.name: external
members.description: Defaults to true — a workspace link usually leaves this application.

members.name: status
members.description: A chip beside the label — "Draft", "Published".

WorkspaceLocaleStrip.description:
The languages a record exists in, and how complete each is. A strip rather than a
select, because the completeness is the reason to switch and a select hides it behind a
press.

props.name: actions
props.description: Controls at the strip's trailing edge — "Add language".

WorkspaceNav.description:
Navigation for a record filled in over time. The difference from every other nav in the
kit is COMPLETION: each section reports how much of it is done, because that is what
decides where the reader goes next.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Runs on enabled link/button activation. Rows with neither a URL nor onSelect stay static.

props.name: renderLink
props.description: Renders links through the application's router; without it, plain anchors.

members.name: completion
members.description: 0–100. Drives the bar, and the status when none is set.

members.name: status
members.description: Overrides the derived status.

members.name: warning
members.description: Shorthand for `status="attention"`.

members.name: href
members.description: Renders a navigation link through renderLink. Without a URL, onSelect uses a button.

members.name: label
members.description: Names the region.

members.name: current
members.description: Announced beside the current entry, which is otherwise only tinted.

props.name: title
props.description: What the record IS. Gives way before the badges do.

props.name: description
props.description: One line under the title.

props.name: media
props.description: An avatar, an icon medallion, a thumbnail.

props.name: badges
props.description: Status marks beside the title. Short — the title is what gives way, not these.

props.name: status
props.description: A single prominent status, rendered after the badges.

props.name: metadata
props.description:
Key/value pairs, drawn as an inline MetadataList: each label and its value are one item,
read as one fact, with a middle dot between items.

props.name: strings
props.description: Overrides this header's own copy — the names of its two unlabelled regions.

props.name: actions
props.description: Primary actions, pinned to the end of the title row.

props.name: secondaryActions
props.description: A second, quieter row beneath — filters, tabs, bulk controls.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The heading element, for the document outline.

members.name: metadata
members.description: Names the metadata list, which is a definition list with no visible caption.

members.name: actions
members.description: Names the actions region.

applyRounding.description:
The rounding `DecimalInput` applies, exported so a caller can match it: `value` to
`decimals` places under a `RoundingMode`.
applyRounding.signature: (value: number, decimals: number, mode: RoundingMode) => number

base/action-menu#ActionDefinition.description: One command, in the shape `ActionMenu`, `ActionButtons` and a card's `actions` all take.

members.name: id
members.description: Stable key. Falls back to a string `label`, then the index.

members.name: label
members.description:
What the entry says. The only part of the row that gives way: a long label truncates
instead of pushing the shortcut or trailing content off.

members.name: type
members.description: `checkbox` renders a toggle driven by `checked` / `onCheckedChange`.

members.name: href
members.description:
Renders the entry as a link. A native `<a href>` by default, which is a full page
navigation — pass `renderLink` to route it through the app's router instead.

members.name: description
members.description: Second line under the label.

members.name: shortcut
members.description: Trailing content — a keyboard shortcut, rendered in the shortcut treatment.

members.name: trailing
members.description: Trailing content beside the shortcut — a badge, a count.

members.name: group
members.description:
Starts a new group, ruling off above this entry. A string also captions it; `true`
rules off without a heading (e.g. to set apart a sign-out or delete).

members.name: tone
members.description: Semantic intent. `destructive` also moves the entry last and separates it.

members.name: buttonStyle
members.description: Treatment when the action renders as a button. `link` is a ghost that underlines.

members.name: visible
members.description: `false` omits the action entirely.

members.name: closeOnSelect
members.description: Overrides the menu's `closeOnSelect` for this entry.

members.name: render
members.description: Replaces the rendered entry — a framework `<Link>`, for instance.

members.name: amount
members.description: The amount, as typed. Never parsed here.

members.name: currency
members.description: ISO 4217 code.

Serialises a mention into the span that goes into a body. The trailing ` ` gives
the caret somewhere to land after the chip.

calculateSeoScore.description:
Plain function, no React. Returns the total, a status, and a per-check breakdown with the
measured lengths.

clearAsyncPreviewCache.description: Clears one key, or everything. Call it after a mutation invalidates a record.

Binds the generics once, for a record shape used in more than one place, instead of restating
them at every part.

createFilterCache.description:
The async option and label cache, with its own lifetime. FilterProvider makes one per
mount, which is the isolating default: two roots on a page, or two users in a session, never
see each other's results. Create one and pass it as FilterProvider's `cache` when results
and pill labels should survive a navigation. A Map at module scope would be one cache for
the whole realm — an embedded widget would be served the host application's options, and
signing in as somebody else would keep the first user's labels.

One cache for the whole session, so filters survive navigation:

  const cache = useMemo(() => createFilterCache(), [])
  <FilterProvider cache={cache} …>

createToastStore.description:
An independent queue with its own timers and its own bound `toast()`, for a second,
isolated Toaster — a host application and an embedded widget. With only the module-level
queue, one for the whole realm, two Toasters on a page would render the same toasts, and
`pauseAll` would walk a timer map neither owned. The singleton stays the default, because
`toast("Saved")` working with no wiring is the point of it.

`defineAction` for a destructive action: its tone defaults to `"destructive"`, and its
modality to a destructive `"alert"`.

features/actions#ActionDefinition.description:
One action, defined once and read from every surface: what it is called, where it appears, how
it asks, and what it runs.

members.name: modality
members.description:
How the action asks. The outlet renders it; no surface needs its own dialog. `"none"`, or no
modality, runs the action at once.

members.name: request
members.description: A declarative request, run by `requestRunner` — for apps whose actions are mostly HTTP.

members.name: parseErrors
members.description: Turns a failure into field errors, so a form modality can show them inline.

members.name: tone
members.description: Semantic colour intent. Colour is always `tone`, never `variant`.

members.name: buttonStyle
members.description: Button treatment, independent of the colour.

members.type: (values?: TValues, payload?: TPayload, metadata?: ActionMetadata) => Promise<TResult | undefined>

formatAddressLines.description:
The same ordering outside React: the address as lines, each already joined. Empty fields
drop out, and a line left with nothing drops with them, so a missing `line2` never leaves
a blank row.
formatAddressLines.signature: (parts: AddressParts, { countryCode, order, separator, locale }?: FormatAddressOptions) => string[]

formatDateRange.description:
The same collapsing outside React: a range reduced to its distinct parts. The same day
renders once, and a range within one month drops the repeated month from the start date.
formatDateRange.signature: (start: DateInput, end: DateInput, { pattern, separator, locale }?: FormatDateRangeOptions) => string | undefined

formatDecimal.description:
The formatting `DecimalInput` applies as the reader types, exported so a caller can match
it. Accepts a comma as the decimal separator — most of the world types one.
formatDecimal.signature: (value: string, decimalPlaces: number, allowNegative: boolean) => string

formatDimensions.signature: (width: DimensionPart, height: DimensionPart, { depth, unit, separator, locale, options }?: FormatDimensionsOptions) => string | undefined

formatFileSize.signature: (value: number, { from, base, locale }?: FileSizeFormatOptions) => string

formatInitials.description:
The same derivation outside React: short, Unicode-aware initials from a person or
resource name.

`first-last` is the identity default (`Mary Jane Smith` → `MS`). Use
`first-words` for admin surfaces that intentionally use the first
two words (`Mary Jane Smith` → `MJ`). Single-word `first-last` values use
the first N letters (`OpenAI` → `OP`).
formatInitials.signature: (value: string | null | undefined, options?: InitialsFormatOptions) => string

formatName.description: The same normalisation outside React — for a sort key, an export, a document title.

paginationRange.description:
The page numbers a pager renders, with `null` marking a gap: the arithmetic on its own,
for a custom control. Always includes the first and last page.
paginationRange.signature: (page: number, total: number, siblings?: number) => (number | null)[]

parseDateInput.description:
The single parse every date primitive goes through. Returns undefined rather than an
Invalid Date, so the empty state renders instead.

parseFiltersFromQuery.description:
A plain query record → the active filters, for whichever router you have. Driven by the
CONFIGS, not the query: an undeclared key is somebody else's parameter.
parseFiltersFromQuery.signature: (filterConfigs: readonly FilterConfig[], query: FilterQueryInput, options?: FilterQueryOptions) => ActiveFilter[]

parseMentionsFromHtml.description:
Reads the mentions back out of a body — the other direction from `buildMentionHtml` — e.g. so
a composer's list shrinks when a chip is deleted. First occurrence wins. Returns id, kind and
label only; merge against the mentions you already know to keep `href` and `data`, which
HTML cannot express.

members.name: amount
members.description:
The amount, in a channel separate from its currency. A number or a decimal string: a
single dot is decimal, and a grouped US or EU string is parsed by POSITION — whichever
of , or . appears last is the decimal point — so a value that came back through a
European locale does not parse a thousand times too large.

members.name: currency
members.description: The amount's ISO currency code, kept apart from the amount all the way to the render.

members.name: unit
members.description: The unit the amount ARRIVES in. Use `minor` for APIs that store integer minor units.

members.name: minorUnitScale
members.description: Minor units per major unit, for a currency whose exponent is not two.

members.name: formatMode
members.description:
How this amount is written. Falls back to the scope's `money.formatMode`, so
`UIProvider` defaults can change it.

rhfFormControl.description:
Wraps a react-hook-form `control` in the kit's headless contract. `useField` delegates to
`useController`, so registration, validation and dirty tracking keep working. Imported
from `themelia-ui/forms-rhf`, never from `themelia-ui/forms`, which stays dependency-free.

serializeFiltersToQuery.description:
The active filters → a plain query record, laid over `currentQuery`, for whichever router
you have. Driven by the CONFIGS, not the query: an undeclared key is somebody else's
parameter, and is left alone. The operator travels in a companion key
(`status=confirmed&status__op=not`), written only when it differs from the type's default.
serializeFiltersToQuery.signature: (filterConfigs: readonly FilterConfig[], activeFilters: readonly ActiveFilter[], currentQuery?: FilterQueryInput, options?: FilterQueryOptions) => FilterQueryRecord

toast.description:
Raises a toast on the default store and returns its id. Also `.success`, `.info`,
`.warning`, `.error`, `.loading`, `.promise` and `.dismiss`.

useAction.description:
One action by id, when a surface is not the right shape. `null` when none is registered in
scope or it is not visible.
useAction.signature: <TPayload = unknown, TValues = unknown, TResult = unknown>(actionId: string, options?: UseActionOptions<TPayload>) => ResolvedAction<TPayload, TValues, TResult> | null

useActionScope.description: The nearest `ActionScope`'s id, or the global scope. For a surface resolving its own actions.

useActionSnapshot.description:
Subscribes to the whole store. Prefer a narrower hook — this re-renders on any registry or
run change.

useActionStore.description:
The store itself, for logic the hooks do not cover. Throws outside an `ActionProvider` rather
than returning null.

useActionSurface.description: The actions for one surface, already filtered by visibility, permission, and guards.
useActionSurface.signature: <TPayload = unknown, TValues = unknown, TResult = unknown>(options: ActionSurfaceOptions<TPayload>) => ResolvedAction<TPayload, TValues, TResult>[]

useActiveAction.description:
Whichever action is currently open, or `null`. The outlet reads this; a bespoke outlet would
too.
useActiveAction.signature: <TPayload = unknown, TValues = unknown, TResult = unknown>() => ResolvedAction<TPayload, TValues, TResult> | null

useActivityResources.description:
Resolves the resources an event refers to, from a registry keyed like `order:1234`, so a feed
can render a chip per subject without every consumer re-implementing the lookup and its
cache. Every mutation emits the whole registry through `onResourcesChange` for persistence.

useAiChatScroll.description:
The stick-to-bottom behaviour without the layout, for a consumer building their own
transcript: new content scrolls it only while the reader is at the bottom. Returns the
`containerRef` for the scroll viewport, the `endRef` sentinel for the end of the content,
`isAtBottom`, and `scrollToBottom`.

useAppliedTheme.description:
Writes an edited theme onto a live element and removes it on cleanup. Keep it mounted with
`target: "document"` and `apply: true` to apply document-wide values; set
`manageModeClass: false` when UIProvider owns the colour scheme.
useAppliedTheme.signature: ({ apply, manageModeClass, selfRef, target, theme }: UseAppliedThemeOptions) => void

members.name: apply
members.description: Writes the theme while `true`; `false` removes what it wrote.

members.name: manageModeClass
members.description: Manages `.light` / `.dark` on the target. `false` when UIProvider owns the colour scheme.

members.name: selfRef
members.description: The editor's own element, which a `self` target means.

members.name: target
members.description:
Where the theme goes: `document` for document-wide values, an element, or a function
returning one; `null` applies nothing. A `self` target is left to ThemeScope's inline style.

useAsyncOptions.description:
The fetch, debounce and cache behind AsyncFilterEditor, for a caller supplying their own
editor against the same lifecycle. Results are cached by filter and query for `staleTime`,
each keystroke aborts the previous request, and only the newest response may land.
useAsyncOptions.signature: (filter: FilterConfig, search: string, isActive: boolean, options?: { onError?: FilterErrorHandler; }) => UseAsyncOptionsResult

useAsyncPreview.description:
Fetching tied to a popover's open state. Closing aborts the request, only the newest request
may write state, and a module cache keyed by `cacheKey` spares a repeat within `staleTime`.
useAsyncPreview.signature: <TData, TContext = unknown, TType extends string = string>(options: UseAsyncPreviewOptions<TData, TContext, TType>) => UseAsyncPreviewReturn<TData, TContext, TType>

useAsyncPreviewContext.description:
The current state and data, for a part rendered outside the provided ones — a footer that
counts results, a header that names what is loading.
useAsyncPreviewContext.signature: <TData, TContext = unknown, TType extends string = string>() => AsyncPreviewState<TData, TContext, TType>

useAttachmentUpload.description:
The files staged on a draft and their uploads — the part with three things that are easy to
get wrong: cancelling in flight, retrying one of several, and discarding a draft that still
has uploads running.

useCarousel.description:
The track's position, its slide count, and the scroll helpers, for a fully custom control
surface. Must be called inside a `Carousel`.
useCarousel.signature: () => { index: number; count: number; atStart: boolean; atEnd: boolean; scrollToSlide: (index: number) => void; strings: CarouselStrings; }

useComboboxCore.description:
The list state every picker shares: the threshold, the selection merged ahead of the
results, the groups, the create row and the pager. The pickers differ only in what
selected means, the field, and where the results come from.
useComboboxCore.signature: <T>({ items, searchValue, getItemLabel, getItemKey, loading, showListContent, minSearchLength, strings, renderItem, onSearch, debounceMs, creatable, onCreate, getItemGroup, hasMore, onLoadMore, loadingMore, highlightMatch, ensuredItems }: UseComboboxCoreOptions<T>) => UseComboboxCoreReturn<T>

useComboboxFilter.description:
Locale-aware matchers from Base UI — `contains`, `startsWith` and the rest — for a caller
filtering a list themselves who still wants the popup's rules about what counts as a match.

useComments.description:
The state machine on its own — `composerMode`, `submit`, `deleteComment`, `resetKey` — for a
fully custom thread. The mode is one union rather than three booleans, so “editing a reply
while replying” cannot be represented.
useComments.signature: <TUser extends CommentUser = CommentUser, TMeta = unknown, TResource extends string = string>(options?: UseCommentsOptions<TUser, TMeta, TResource>) => UseCommentsReturn<TUser, TMeta, TResource>

useCopyToClipboard.description:
Copy a value, confirm it, and reset — the hook `Copyable` is built on, and the shared
implementation for every copy surface. `copy(value)` resolves `true` or `false` rather than
rejecting. Takes `confirmMs`, `onCopy`, `onError`, and `write` — a destination for where
`navigator.clipboard` is absent.
useCopyToClipboard.signature: ({ confirmMs, write, onCopy, onError }?: UseCopyToClipboardOptions) => UseCopyToClipboardResult

useDataTableScrollState.description:
Whether the table is scrolled away from either edge, and the nudges that move it — what the
toolbar's scroll arrows react to. For a consumer building their own toolbar: reimplementing the
overflow booleans and the nudges means two answers to “can this scroll right”.
useDataTableScrollState.signature: (tableAreaRef: RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null>, options?: { stepPx?: number; deps?: readonly unknown[]; }) => UseDataTableScrollStateResult

useDataTableSize.description: The table's `size` — its row density — for a part rendered inside a row.

useDataView.description:
The rows after filtering, plus `failed` and the `error` for a custom surface. If a matcher
throws, the unfiltered rows come back with `failed` set and `onError` called, rather than a
misleading empty list; DataView shows a warning for this fallback, which `strings.filterError`
customizes.
useDataView.signature: <TData extends object>({ data, filtering }: UseDataViewOptions<TData>) => UseDataViewResult<TData>

useDatesConfig.description:
Date and time presentation defaults, read by the date primitives and pickers: week start,
the fallback pattern, the date-fns locale, and the relative-time hook.

members.name: weekStartsOn
members.description: First day of the week in calendars and pickers. 0 = Sunday.

members.name: format
members.description: date-fns pattern the date primitives fall back to.

members.name: timeFormat
members.description: date-fns pattern for a time of day. `"p"` uses the locale's own convention.

members.name: locale
members.description:
The date-fns Locale OBJECT — what actually translates month and weekday names, and the
built-in relative-time wording. It cannot be derived from a BCP-47 tag such as
`formatting.locale`: the locales are modules, and importing all of them to look one up
would put every language in every bundle, so the consumer imports the one it needs.

members.name: formatRelativeTime
members.description: Replaces the relative-time wording ("7 days ago", "in 2 hours").

useDefaults.description:
Per-component prop defaults for one family. The component passes its OWN defaults and
the scope's overrides merge over them, which keeps the values beside the component, makes
the call order-independent, and lets an unused module tree-shake away.
useDefaults.signature: <K extends keyof ComponentDefaults>(family: K, fallback: ComponentDefaults[K]) => ComponentDefaults[K]

useDensity.description:
The resolved density, with the scale factor beside it. The visual effect comes from the
`data-density` attribute; this is for logic that must branch on it.

useEventCalendar.description:
The date, the view, and the days — for a calendar whose surface is entirely yours. Each is
independently controllable: the prop wins when given, and setters always call the consumer's
handler.
useEventCalendar.signature: ({ events, date, defaultDate, viewMode, defaultViewMode, onDateChange, onViewModeChange, dataOptions }: UseEventCalendarOptions) => UseEventCalendarResult

parameters.name: { events, date, defaultDate, viewMode, defaultViewMode, onDateChange, onViewModeChange, dataOptions }

useFieldValue.description:
Value bookkeeping shared by Input and Textarea (SearchInput wraps Input): the controlled or
uncontrolled value, a generated id, and the character count with its limit — one branch,
so both fields behave the same under a form library.
useFieldValue.signature: ({ controlledValue, defaultValue, maxLength, showCharacterCount, providedId, idPrefix }: UseFieldValueOptions) => UseFieldValueResult

parameters.name: { controlledValue, defaultValue, maxLength, showCharacterCount, providedId, idPrefix }

useFileDropTarget.description:
The drop behaviour on its own, for a custom target. Its drag state survives descendants:
`dragleave` fires on entering a child, so enters and leaves are counted and dragging
clears only at zero.
useFileDropTarget.signature: ({ disabled, onFiles }: { disabled?: boolean; onFiles: (files: File[]) => void; }) => { isDragging: boolean; dropTargetProps: { onDragEnter: DragEventHandler<HTMLElement>; onDragOver: DragEventHandler<HTMLElement>; onDragLeave: DragEventHandler<HTMLElement>; onDrop: DragEventHandler<HTMLElement>; }; }

returns.type: { isDragging: boolean; dropTargetProps: { onDragEnter: DragEventHandler<HTMLElement>; onDragOver: DragEventHandler<HTMLElement>; onDragLeave: DragEventHandler<HTMLElement>; onDrop: DragEventHandler<HTMLElement>; }; }

members.name: dropTargetProps
members.type: { onDragEnter: DragEventHandler<HTMLElement>; onDragOver: DragEventHandler<HTMLElement>; onDragLeave: DragEventHandler<HTMLElement>; onDrop: DragEventHandler<HTMLElement>; }

useFilterCache.description:
The filter cache in scope, or `null` outside a provider (then `useAsyncOptions` makes its own
short-lived one). For a caller writing their own editor that wants to read or seed the same
store `useAsyncOptions` uses.

useFilterGroups.description:
Partitions the filter list into the four groups a bar draws differently — search, always,
active, and behind the add button — for a consumer laying out their own bar. Exported so
that consumer does not have to re-derive “which filters belong behind the add button”: a
rule that is easy to get subtly wrong and impossible to notice when you do.

useFormFieldBinding.description:
Binds one field: turns a control and a field name into the exact props a kit control
takes — value, onValueChange, onBlur, invalid, error, disabled. The only API a component
needs to be form-library agnostic.
useFormFieldBinding.signature: <TValue, TValues = Record<string, unknown>>({ name, control, disabled }: { name: Extract<keyof TValues, string> | string; control: FormControl<TValues>; disabled?: boolean; }) => FieldBinding<TValue>

parameters.name: { name, control, disabled }
parameters.type: { name: Extract<keyof TValues, string> | string; control: FormControl<TValues>; disabled?: boolean; }

useFormatting.description:
The scope's locale, shared by the primitives' number formatting. Money and dates read it
through their own hooks as well.

members.name: locale
members.description: BCP-47 tag used by every Intl formatter in the kit.

useFullscreenTableModality.description:
The modality full screen has to take so the page behind it stops being reachable: while
`active`, Escape calls `onExit`, Tab cycles inside `regionRef`, the page stops scrolling, and
focus returns to the opener afterwards.
useFullscreenTableModality.signature: (active: boolean, regionRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>, onExit: () => void) => void

useGlobalSearch.description:
The palette's active row, active tab and key handling — `grouped`, `tabCounts`, `activeTab`,
`flat`, `activeIndex` and `onKeyDown` — for a palette whose markup is entirely yours. `flat`
is both what the rows render and what the keys walk, so the highlight and Enter always agree.
useGlobalSearch.signature: <TGroup extends string = string>({ results, query, onResultSelect, onClose }: UseGlobalSearchOptions<TGroup>) => UseGlobalSearchResult<TGroup>

useKanban.description:
The move without the drag: `findItem` and `move` over the same `value`, `onValueChange` and
`getItemValue` the board takes — for a keyboard board, a "move to column" menu, or a test
that moves items without simulating a pointer.
useKanban.signature: <T>({ value, onValueChange, getItemValue, onItemMove }: UseKanbanOptions<T>) => UseKanbanResult<T>

useKanbanContext.description: The board's state, for a custom card or column rendered inside it.

useKanbanItemContext.description: One card's drag state, for a custom card that still needs to know it is being dragged.

useLeaflet.description:
Leaflet itself, with its draw and fullscreen plugins, once it has loaded — and `null` until
then, so callers must check. For a consumer reaching for the imperative API. Everything here
is lazy: Leaflet and its plugins are ~200KB, they touch `window` at import time, and most pages
that ship this kit never render a map. Inside a Map, react-leaflet's hooks reach the controls
through a provider that has already resolved the module, so a control calls `useMap` normally
instead of managing its own load state.
useLeaflet.signature: () => { L: typeof LeafletNamespace | null; LeafletDraw: typeof LeafletDrawNamespace | null; }

returns.type: { L: typeof LeafletNamespace | null; LeafletDraw: typeof LeafletDrawNamespace | null; }

useLocalAction.description:
One action registered for the lifetime of the component that declares it, for a definition no
other surface needs.
useLocalAction.signature: <TPayload = unknown, TValues = unknown, TResult = unknown>(definition: ActionDefinition<TPayload, TValues, TResult>, options?: UseLocalActionOptions<TPayload>) => ResolvedAction<TPayload, TValues, TResult> | null

useMediaLibrary.description:
The whole state without the chrome. Its stable `refetch()` retries the current query without
clearing filters or selection; `fetchError` identifies fetch failures separately from
mutation errors.
useMediaLibrary.signature: <TItem = MediaLibraryItem>({ items: itemsProp, fetcher, accessors: accessorsProp, selectionMode, value, defaultValue, onValueChange, onItemUpdate, applyItemPatch, onItemDelete, onUpload, onError, tab: tabProp, defaultTab, onTabChange, view: viewProp, defaultView, onViewChange, query: queryProp, defaultQuery, onQueryChange, type: typeProp, defaultType, onTypeChange, collection: collectionProp, defaultCollection, onCollectionChange, sort: sortProp, defaultSort, onSortChange, uploadOptions: uploadOptionsProp, defaultUploadOptions, onUploadOptionsChange }: UseMediaLibraryOptions<TItem>) => ResolvedMediaLibraryState<TItem>

parameters.name: { items: itemsProp, fetcher, accessors: accessorsProp, selectionMode, value, defaultValue, onValueChange, onItemUpdate, applyItemPatch, onItemDelete, onUpload, onError, tab: tabProp, defaultTab, onTabChange, view: viewProp, defaultView, onViewChange, query: queryProp, defaultQuery, onQueryChange, type: typeProp, defaultType, onTypeChange, collection: collectionProp, defaultCollection, onCollectionChange, sort: sortProp, defaultSort, onSortChange, uploadOptions: uploadOptionsProp, defaultUploadOptions, onUploadOptionsChange }

members.name: items
members.description: Every asset, after local edits and deletions.

members.name: visibleItems
members.description: What the current filters and sort leave.

members.name: selectedSet
members.description: For a per-row lookup that would otherwise be O(n) inside a map.

members.name: selectVisible
members.description: Select/deselect only the currently visible records, preserving other selections.

members.name: error
members.description: Most recent fetch or mutation failure; cleared when an operation starts.

members.name: fetchError
members.description: Always supplied by useMediaLibrary; optional for existing consumer-owned states.

members.name: refetch
members.description: Stable query reload, always supplied by useMediaLibrary; a no-op in local mode.

useMentions.description:
The search state plus trigger detection from the text before the caret. Any editor
implementing `MentionEditorHandle` plugs in; the kit's rich-text editor does.

useMentionsSearch.description:
The picker's suggestion state. Every kind is searched rather than only the active tab, so the
tab counts are true the moment the panel opens, and the panel can jump to the kind that
matched. Lookup per kind: its `search`, then its static `suggestions`, then the global
`onResourceSearch`.

useMoneyConfig.description:
Currency policy — the default code, the display code, how an amount is written and how a
pair is rendered: what Money reads when a prop is absent.

members.name: defaultCurrency
members.description: Used when a `<Money>` is given no currency.

members.name: displayCurrency
members.description: A converted currency shown beside the primary one.

members.name: dualPricingEnabled
members.description: The master switch. Off, a `secondary` passed at a call site still renders.

members.name: displayMode
members.description:
Whether a second currency shows. `dynamic` shows it only when the two codes differ;
`dual` would print a price twice when they match.

members.name: layout
members.description: Where the second value sits: beside the first, or under it.

members.name: formatMode
members.description:
How an amount is written. `with-symbol` is Intl's own placement, which varies by locale
and currency.

useOptionalSidebar.description:
The panel's state, or `null` outside a provider — for the parts a shell renders whether
or not it has a sidebar. A header above a plain page still wants its breadcrumbs, and
throwing there takes the page down over a toggle that has nothing to toggle.

useOverlayActions.description:
The confirm button's behaviour — the pending state, the error routing, and the close on
success — shared by the three overlays, so they agree on what "confirm" means. For a bespoke
surface that still needs that lifecycle.
useOverlayActions.signature: ({ close, open, onConfirm, onAsyncConfirm, closeOnAsyncComplete, confirmTone, loading, formId, onCancel, onError, strings, defaults, emphasis, tone }: UseOverlayActionsOptions) => UseOverlayActionsReturn

parameters.name: { close, open, onConfirm, onAsyncConfirm, closeOnAsyncComplete, confirmTone, loading, formId, onCancel, onError, strings, defaults, emphasis, tone }

useOverlayConfig.description:
Overlay policy — whether dropdown and context menus render dark (by default they do),
and the modal scrim's blur.

members.name: backdropBlur
members.description:
Blur behind a modal's scrim, in px (a number) or any CSS length. Off by default: a
backdrop filter repaints everything behind the surface each frame.

members.name: darkMenus
members.description:
Dropdown and context menus render in the dark scheme whatever the page is. Default
`true`; `false` lets them follow the scheme they are portalled into, like other popups.
A config value, not a CSS switch: Firefox lacks CSS `if()`.

useOverlayVisibility.description:
One overlay's state, controlled or not, so a component that supports both its own trigger
and external openers keeps one source of truth: `open`, `setOpen`, `show`, `hide`, `toggle`,
and `overlayProps`, which spreads straight onto any overlay in the kit.
useOverlayVisibility.signature: ({ defaultOpen, open: controlledOpen, onOpenChange, onOpen, onClose }?: UseOverlayVisibilityOptions) => UseOverlayVisibilityReturn

parameters.name: { defaultOpen, open: controlledOpen, onOpenChange, onOpen, onClose }

useOverlayVisibilityGroup.description:
Several overlays keyed by name from one hook: one handle per overlay when a component drives
several — create, edit, delete. Three separate useState calls is how two of them end up open
at once; `closeOthersOnOpen` is for a set where two open at once is never right.
useOverlayVisibilityGroup.signature: <TKey extends string>(keys: readonly TKey[], { defaultOpen, open: controlledOpen, onOpenChange, closeOthersOnOpen }?: UseOverlayVisibilityGroupOptions<TKey>) => UseOverlayVisibilityGroupReturn<TKey>

usePlaceSearch.description:
The geocoding search behind PlaceAutocomplete, without the field: debounced and abort-safe —
every keystroke cancels the request before it. For a caller building their own field against
the same debounce, abort and result shape.
usePlaceSearch.signature: ({ debounceMs, searchUrl, query, lang, limit, bbox, lat, lon, zoom, locationBiasScale }: UsePlaceSearchOptions) => { results: PlaceFeature[]; isLoading: boolean; error: Error | null; hasSearched: boolean; }

parameters.name: { debounceMs, searchUrl, query, lang, limit, bbox, lat, lon, zoom, locationBiasScale }

returns.type: { results: PlaceFeature[]; isLoading: boolean; error: Error | null; hasSearched: boolean; }

useRegisterActions.description:
Registers `actions` for as long as the calling component is mounted, under `options.scope` or
else the nearest `ActionScope`'s.
useRegisterActions.signature: <TPayload = unknown, TValues = unknown, TResult = unknown>(actions: readonly ActionDefinition<TPayload, TValues, TResult>[], options?: ActionRegistrationOptions) => void

useScale.description:
The resolved `--scale` factor as a number, for a measurement JavaScript has to compute
rather than let CSS derive. Components read tokens, not this — it is for callers.

useSchemaForm.description:
The values, the errors, and `validate()` without any of the rendering. Server `errors` win
over local messages for the same key; local messages clear on the field's next change,
server messages stay until the consumer replaces them.
useSchemaForm.signature: ({ fields, value, defaultValue, errors: externalErrors, onValueChange, onFieldChange, requiredError, validationError, onError }: UseSchemaFormOptions) => UseSchemaFormResult

parameters.name: { fields, value, defaultValue, errors: externalErrors, onValueChange, onFieldChange, requiredError, validationError, onError }

useSharedResourceCard.description:
The state machine without the card: open state, pending choice, `canConfirmSelection`, and a
confirm that awaits.
useSharedResourceCard.signature: <TResource, TSuggestion>({ resource, mapInitialSelected, onConfirmSelection, isConfirmDisabled, onDialogOpen, onDialogClose, onError, open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, value, defaultValue, onValueChange }: UseSharedResourceCardOptions<TResource, TSuggestion>) => UseSharedResourceCardResult<TResource, TSuggestion>

parameters.name: { resource, mapInitialSelected, onConfirmSelection, isConfirmDisabled, onDialogOpen, onDialogClose, onError, open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, value, defaultValue, onValueChange }

useSidebar.description: The panel's state from anywhere inside `SidebarProvider`. Throws outside one.

useStateFormControl.description:
A `FormControl` over plain React state — the zero-dependency default. Also exposes the
current values and a reset, which a library-backed control owns itself.
useStateFormControl.signature: <TValues extends Record<string, unknown>>(initialValues: TValues, options?: { errors?: Partial<Record<keyof TValues, string>>; }) => FormControl<TValues> & { values: TValues; reset: (next?: TValues) => void; }

returns.type: FormControl<TValues> & { values: TValues; reset: (next?: TValues) => void; }

useSuggestions.description:
The request lifecycle the self-fetching pickers run on — query, results, loading, error,
selection and open, each controllable on its own — for a caller putting it behind their
own field, or a surface that is not a combobox at all.

useTypographyConfig.description: Typographic defaults, such as the size components fall back to when they set none.

members.name: scale
members.description:
Type-only override (`--text-scale`): multiplies every `--text-*` role, control labels
included, without changing geometry. Unset, type follows `scale`.

members.name: defaultTextSize
members.description:
Size components fall back to when they set none. 14px, not 16px: `base` is a deliberate
step up for a dense surface.

members.name: fonts
members.description: Font stack overrides.

members.name: sizes
members.description: Per-step size overrides, keyed without the `--text-` prefix.

useUIConfig.description:
The whole resolved configuration at this point in the tree. Prefer a narrower hook, which
says what a component depends on.

useUIPortalContainer.description:
The container a portal in this subtree should use: the caller's `explicit` value, else
the nearest `UIPortalHost`, else `undefined` so the primitive keeps its own default.
`undefined` rather than `document.body` on purpose: the primitive's default is the thing
that knows about shadow roots, SSR and nested portals.

validateFileSelection.description:
The validation FileUpload runs, as a plain call, so a caller can pre-check. Each file gets
its own verdict, so one rejection does not stop the rest.
validateFileSelection.signature: ({ incoming, current, maxFiles, append, ...constraints }: ValidateOptions) => ValidationResult
